front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah name is from Ayat 1.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: The subject matter of the Surah and its style clearly indicate that it is not only Makki but was revealed in the earliest stage of Makkah.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
Its aim is to show how people become morally corrupt when they deny, or ignore, the Hereafter, and to warn people of the DoJ.

To make this clear, the Quran points to the condition of Arabia at the time. The land was filled with chaos. Violence, looting, and tribal raids were common, and people lived in constant fear of attack. Everyone knew this situation was wrong. Those who were robbed suffered, and those who robbed others felt powerful, yet when the same violence turned against them, they too realized how miserable and unjust society had become.

This condition shows that when people are unaware of accountability before Allah SWT in the life after death, they become ungrateful to their Lord. They misuse the strength and abilities Allah SWT has given them to oppress others. Driven by love of wealth, they pursue it by any means, even unjust ones. Their own behavior proves their ingratitude toward Allah SWT.

Had they believed that the dead would be raised, and that their hidden motives would be exposed, they would not have acted this way. On that Day, Allah SWT, the Lord of all people, will be fully aware of what each person has done and will judge them accordingly.

sections.title: 1-11 EXAMPLE OF HORSES WHO ARE MORE GRATEFUL TO THEIR OWNERS THAN MEN TO THEIR RABB

translation.text: By the galloping, panting horses,

commentary.text: Allah SWT swears/takes an oath by the horses وَالۡعٰدِيٰتِ when they are made to gallop into battle in His path (i.e., Jihad), and thus they run and pant/snort, which is the sound that is heard from the horse when it runs. (Heavy breathing).
The surah opens with vivid imagery of charging horses to shame humans who give their energy, risk, and devotion to worldly pursuits but withhold gratitude and obedience from their Lord.
Lesson: What are you running towards? This world or the Hereafter??

translation.text: striking sparks of fire ˹with their hoofs˺,

commentary.text: The striking of their hooves on the rocks, which causes sparks of fire to fly from them.
Strike sparks indicates that the horses run in the dead of night, for the sparks struck by their hoofs become conspicuous only at night.

translation.text: launching raids at dawn,

commentary.text: And scouring to the raid at dawn, meaning, the raid that is carried out in the early morning time.
Lesson: Even a patient who is up all night will fall asleep at the time of dawn. So it is the best time to conduct a raid.

translation.text: stirring up ˹clouds of˺ dust,

commentary.text: As they attack you see dust clouds. Thus, so powerful if the attack that dust is stirred up by it.

translation.text: and penetrating into the heart of enemy lines!

commentary.text: "This means into the midst of the disbelieving enemy." Meaning they go straight into the middle of the enemy. Fearless.

Horses are mentioned because they do this at the command of their master. They are obedient to their master no matter if its launching raids at dawn in a powerful attack that stirs up clouds of dust and running straight into the enemy’s swords. This is how Arabs fought.
So the core issue here is why is the horse making all this effort and taking all this risk??
Human is only master not creator.

translation.text: Surely humankind is ungrateful to their Lord—

commentary.text: This is the conclusion of the oath or the subject of what is being sworn about, and it means that he (man) is ungrateful for the favors of His Lord and he rejects them. Allah SWT is our Master and Creator, yet we are not at all grateful or loyal.

However just look at the horse. Therefore, the oaths sworn in the first five Ayats of this Surah -- sworn by the horses, which run with panting breath and dash off sparks at night, then raising dust in their rush to assault a settlement at dawn and penetrate into the enemy host.
Contrasting human disloyalty with the fierce loyalty of warhorses to their masters.
But humans are ungrateful and thankless to their Master who has given them so much. Their attitude is to take the blessings with no obedience or gratitude. And misuse the blessings.
Therefore, this indeed is sheer ingratitude that the resources granted by Allah and the power given by Him should be used for causing chaos and corruption to spread in the earth, which Allah abhors.

translation.text: and they certainly attest to this—

commentary.text:
Allah SWT is a witness to this. 
It is also possible that the pronoun (He) could be referring to man. Thus, man is a witness himself to the fact that he is ungrateful.

translation.text: and they are truly extreme in their love of ˹worldly˺ gains.

commentary.text: Man has an extreme/severe love of wealth.
Man is intensely and violently in love with money. He will wage wars, cut off relations due to money. Money is often what keeps us from the worship of Allah SWT.

translation.text: Do they not know that when the contents of the graves will be spilled out,

commentary.text: The graves on the DoJ will be scattered around. So, remember the DoJ often.

translation.text: and the secrets of the hearts will be laid bare—

commentary.text: Whatever is in the chest will come out on the DoJ. Every secret will be exposed. Hidden will become apparent.

translation.text: surely their Lord is All-Aware of them on that Day.

commentary.text: Allah SWT knows everything and the reality of man in not hidden.
After these Surahs make dua: Oh Allah make our hiaab/accounting easy. Ameen.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: This Surah is named after its opening word, al-qari‘ah, which not only serves as its title but also reflects its central subject. The Surah is focused on the concept of Resurrection, emphasizing the momentous event that is to come.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: There is consensus that Surah Al Qaria is a Makki Surah. Its content indicates that it is among the earliest revelations received in Makkah.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
The central theme of the Surah is Resurrection and the events of the Hereafter.

The Surah begins by grabbing the listener’s attention with a dramatic proclamation: “The Great Disaster! What is the Great Disaster? And what do you know what the Great Disaster is?” This introduction serves to alert and prepare the audience for the revelation of a terrible, significant event.

The scene of Resurrection is then vividly portrayed, describing people in a state of confusion and panic, likened to scattered moths, while mountains are uprooted and become like fluffed wool. Following this depiction, the Surah explains that on the Day of Judgment, Allah’s Court will be established, and people will be held accountable for their deeds. Those whose good deeds outweigh their bad deeds will be rewarded with happiness and bliss, while those whose good deeds are lighter will be cast into a deep pit filled with blazing fire.

sections.title: 1-11 A SCENE EXPLAINING THE DAY OF JUDGEMENT

translation.text: The Striking Calamity –

commentary.text: The great or striking calamity is one of the names of the DoJ. Qariah literally means striking or banging. Qar is to strike one thing upon another so severely as to produce a noise like when someone loudly bangs on a door. In view of this literal meaning, the word qariah is used for a dreadful disaster and a great calamity.
Lesson: In life when we have to face a calamity and are overwhelmed remember this is nothing compared to the mother of all calamities i.e. DoJ.

translation.text: What is the Striking Calamity?

commentary.text:
What is Al-Qari`ah?  Al-Qari`ah is one of the names of the Day of Judgement, like Al-Haqqah, At-Tammah, As-Sakhkhah, Al-Ghashiyahand other names. 
One that suddenly strikes.

translation.text: And what can make you know what is the Striking Calamity?
On that Day human beings shall be like scattered moths,

commentary.text: Humans will be like scattered moths that collide, crash into things as they rush towards the light. Humans on the DoJ will be confused, lost and bewildered at what is happening to them, they will be like scattered moths.

Also see (54:7)
As if they were locusts spread abroad.

translation.text: And the mountains will be like wool, fluffed up.

commentary.text: This will be the first stage of Resurrection, when the order of the world will be overthrown; the people will then be running about in confusion and bewilderment like so many scattered moths around a light; and the mountains will be flying about like carded wool of different colors. The mountains have been compared to wool of different colors because of the existence of a variety of colors in them.

translation.text: Then as for one whose scales are heavy [with good deeds],

commentary.text: From here begins description of the second stage of Resurrection when after having been resurrected man will appear in the court of God.

If his good deeds are more than his bad deeds. Deeds will have weight. Heavy weights will be for Iman + good deeds (deeds done with the correct intention, that is, to please Allah SWT and done in the way prescribed by the Prophet (PBUH).

translation.text: they will be in a life of bliss.

commentary.text: He will live a pleasant life meaning, in Paradise.

translation.text: But as for one whose scales are light,

commentary.text: But as for him whose Balance will be light meaning, his bad deeds are more than his good deeds. A deed can be large in the world’s eyes and weightless before Allah SWT if it is driven by ego, denial, or hypocrisy. Conversely, a small act done with true faith and sincerity can carry immense weight.

“Divine justice” means the scale is calibrated by truth, not perception. Not reputation. Not self-confidence. Not social applause. The Balance measures reality as Allah SWT defines it. So, the statement means: On the Day of Judgment, what saves a person is not how impressive they looked or how hard they tried, but whether their faith and deeds had genuine value in the sight of Allah SWT.

translation.text: their home will be the abyss.

commentary.text: Their home will be hell. They will fall into hell’s embrace.
Such a person will be falling and tumbling headfirst into the fire of Hell, and the expression `his mother' has been used to refer to his brain (as it is the mother of his head).
هَاو desire literally means to fall. To pursue one’s desires leads to failure. The only place that will take him is Hell.

translation.text: And what will make you realize what that is?

commentary.text: And what will make you know what it is.

translation.text: ˹It is˺ a scorching Fire.

commentary.text: A fire Hamiyah! meaning, extreme heat. It is a heat that is accompanied by a strong flame and fire.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: This Surah derives its name from a word found in the very first Ayat, which is at takathur.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: Surah At-Takathur is a Makki.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
The Surah warns people about the negative consequences of worshipping worldly things. It highlights how individuals dedicate their lives to accumulating material wealth, benefits, pleasures, status, and power, often until death, competing with each other and boasting about their achievements.

This relentless pursuit occupies them so thoroughly that they cannot focus on more meaningful aspects of life. After warning about the harmful outcomes of such behavior, the Surah points out that these blessings are not simply gifts but also tests. Each of these comforts will be accounted for in the Hereafter.

sections.title: 1-8 MAN'S CAUSE OF DESTRUCTION IS MUTUAL RIVALRY OF WORLDLY GAINS, AND REAL SUCCESS IS IN WORKING FOR THE LIFE HEREAFTER

translation.text: Competition for more ˹gains˺ diverts you ˹from Allah˺,

commentary.text: The competition to increase keeps man busy and distracted from Allah SWT’s worship.

Alhakum at-takathur broadly refers to people’s obsession with accumulating wealth and power, making them neglectful of more important matters like God, morality, and others’ rights. This pursuit of greater comfort and status leads many to disregard ethical boundaries and humanity, fueling competition, tyranny, and widespread harm. Ultimately, takathur describes a fixation that blinds individuals and societies to anything beyond worldly gain and pleasure.
Lesson: Allah SWT is describing man’s nature. Our main concern should not be wanting more. The more we run after this world the more it will stop us from the Hereafter.

translation.text: until you end up in ˹your˺ graves.

commentary.text: This pursuit does not end until we die.

Ibn Kathir explains that Surah At-Takāthur warns us that the obsession with accumulating wealth, status, and worldly possessions distracts people from preparing for the Hereafter. This heedlessness continues until death comes and they “visit the graves.”

The Prophet (PBUH) clarified that the only wealth that truly benefits a person is what they consumed, wore, or gave in charity for the sake of Allah SWT; everything else is left behind. At death, family and wealth return, but a person’s deeds remain with them, showing that only righteous actions have lasting value.
Lesson: Only the dust of the grave finishes our appetite for more!

translation.text: But no! You will soon come to know.

commentary.text: This is not why we were created.

Many mistakenly believe that material wealth and surpassing others equals success. The truth of this error will become clear, in the Hereafter or at the time of death, only then will it be evident if one’s pursuits brought real fortune or failure.

translation.text: Again, no! You will soon come to know.

commentary.text:
Again nay! you shall come to know!
Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, "This is a threat after a threat."

translation.text: Indeed, if you were to know ˹your fate˺ with certainty, ˹you would have acted differently˺.

commentary.text: If only you knew with certainty this knowledge عِلۡمَ الۡيَقِيۡنِؕas to how meaningless the striving and distractions are for you then you would never pursue them. Meaning, `if you knew with true knowledge, you would not be diverted by rivalry for wealth away from seeking the abode of the Hereafter until you reach the graves.'

translation.text: ˹But˺ you will surely see the Hellfire.

commentary.text: You will see the fire of Hell.

translation.text: Again, you will surely see it with the eye of certainty.

commentary.text:
This is the explanation of the previous threat, which was in Allah's saying, Nay! you shall come to know! Again nay! you shall come to know!

Thus, Allah SWT threatens of a Fire, which if it exhaled one breath, every angel who is near (to Allah) and every Prophet who was sent would all fall down on their knees due to fear, awe and the sight of its horrors. Both believers and non-believers will see Hell.

translation.text: Then, on that Day, you will definitely be questioned about ˹your worldly˺ pleasures.

commentary.text: On the Day of Judgment people will be questioned about the blessings Allah SWT granted them such as health, safety, food, and comfort, and whether they showed gratitude by obeying and worshipping Him.

The Prophet (PBUH) illustrated this when he told Abu Bakr and Umar that even the simple meal they ate after hunger was a blessing they would be asked about. The hadith also teaches that many people fail to appreciate two great favors in particular: health and free time.
The Ayat therefore reminds believers that every blessing carries responsibility and that gratitude to Allah SWT must be shown through faith, worship, and righteous actions.
Dua: Oh Allah give me the ability to show gratitude for every blessing.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah takes its name from the word occurring in the first Ayat al-`asr.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: it is Makki; its subject matter also testifies that it must have been sent down in the earliest stage at Makkah, when the message of Islam was being presented in brief but highly impressive sentences so that the listeners who heard them once could not forget them even if they wanted to, for they were automatically committed to memory.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
Significance and Impact of Surah Al-Asr

Surah Al-Asr stands out as a unique example of being the most comprehensive in size but the an ocean of meaning and depth. Its content so profound that even an entire book would not suffice to capture its full message. Imam Shafi said that if only this only surah was revealed in the Quran it would be enough guidance for mankind. If only man would reflect and do tadabur on this Surah.

The Surah clearly outlines the path to genuine success for humanity, as well as the route to failure and destruction. Imam Shafe emphasized its importance, stating that if people were to reflect deeply upon this Surah, it would alone be sufficient for their guidance.

sections.title: 1-3 FORMULA FOR THE WAY TO SALVATION

translation.text: By the ˹passage of˺ time!

commentary.text: Allah SWT is taking an oath by time. Time will not stop. وَالۡعَصۡرِۙ   means to press or squeeze often used in the context of extracting juice here it metaphorically refers to the concept of time slipping away it suggest urgency like time that is slipping away. It also refers to the Asr or late afternoon prayer. It is a reminder that another day is coming. Sunset after sunset.
Time is precious so value it. Allah SWT draws our attention to the fleeting nature of time and the critical need for awareness of how we spend it.

translation.text: Surely humanity is in ˹grave˺ loss,

commentary.text: Thus, Allah swears by Al-Asr that mankind/humanity is in loss and destruction. Every second we are losing.
خُسۡرٍ from Kasara or loss.
We are given time so how are we using it?

arabic_lines: اِلَّا الَّذِيۡنَ اٰمَنُوۡا وَعَمِلُوا الصّٰلِحٰتِ وَتَوَاصَوۡا بِالۡحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوۡا بِالصَّبۡرِ

translation.text: except those who have faith, do good, and urge each other to the truth, and urge each other to perseverance.

commentary.text: Except those who believe/have iman and do righteous good deeds, thus pure intentional actions aimed to please Allah SWT. These are the people who will be saved because they make their existence worthwhile.

First is faith (īmān), meaning sincere belief in Allah SWT, His Messenger, and the Hereafter, accompanied by conviction and submission with iman in our hearts even every day chores become an act of worship, for example, taking care of children, cooking for the family and even sleeping.

Second is righteous action, because faith must manifest in deeds that follow the guidance of Allah SWT and His Messenger (PBUH). These people don’t just sit around idle rather continue to do good deeds. They even use their idle time in worship/zikr because they know that every moment counts.

Third is mutual exhortation to truth, meaning believers do not live as isolated individuals but form a morally conscious community that upholds truth, justice, and the rights of Allah SWT and people. They warn and remind others towards the truth, recommending acts of obedience and avoiding prohibited acts.
Fourth is mutual exhortation to patience, encouraging one another to remain steadfast through the hardships and trials that inevitably come when living by the truth.

Encourage others to be patient and perseverance/steadfastness.  This patience and forbearance is essential when commanding good and forbidding evil. (People do not appreciate this advice at tiems and can be very harsh and cruel).
Together, these four qualities form the Qur’anic formula for true success (falāḥ) and protection from ultimate loss (khusr), both in this world and in the Hereafter.

Surah Al-‘Asr teaches that time itself testifies that humanity is in a state of loss, because life is limited and constantly slipping away. Every person, nation, and generation is subject to this rule unless they possess four qualities that transform life from loss into success.
The first two are personal foundations: true faith (īmān) in Allah SWT, His Messenger (PBUH) and the Hereafter, and righteous deeds that express that faith in obedience to divine guidance.

The next two are social responsibilities: believers must encourage one another to uphold truth, ensuring justice and moral integrity in society, and encourage one another to patience, supporting steadfastness through the trials that inevitably come when living by truth.

In this way, the surah presents a complete Qur’nic principle: time is humanity’s capital, and only a life built on faith, righteous action, truth, and perseverance leads to true success (falāḥ) instead of ultimate loss (khusr) in this world and the Hereafter.

items.text: IMAN + RIGHTEOUS DEEDS + URGE EACH OTHER TO TRUTH AND URGE EACH OTHER TO PERSEVERANCE = SUCCESS
Human life is slipping away in time, and without the right way of living it ends in total loss.
WHAT IS SPENT FOR ALLAH SWT IS THE PART THAT IS TRULY SAVED.
Time saved is the time in worship of Allah SWT, which is ironic given the surah is literally about not wasting time.

Hadith: The Prophet (PBUH) asked about a sheep that had been slaughtered and distributed. Aishah (RA) said that nothing remained except the shoulder. The Prophet (PBUH) replied that everything remains except the shoulder. Meaning: what was given in charity is what truly remains with Allah SWT, while what people keep and eat is what actually disappears.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah takes its name from the word occurring in the first Ayat. humazah

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: it is a Makki Surah; a study of its subject matter and style shows that this too is one of the earliest Surahs to be revealed at Makkah.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
This text criticizes the materialism and greed of pre-Islamic wealth-hoarders, highlighting their negative character and ultimate fate in the Hereafter. It argues that since such people often go unpunished in life, belief in the Hereafter is necessary. By reading Surahs from Az-Zilzal to Al-Humazah sequentially, one sees how core Islamic beliefs were instilled: every deed and intention will be judged; acts of violence and ingratitude are condemned; the outcome of the Hereafter depends on good versus bad deeds; materialistic pursuits distract from spiritual responsibility; and everyone must account for blessings received. Surah Al-Humazah culminates by questioning what fate should befall such negative leadership.

Surah Al-Humazah exposes a personality type that mocks people, spreads gossip, and measures success only by accumulated riches, imagining that wealth will secure permanence or protection.

Allah SWT warns that such arrogance and cruelty lead not to honor but to humiliation and punishment in the Hereafter.

The surah therefore teaches that wealth without humility and ethical conduct becomes a cause of spiritual ruin, and that dignity before Allah SWT lies not in material accumulation but in righteous character and accountability before divine judgment.

sections.title: 1-9 SLANDERER, DEFAMER AND STINGY SHALL BE THROWN INTO THE BLAZING FIRE

translation.text: Woe to every backbiter, slanderer,

commentary.text: The condemnation of Allah SWT is for those who habitually engage in (i) back biting and (ii) slander. Those who defame, ridicule humiliate and embarrass others. This means that the person finds fault with people and belittles them.This Ayat serves as a stark warning.

Woe to every Humazah Lumazah. 
Al-Hammaz refers to (slander) by speech, and Al-Lammaz refers to (slander) by action.
"Al-Humazah is with the hand and the eye, and Al-Lumazah is with the tongue."
Lesson: Previous Surah we are told to do good with people and encourage them to do good to others.

translation.text: who amasses wealth ˹greedily˺ and counts it ˹repeatedly˺,

commentary.text: The one who hoards, loves and is obsessed with wealth. But is devoid of spiritual wealth.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah derives its name from the word in the very first Ayat, ashab al fil.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: This is unanimously a Makki Surah; and if it is studied against its historical background, it appears that it must have been sent down in the very earliest stage at Makkah.

front_matter.label: Theme and subject matter
front_matter.text:
The background of Surah Al-Fil lies in the 6th-century political struggle over Arabia. Yemen had come under the Christian Kingdom of Aksum with support from the Byzantine Empire, partly to control regional trade routes. The Abyssinian governor Abrahah built a grand cathedral in Sana’a intending to redirect the Arabs’ pilgrimage away from the Kaaba.

When the cathedral was desecrated by an Arab, Abrahah marched toward Makkah with a large army and elephants to destroy the Ka'bah. The Quraysh, led by Abdul Muttalib, realized they could not resist such a force and withdrew, entrusting the protection of the sanctuary to Allah SWT. According to the Quran, Allah SWT destroyed the invading army through flocks of birds that struck them with stones, an event remembered as the “Year of the Elephant,” shortly before the birth of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).

sections.title: 1-5 A REMINDER THAT ALLAH CAN DEFEAT AN ARMY WITH ELEPHANTS THROUGH THE FLOCK OF BIRDS

arabic_lines: اَلَمۡ تَرَ كَيۡفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِاَصۡحٰبِ الۡفِيۡلِؕ

translation.text: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the people of the elephants?

commentary.text: The story of the People of the Elephant shows one of the great favors of Allah SWT to the Quraysh. After the Abyssinians took control of Yemen, their ruler Abrahah built a grand church in Sana’a to divert Arab pilgrimage from the Kaaba. He wanted people to come to worship there and not the Kaaba.

When the church was desecrated, he marched toward Makkah with a massive army and elephants to destroy the Ka'bah. On the way he defeated Arab tribes who tried to resist and eventually camped near Makkah, seizing property including the camels of Abdul Muttalib (the grandfather of the Prophet (PBUH) and leader of the Banu Hashim tribe). Unable to fight such a force, the Quraysh withdrew to the mountains while Abdul Muttalib prayed to Allah SWT for protection.

When the army attempted to advance, the lead elephant refused to move toward the Ka'bah, and Allah SWT sent flocks of birds carrying stones that destroyed the army and forced them to flee. This miraculous protection of the Ka'bah occurred in the Year of the Elephant, the same year that Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was born, preparing the way for his mission and demonstrating that Allah SWT Himself guards His Sacred House.

translation.text: Did He not frustrate their scheme?

commentary.text: In Surah Al-Fil, the word kayd refers to a harmful scheme. Although Abrahah openly marched with a large army to destroy the Kaaba, the real hidden plan was not merely religious retaliation but political and economic control. By destroying the Ka'bah, subduing the Quraysh, and intimidating the Arabs, the Abyssinians hoped to dominate the major trade route linking southern Arabia with Syria and Egypt.

Allah SWT, however, rendered this scheme fi-tadlil, meaning He caused their plan to go astray and become completely futile, nullifying their efforts and defeating their objective, just as the Quran elsewhere states that the plots of disbelievers ultimately fail.

translation.text: For He sent against them flocks of birds,

commentary.text: The word abābīl اَبَابِيۡلَۙrefers to many separate flocks coming from different directions in successive groups. These birds came from the direction of the Red Sea and were unlike any birds normally seen in Arabia. According to Ibn Abbas, they had beaks like birds and claws resembling a dog’s paw, while other reports describe their heads like birds of prey.

translation.text: that pelted them with stones of baked clay,

commentary.text: Each bird carried small stones of sijjīl, one in its beak and two in its claws, which they dropped on the army of the elephant. Reports preserved by historians mention that some people of Makkah later kept these stones; they were described as small, roughly the size of a pea or pine kernel, and dark reddish in color. These details emphasize the extraordinary nature of the event and how Allah SWT destroyed the army with seemingly small but divinely directed means.
Lesson: Rumi that we do in Haj is from here. Throwing small pebbles on Satan.

translation.text: leaving them like chewed up straw.

commentary.text: Allah SWT left the army of the Elephant like eaten straw or crushed crop husks; something completely destroyed and worthless. Allah SWT thus annihilated the army of Abrahah, scattering and weakening them so severely that they fled in ruin and their king died soon after returning to Yemen.

The Prophet (PBUH) later referred to this divine protection of Makkah, saying that just as Allah had restrained the Elephant from entering the city, He continued to preserve the sanctity of the Kaaba, a sacred status reaffirmed during events like the conquest of Makkah and the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

“I am the owner of the camels, so I ask for my camels.
The House has its Owner, and He will protect it.”

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah has been so entitled after the word in the very first Ayat, Quraish.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text:
Most scholars agree that Surah Quraysh is Makki.

Historically, the Quraysh gained their prominence after Qusayy ibn Kilab united the tribe in Makkah and organized the administration of the Ka'bah and the services for pilgrims. Because the Quraysh were custodians of the Ka'bah and served pilgrims generously, other tribes respected them and allowed their caravans to travel safely during their winter and summer trade journeys. And also because the other tribes had their idols in the Kaaba so they were afraid that their idols may be destroyed by the Quraysh if they misbehaved.

When Allah SWT destroyed Abrahah’s army in the Year of the Elephant, the prestige of both the Ka'bah and the Quraysh increased greatly across Arabia. Their trade routes became even more secure, and the Arabs regarded them as people under Allah’s protection. Surah Quraysh therefore reminds them that the prosperity, food, and safety they enjoy are favors from Allah SWT, and that they should therefore worship the Lord of this House alone.

Theme and Substance

Four brief sentences of this Surah, Quraish simply asked to consider: "When you yourselves acknowledge this House (i. e. the Ka'bah) to be Allah's House, and not of the idols, and when you fully well know that it is Allah alone Who has granted you peace by virtue of this House, made your trade and commerce flourish and saving you from destitution favored you with prosperity you should then worship and serve Him alone."

The central message of Surah Quraysh is that the Quraysh must worship Allah SWT alone because He is the One who granted them their prosperity, security, and unity. By protecting the Kaaba from the army in Surah Al-Fil, Allah SWT preserved the honor of the Quraysh, enabling their safe winter and summer trade journeys and providing them with food and protection from fear. The surah therefore reminds them that these blessings come from Allah SWT alone, and the proper response is to worship the Lord of this House instead of idols.

In short: security, provision, and prosperity are divine favors, and they obligate gratitude and exclusive worship of Allah SWT.

sections.title: 1-4 BELIEVE IN ALLAH WHO IS THE PROVIDER OF YOUR SUSTENANCE.

translation.text: Since the Quraysh became accustomed,

commentary.text: Surah Quraysh was written as a separate surah in the official Muṣḥaf compiled under Uthman ibn Affan, with Bismillah placed between it and Surah Al-Fil, even though the two are closely connected in meaning.
The word īlāf comes from alf, meaning familiarity, harmony, or becoming accustomed. Allah SWT instilled in the Quryash a love for trade. Quryash had a monopoly on trade.
Because they were custodians of the Kaaba they themselves thought they were the best, and other tribes respected and honored them and allowed their caravans to travel safely.

translation.text: accustomed to the journey of winter and summer

commentary.text: The trade journeys. In summer the Quraish travelled northward to Syria and Palestine, for they are cool lands, and in winter southward to Yaman, etc. for they are warm. It refers to how the Quraysh became accustomed to their safe winter and summer trade journeys to Yemen and Syria.

translation.text: therefore, let them worship the Lord of this House;

commentary.text: The Quraish have been blessed only by virtue of the House of Allah SWT. They themselves acknowledge that the 360 idols, which they worship, are not its lord, but Allah SWT alone is its Lord. He alone saved them from the invasion of the army of elephants. Him alone they had invoked for help against Abrahah’s army.

It was His House the keeping of which enhanced their rank and position in Arabia, for before that they were dispersed and commanded no position whatever. Like the common Arab tribes, they too were scattered factions of a race. But when they rallied round this House in Makkah and began to serve it, they became, honorable throughout Arabia, and their trade caravans began to visit every part of the country fearlessly.
Therefore, whatever they have achieved, it has been possible only by the help of the Lord of this House; therefore, they should worship Him alone.

translation.text: Who has fed them against hunger and made them secure against fear.

commentary.text: Allah SWT favors them with safety and gentleness, so they should single Him out for worship alone, without any partner. They should not worship any idol, rival or statue besides Him. Therefore, whoever accepts this command, Allah SWT will give him safety in both this life and the Hereafter. However, whoever disobeys Him, He will remove both of them from him.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah has been so designated after the word occurring in the first Ayat, al-kauthar.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text:
The surah was revealed when the Prophet (PBUH)was facing deep emotional and social pressure:

The Quraysh had turned hostile to him.

His followers were few and persecuted.

His sons Qasim and Abdullah had died, and his enemies mocked him as “abtar” (cut off, without legacy).

They assumed that once he died, his message would disappear.

Divine Response

front_matter.label: Allah SWT answers this cruelty with three concise declarations:
front_matter.text:
“Indeed We have granted you Al-Kawthar.”
This refers to abundant good, including the river in Paradise, but also the vast blessings given to the Prophet (PBUH): the Qur’an, his Ummah, his enduring remembrance, and the global spread of his message.

“So pray to your Lord and sacrifice.”
In response to divine favor, the Prophet (PBUH) is instructed to devote worship purely to Allah SWT, in contrast to the idolatry of Quraysh.

“Indeed your enemy is the one who is cut off.”
The insult is turned back on the mockers: they, not the Prophet (PBUH), will be the ones whose names and influence vanish.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text: Surah Al-Kawthar is a brief but powerful message in which Allah SWT consoles the Prophet (PBUH), promises him immense and everlasting الخير (abundant good), and declares that his enemies will ultimately be the ones cut off and forgotten.

front_matter.label: The surah establishes a profound reversal:
front_matter.text:
The Prophet (PBUH), whom people called “cut off,” is granted abundance and everlasting legacy.

His enemies, who appeared powerful at the time, are the ones historically erased.

Which history has confirmed with brutal clarity. Billions remember the Prophet (PBUH) daily, while the names of those mockers survive mostly as footnotes in tafsīr. Not exactly the outcome they were betting on.

Surah Al-Kawthar reassures the Prophet (PBUH) that Allah SWT has granted him immense and lasting blessing, commands him to respond with sincere worship, and declares that those who oppose him will ultimately be the ones truly cut off.

sections.title: 1-3 ALLAH HAS MADE MUHAMMAD'S NAME EVERLASTING

translation.text: Indeed, We have granted you ˹O Prophet˺ abundant goodness.

commentary.text: Allah SWT granted the Prophet (PBUH) “al-Kawthar,” an immense and limitless abundance of good and blessings. This includes the blessings of Prophethood, the Quran, knowledge and wisdom, the spread of Tawḥīd, the elevation of his name, and the vast Ummah that continues to follow him.

It also refers to the Fountain on the Day of Judgment and the River of Kawthar in Paradise granted to him. The Ayat was revealed when his enemies mocked him as “cut off,” assuring him that in reality Allah SWT had bestowed upon him boundless good and an enduring legacy.

Hadith Explanation:  the Prophet (PBUH) once dozed in the mosque, then woke smiling and recited Surah Al-Kawthar, saying it had just been revealed to him. He explained that Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise granted to him by Allah SWT, overflowing with abundant goodness. From it flows the Hawd (fountain) where his Ummah will gather on the Day of Judgment, whose vessels will be as numerous as the stars. The hadith also warns that some people will be turned away from it because they introduced changes after the Prophet (PBUH), showing that Al-Kawthar symbolizes both a literal river in Paradise and the immense blessings granted to the Prophet (PBUH).

translation.text: So pray and sacrifice to your Lord ˹alone˺.

commentary.text: Allah SWT commands the Prophet (PBUH) that, in response to the immense blessings granted by Allah SWT, he should devote his prayer and sacrifice solely to Allah SWT. In a society where the Quraysh and other Arabs performed worship and sacrifices for idols, the Ayat affirms the principle of pure Tawḥīd: all acts of worship, whether prayer or sacrifice, must be directed to Allah SWT alone. Thus, the Ayat calls for sincere gratitude and exclusive devotion to Allah SWT, rejecting all forms of polytheistic practice.

All acts of worship, whether obligatory or voluntary, must be performed with sincerity and without associating any partner with Him. The Ayat therefore emphasizes pure Tawḥīd, contrasting the Prophet’s devotion with the practice of the idolaters who prayed and sacrificed in the names of their false gods.

translation.text: Only the one who hates you is truly cut off ˹from any goodness˺.

commentary.text: Allah SWT declares that the Prophet’s true enemies, those who hated and mocked him, are the ones who are “abtar” (cut off) الۡاَبۡتَرُ. The Quraysh used this term to insult the Prophet (PBUH) after the death of his sons, claiming his legacy would end, but Allah SWT reversed the accusation and foretold that it would be his opponents who would be cut off from lasting honor, influence, and remembrance, while the Prophet (PBUH) would be granted an enduring legacy through his message and followers.

Surah Al-Kawthar (108:3) explains that the one who hates and mocks the Prophet (PBUH) is the one truly “abtar” (cut off). According to Ibn Kathir, several early scholars such as Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, and Qatadah said the Ayat referred to enemies like al-ʿAs ibn Wa’il, who mocked the Prophet (PBUH) after the death of his sons and claimed his legacy would disappear.

Allah SWT revealed this Ayat to declare the opposite: those who oppose and insult the Prophet (PBUH) will be cut off from lasting honor and remembrance, while Allah SWT will preserve the Prophet’s name, message, and followers until the Day of Judgment.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah takes its name from the word occurring in the first verse, al-kafirun.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text:
Surah Al-Kafirun is generally regarded by the majority of scholars as a Makki surah.

Historic background

Surah Al-Kafirun was revealed in Makkah when the leaders of the Quraysh repeatedly tried to persuade the Prophet (PBUH) to compromise in matters of faith. They offered wealth, leadership, and social status, and even suggested a mutual arrangement where each side would worship the other’s gods for a period of time. In response to these proposals, Allah SWT revealed this surah to give a clear and decisive rejection of such compromises, establishing that the worship of Allah SWT alone cannot be mixed with idolatry and that there can be no bargaining or “give and take” in matters of Tawḥīd.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
Surah Al-Kafirun establishes the principle of complete separation between Tawḥīd and disbelief, rejecting any compromise in matters of faith. Revealed when the Quraysh proposed mutual worship or “give and take” between Islam and their idols, the surah firmly declares that the Prophet (PBUH) and the believers will worship Allah SWT alone, and that Islam cannot be mixed with shirk in any form. Although originally addressed to the Quraysh, it serves as a permanent declaration for Muslims to dissociate themselves from disbelief and its practices, affirming unwavering commitment to pure monotheism.

Surah Al-Kafirun was revealed when the Quraysh tried to persuade the Prophet (PBUH) to compromise by alternating between worshipping Allah SWT and their idols. It establishes the principle of complete dissociation from shirk and unwavering commitment to Tawḥīd, affirming that the Prophet (PBUH) and the believers will worship Allah SWT alone while the disbelievers remain upon their own religion.

This is after the Prophet (PBUH) completed his guidance, yet the nation did not believe so at this point the Prophet (PBUH) stated his dissociation with the nation. There is now a separation as we see in the first Ayat. Where the Prophet is told to say you disbelievers not mankind.

commentary.text: Surah Al-Kafirun begins with the command, “Say: O disbelievers,” addressing those who reject the message of the Prophet (PBUH). The term kāfir الۡكٰفِرُوۡنَۙis not an insult but a description of those who deny the truth, and although the command is directed to the Prophet (PBUH), it also establishes a declaration for all believers.

The surah was revealed when the Quraysh proposed a compromise in which the Prophet (PBUH) would worship their idols for a time and they would worship Allah SWT in return. In response, Allah SWT revealed this surah as a clear renunciation of shirk, commanding the Prophet (PBUH) to completely disassociate himself from the idolaters and affirm that Islam and disbelief cannot be mixed or compromised.
Now there is a clear separation!!

translation.text: I do not worship those that you worship

commentary.text: Meaning, statues and rival gods.

The Prophet (PBUH) does not worship the gods that the disbelievers worship. This includes every form of worship directed to anything besides Allah SWT, whether idols, spirits, prophets, angels, natural objects, or imagined deities.

Even if people claim to worship Allah SWT while associating other beings with Him, that is not true worship of Allah SWT, because genuine worship must be pure and exclusive (Tawḥīd). Therefore, the Ayat establishes a complete rejection of any form of worship that mixes devotion to Allah SWT with partners or intermediaries. FYI – The Arabs would worship Allah SWT along with their idols and deities.
Lesson: Today we don’t have idols so much as we have shirk in the form of worshiping money, celebrities etc.

translation.text: neither do you worship Him Whom I worship;

commentary.text: This emphasizes that the disbelievers do not worship the same God in the same way as the Prophet (PBUH). Although some people claim to worship Allah SWT while associating partners, intermediaries, or incorrect attributes with Him, this differs fundamentally from the pure worship of Allah SWT taught by the Prophet (PBUH).
The Ayat therefore stresses that the true worship of Allah SWT based on pure Tawḥīd is completely distinct from any form of worship mixed with shirk or false conceptions of God.

commentary.text: This emphasizes the complete and lasting separation between the worship of the Prophet (PBUH) and that of the disbelievers. Unlike the earlier Ayat describing their current state, this statement indicates that they will not adopt the pure worship of Allah SWT, just as the Prophet (PBUH) will never worship the gods they or their forefathers worshipped.
The Ayat therefore reinforces that Islamic monotheism and polytheistic worship are fundamentally incompatible and cannot be reconciled.

translation.text: To you is your religion, and to me, my religion.

commentary.text: This is not a statement of religious compromise but a firm declaration of complete separation in matters of faith. It means that the Prophet (PBUH) and the believers will never worship the gods of the disbelievers, and the disbelievers are unwilling to worship Allah SWT alone; therefore, the two paths cannot be merged.

The Ayat decisively rejects the Quraysh’s proposals of religious “give and take” and establishes that Islam and disbelief are fundamentally distinct, leaving each side responsible for its own belief and deeds while affirming unwavering devotion to Allah SWT alone.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah takes its name from the word occurring in the first Ayat, nasr.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: This is a Makki Surah.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text: Surah An-Nasr declares that when Allah SWT grants victory and people enter Islam in large numbers. At that moment of triumph, he is commanded not to celebrate worldly success, but to glorify Allah SWT and seek His forgiveness, showing humility before his Lord. The Prophet (PBIUH) followed this command in his final days by frequently reciting words of tasbīḥ and istighfār, demonstrating that true success ends with gratitude, repentance, and preparation to meet Allah SWT.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah takes its name from the word in the first Ayat Lahab.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text:
Surah Al-Lahab is unanimously regarded as a Makki surah, though the exact time of its revelation is uncertain. It was likely revealed after Abu Lahab’s hostility toward the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) had become extreme and publicly evident, possibly around the period of the Quraysh boycott of Banu Hashim in Shiʿb Abi Talib, when he even sided with the Prophet’s enemies against his own clan. Because Abu Lahab was the Prophet’s uncle, such direct condemnation in the Qur’an would only have occurred after his persistent and widely recognized opposition to Islam.

Background

Surah Al-Lahab uniquely condemns Abu Lahab, the Prophet Muhammad’s (PBUH) uncle, by name because his hostility to Islam was exceptional. In Arab society, loyalty to one’s clan and protection of relatives (silah al-rahm) was a sacred moral duty, and even the Prophet’s clan supported him despite not all believing in his message. Abu Lahab alone broke this tradition by openly opposing, mocking, and harming the Prophet (PBUH), following him to gatherings to call him a liar and even supporting the Quraysh boycott against his own family. Because his public opposition misled others and violated the strongest social norms of Arabia, the Quran condemned him explicitly, establishing that faith, not blood ties or status, determines a person’s standing before Allah SWT.

When the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was commanded to warn his close relatives, he climbed Mount Ṣafā and called the Quraysh, asking whether they would believe him if he warned them of an approaching enemy. When they affirmed his truthfulness, he warned them of the coming punishment if they rejected the message of Allah SWT. At this point Abu Lahab, his uncle, reacted with open contempt and said: “May you perish! Did you gather us for this?” In response to this public rejection and his continued efforts to mock and obstruct the Prophet (PBUH), Allah SWT revealed Surah Al-Lahab, declaring the inevitable ruin of Abu Lahab and the futility of his wealth and status. The surah thus serves both as a condemnation of his persistent hostility and a prophetic declaration that his attempts to defeat Islam would ultimately fail.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text: In essence, the surah establishes a moral principle: neither lineage, social standing, nor material wealth can shield a person from accountability before Allah SWT. Persistent arrogance and opposition to truth lead inevitably to loss in both this life and the Hereafter.

sections.title: 1-5 CURSE OF ALLAH ON ABU LAHAB AND HIS WIFE, THE OPPONENTS OF THE HOLY PROPHET

translation.text: May the hands of Abu Lahab perish, and he ˹himself˺ perish!

commentary.text: His real name was Abd al-Uzza, and he was called Abu Lahab on account of his glowing, ruddy complexion. Lahab means the flame of fire, and Abu Lahab the one with a flaming, fiery face.

This, in fact, was not a curse which was invoked on him, but a prophecy in which an event taking place in the future, has been described in the past tense, to suggest that its occurrence in the future is certain and inevitable.

In fact, at last the same thing happened as had been foretold in this Surah a few years earlier. Breaking of the hands obviously does not imply breaking of the physical hands, but a person’s utterly failing in his aim and object for which he has exerted his utmost. And Abu Lahab indeed had exerted his utmost to defeat and frustrate the message of Islam presented by the Prophet (PBUH).

Hardly seven or eight years after the revelation of this Surah most of the big chiefs of Quraish, who were a party with Abu Lahab in his hostility to Islam, were killed in the Battle of Badr. When the news of the defeat reached Makkah, he was so shocked that he could not survive for more than seven days. His death occurred in a pitiable state. He became afflicted with malignant pustule and the people of his house left him to himself, fearing contagion. No one came near his body for three days after his death, until the body decomposed and began to stink. At last, when the people began to taunt his sons, according to one tradition, they hired some black people, who lifted his body and buried it.

According to another tradition, they got a pit dug out and threw his body into it by pushing it with wood, and covered it up with earth and stones. His utter failure became manifest when the religion which he had tried his utmost to impede and thwart, was accepted by his own children. First of all, his daughter, Darrah, migrated from Makkah to Madinah and embraced lslam; then on the conquest of Makkah, both his sons, Utbah and Muattab, came before the Prophet (peace be upon him) through the mediation of Abbas, believed and took oath of allegiance to him.

arabic_lines: مَاۤ اَغۡنٰى عَنۡهُ مَالُهٗ وَمَا كَسَبَؕ

translation.text: Neither his wealth nor ˹worldly˺ gains will benefit him.

commentary.text: Abu Lahab was a stingy, materialistic man. Ibn Jarir has stated that once in the pre-Islamic days he was accused of having stolen two golden deer from the treasury of the Kabah. Though later the deer were recovered from another person, the fact that he was accused of stealing indicates the opinion the people of Makkah held of him.

He was one of the four richest men of the Quraish, who owned one qintar (about 260 oz) of gold each. His love of wealth can be judged from the fact that when on the occasion of the battle of Badr the fate of his religion was going to be decided forever, and all the Quraish chiefs had personally gone to fight, he sent Aas bin Hisham to fight on his own behalf, telling him: This is in lieu of the debt of four thousand dirhams that you owe to me. Thus, he contrived a plan to realize his debt, for Aas had become bankrupt and there was no hope of the recovery of the debt from him. 
Some commentators have taken maa kasaba وَمَا كَسَبَؕin the meaning of the earning, i.e. the benefits that accrued to him from his wealth were his kasab (earning), and some other commentators have taken it to imply children, for the Prophet (peace be upon him) has said that a man’s son also is his kasab (earning).

Both these meanings fully correspond to the fate met by Abu Lahab. For when he was afflicted with the malignant pustule, his wealth availed him nothing, and his children also left him alone to die a miserable, wretched death. They did not even bury him honorably. Thus, within a few years the people witnessed how the prophecy which had been made in this Surah about Abu Lahab was literally fulfilled.

translation.text: Surely, he will be cast into a Flaming Fire

commentary.text: He will be cast in a flaming fire (Lahab).

translation.text: along with his wife, that carrier of slanderous tales;

commentary.text: Her name was Arwa and her nickname (kunyat) Umm Jamil. She was sister of Abu Sufyan and was no less bitter than her husband, Abu Lahab, in her enmity to the Messenger (PBUH).

Abu Bakr’s daughter Asma has related that when this Surah was revealed, and Umm Jamil heard it, she was filled with rage and went out in search of the Prophet (PBUH). She carried a handful of stones, and she was satirizing the Prophet (PBUH). She came to the Kabah, where the Prophet (PBUH) was sitting with Abu Bakr. The latter said: O Messenger of Allah, there she comes and I fear lest she should utter something derogatory to you. The Prophet (PBUH) replied: She will not see me. The same thing happened. She could not see the Prophet (PBUH) although he was there. She said to Abu Bakr: I hear that your companion has satirized me. Abu Bakr replied: No, by the Lord of this house, he has not satirized you. Hearing this she went off. What Abu Bakr meant was that she had not been satirized by the Prophet (PBUH), but by Allah Himself.

She used to strew thorns at the Prophet’s (PBUH) door in the night; therefore, she has been described as carrier of the wood. She used to carry evil tales and slander from one person to another in order to create hatred between them; therefore, she has been called the bearer of wood idiomatically.
She was supportive of her husband in his disbelief, rejection and obstinacy. Therefore, she will be helping to administer his punishment in the fire of Hell on the Day of Judgement.
FYI - Surah Tahreen we find examples of wives that are good with evil husbands and vice versa for example, Asia the wife of Pharon. Here we find two persons who are evil as husband and wife.

translation.text: upon her neck shall be a rope of palm-fibre.

commentary.text: The word used for her neck is jeed, جِيۡدِهَا  which in Arabic means a neck decorated with an ornament. She wore a valuable necklace and used to say: By Lat and Uzza, I will sell away this necklace and spend the price to satisfy my enmity against Muhammad (PBUH). That is why the word jeed has been used here ironically, thereby implying that in Hell she would have a rope of palm-fiber round her neck instead of that necklace upon which she prides herself so arrogantly.
Another example of this ironical style is found at several places in the Quran in the sentence: Bashshir-hum bi-adhab-in alima “Give them the good news of a painful torment.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: Al-Ikhlas is not merely the name of this Surah but also the title of its contents, for it deals exclusively with Tauhid. It has been given this name in view of its meaning and subject matter. Whoever understands it and believes in its teaching, will get rid of shirk (polytheism) completely.

front_matter.label: Period and Occasion of Revelation
front_matter.text: The exact occasion of revelation is debated because several different groups asked the Prophet (PBUH) similar questions about Allah SWT, and the same Surah answered them each time.

front_matter.label: The reports mention:
front_matter.text:
In every case, people were trying to understand Allah SWT using human categories like ancestry, material substance, gender, inheritance, or physical composition. The Quran responded by revealing or instructing the Prophet (PBUH) to recite Surah al-Ikhlāṣ, which completely rejects those assumptions.

Scholars explain that the Surah was originally revealed in Makkah, very early in the Prophet’s mission. Later, whenever similar questions arose, Allah SWT directed the Prophet (PBUH) to recite the same Surah again as the answer. Some narrators therefore described this as if it was revealed on those occasions, which explains the multiple reports.

Evidence it is an Early Makkan Surah

Its subject matter
Early Makkan revelation focused on the pure concept of Tawḥīd before detailed theology was revealed.

The story of Bilāl (RA). When his master Umayyah ibn Khalaf tortured him in Makkah, Bilāl repeatedly cried:

“Aḥad, Aḥad” (One, One).

That declaration comes directly from “Allāhu Aḥad” in this Surah, showing it was already known in the earliest period of Islam.

The Historical Purpose

The Surah answers a fundamental misunderstanding: People thought God must have;

items.text: The Quraysh in Makkah asking: “Tell us the lineage or ancestry of your Lord.”
A Bedouin asking what Allah SWT is made of.
Jewish rabbis asking about Allah’s nature, substance, and attributes.
Christians from Najran asking what Allah SWT is composed of.
a lineage,
a material composition,
offspring,
or something comparable to creation.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
At the time this Surah was revealed, the idolatrous polytheists were worshiping gods made of wood, stone, gold, silver and other substances. These gods had a form, shape and body. No goddess was without a husband and no god without a wife. They stood in need of food and drink, and their devotees arranged these for them.

Under such conditions when the people were invited to believe in Allah, the One Who has no associate, it was inevitable that questions arose in the minds as to what kind of a God it was.

It is a miracle of the Quran that in a few words briefly it answered all the questions and presented such a clear concept of the Being of Allah that destroyed all polytheistic concepts, leaving no room for the ascription of any of the human qualities to His Being.

Merit and Importance

That is why the Holy Messenger of Allah (PBUH) held this Surah in great esteem, and he made the Muslims realize its importance in different ways so that they recited it frequently and disseminated it among the people. For it states the foremost and fundamental doctrine of Islam (viz. Tauhid) in four such brief sentences as are immediately impressed on human memory and can be read and recited easily. There are a great number of the traditions of Hadith, which show that the Holy Prophet on different occasions and in different ways told the people that this Surah is equivalent to one third the Quran.

items.text: Although the Christians claimed to believe in One God, yet their God also had at least a son, and besides the Father and Son, and the Holy Ghost.

The Jews also claimed to believe in One God, but their God too was not without physical, material and other human qualities and characteristics. He went for a stroll, appeared in human form, wrestled with a servant of His, and was father of a son, Ezra.
Besides these religious communities, the Zoroastrians were fire worshipers, and the Sabeans star worshipers.

sections.title: 1-4 UNIQUE ATTRIBUTES OF ALLAH

translation.text: Say:1 “He is Allah, the One and Unique;

commentary.text: The Ayat answers the question people asked the Prophet (PBUH) Who is your Lord and what is He like?

The reply is direct and decisive. The Prophet (PBUH) is instructed to declare that the Lord being worshipped is Allah SWT, the very Creator whom even the Arabs already acknowledged as the Maker and Sustainer of the universe. Islam therefore did not introduce a new deity; it called people back to exclusive devotion to the One they already recognized as the supreme Creator.

The word “Ahad” اَحَدٌ ۚexpresses a deeper level of oneness than the ordinary word wāḥid. It affirms that Allah SWT is absolutely unique and indivisible. His being has no partners, no composition, no ancestry, no lineage, and no resemblance to creation. He alone creates, sustains, governs the universe, and responds to human need. His oneness is therefore complete in every sense: in His essence, His authority, His actions, and His right to be worshipped.
In short, the Ayat establishes the foundation of Islamic belief: Allah SWT is the one and only God, utterly unique, without partner, equal, or likeness.

“Qul huwa Allahu Ahad” answers the question about the Lord by clarifying that the Prophet (PBUH) had not introduced a new deity, but was calling to Allah SWT, the same Creator whom the Arabs already recognized as the Sustainer and Master of the universe, especially in times of hardship when they turned to Him alone.

The word Ahad does not mean merely one in number, but absolutely One, unique and without equal, partner, origin, or composition. It affirms that Allah SWT alone is the Creator, Owner, and Controller of all things, and that His being is completely indivisible, unlike anything in creation, with no lineage, no offspring, and no likeness in any way.

translation.text: Allah, Who is in need of none and of Whom all are in need;

commentary.text: Allah SWT, As-Ṣamad, means the One to whom all creation turns for its needs, while He Himself is completely free of need. Ibn ʿAbbās explained that He is perfect in every attribute of honor, authority, and lordship, and such absolute perfection belongs to none but Him, for nothing is equal to Him and nothing resembles Him.

The early scholars also said that As-Ṣamad is the Master whose control is complete and the One upon whom all depend in every affair, which shows that Allah SWT alone is perfectly self-sufficient, while all creation relies on Him for existence, help, and fulfillment of every need.

translation.text: He has never had offspring, nor was He born.

commentary.text: “Lam yalid wa lam yūlad” firmly denies that Allah SWT has any offspring or that He Himself was born, refuting the common belief of the polytheists that gods belong to a kind or race that begets and is begotten. Meaning, He does not have any child, parent or spouse.
Many people imagined their deities as having children, spouses, or ancestry, and even the Arabs called the angels daughters of Allah, while others declared certain holy men to be sons of God.
Such ideas would mean that God is physical, dependent, mortal, and part of a chain of inheritance, since procreation exists only among beings who are limited and need their species to continue.

By declaring that He neither begets nor is begotten, the Quran removes every trace of these false notions, affirming that Allah SWT is eternal, without origin, without offspring, without partner, and completely unique, as required by His being Ahad and As-Ṣamad.
Lesson: Arabs would say that the angels are Allah SWT daughters and Christians say the Jesus is Allah SWT’son. So this negates both views.

translation.text: and none is comparable to Him.

commentary.text: The word kufu كُفُوas used in the original means an example, a similar thing, the one equal in rank and position. In the matter of marriage, kufu means that the boy and the girl should match each other socially.
Thus, the Ayat means that there is no one in the entire universe, nor ever was, nor ever can be, who is similar to Allah SWT, or equal in rank with Him, or resembling Him.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text:
The name of this Surah is from the first Ayat. 
The surah is about protection from evil, and the One who can split the darkness and bring out light is the One who can remove harm. So, it is called the Daybreak not just to describe morning, but to show:
the One who brings light out of darkness is the One whose refuge is sought from the evils that appear in darkness.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text:
This Surah is a Makki Surah.

Introduction

The introduction explains that Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas are two separate Surahs, but because their subject matter is so closely related, they are known together as Al-Muʿawwidhatayn, meaning the two surahs in which refuge is sought with Allah SWT. Both teach the believer to seek protection in Allah SWT from different kinds of harm, so they are often discussed together even though each has its own wording and focus.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
The theme of Al-Muʿawwidhatayn (Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas) is seeking refuge in Allah SWT alone

when the Prophet (PBUH) faced intense opposition in Makkah after openly rejecting all compromise with disbelief, especially after the declaration in Surah Al-Kāfirūn that each side would follow its own religion. When hostility reached its peak, enemies resorted to plots, jealousy, slander, magic, and secret plans to harm him, while whispers from both men and jinn were spread to turn people away from the truth.

These surahs therefore teach that real safety does not come from worldly strength but from turning to Allah SWT alone, whose power is supreme over every hidden and open evil.

Is reciting verses, blowing, or using amulets allowed in Islam, or is it superstition?

The recitation of Ayats, supplications, and seeking protection through the words of Allah SWT, as done with Al-Muʿawwidhatayn, is permitted in Islam, as it is established that the Prophet (PBUH)  who used to recite these surahs, blow into his hands, and wipe over his body, especially during illness, and he also allowed others to recite prayers for protection and healing.

However, such practices are allowed only when the words are from the Quran, the names of Allah SWT, or clear supplications free from shirk, and when one believes that benefit comes from Allah alone, not from the words themselves.

The Prophet (PBUH) encouraged medical treatment and taught that every illness has a cure, but he also allowed ruqyah (supplication for healing) alongside treatment, provided it did not involve superstition or dependence on charms. Therefore, recitation for protection is permissible as a form of duʿā and trust in Allah SWT, but turning it into a profession, relying on amulets, or abandoning proper means of treatment contradicts the spirit of tawakkul and the practice of the Prophet (PBUH).

The relation between Surah Al-Fatihah and Al-Muʿawwidhatayn shows the harmony between the beginning and the end of the Quran.

The Quran opens with Al-Fatihah, where the servant praises Allah SWT, declares that he worships Him alone, and asks for guidance to the Straight Path. In response, the entire Quran is revealed as that guidance. At the end, in Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas, the servant again turns to Allah SWT, seeking refuge in the Lord of all creation, the Lord, King, and God of mankind, asking protection from every evil, especially from the whisperings of devils from among jinn and men, which are the greatest obstacles to remaining on the Straight Path.

Thus, the Quran begins with a prayer for guidance and ends with a prayer for protection, showing that a person needs Allah SWT not only to find the truth, but also to remain firm upon it.

sections.title: 1-5 SEEK REFUGE WITH ALLAH FROM ALL EVILS

translation.text: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak

commentary.text: Reason: Surah Al-Falaq and An-Nas were recited when the Prophet (PBUH) was affected by a spell cast by the Jew Labīd ibn al-Aʿṣam, who used strands of the Prophet’s hair placed in a well. The Prophet (PBUH) became ill for a period, and Allah SWT informed him of the cause through a dream in which angels showed him where the spell was hidden. When it was removed, he recited the two surahs, and with each verse the knots of the spell were undone until he was fully cured by Allah’s permission. This report is found in authentic hadith collections such as Bukhari and Muslim, but many scholars explain that the incident does not mean the Prophet (PBUH) was affected in his message or revelation. Rather, the effect was only physical, like illness, and Allah protected him from any harm related to conveying the Qur’an. The surahs therefore were not revealed only for this event but serve as general supplications teaching believers to seek refuge in Allah SWT from every kind of evil, including envy, magic, and the whispering of devils.
Say, "I seek refuge with the Lord of Al-Falaq." Al-Falaq is the morning.

In “Qul aʿūdhu bi-Rabbil-falaq”, the command Qul is part of revelation, so although it is addressed first to the Prophet (PBUH), it also applies to every believer, teaching them how to seek refuge in Allah SWT.

The refuge meant here is not ordinary physical protection, but seeking safety with Allah SWT from every kind of evil, whether material, moral, or spiritual, which is required by tawḥīd, since such absolute protection can be sought from none but Him.

The word falaq means splitting or cleaving and is understood as the breaking of dawn from the darkness of night, and also as the bringing forth of all creation, since everything comes into existence by being split open from something else. Thus Rabbil-falaq means the Lord who brings light out of darkness and brings creation into being, and seeking refuge with Him means turning to the One who has complete power over all creation to protect from the evil that may arise from it.

translation.text: from the evil of all that He created;

commentary.text: Refuge is sought from the evil found in creation, not from the act of creation itself. Evil is not attributed to Allah SWT, for He created all things with wisdom and for good purpose, but harm may arise from some creatures because of the qualities placed in them.

This general statement already includes seeking protection from every kind of harm, whether physical, moral, or spiritual, known or unknown, in this world or the Hereafter, and the Ayats that follow mention particular evils only for emphasis because of their severity.
Seeking refuge with the Creator is the most complete protection, since He alone has full power over His creation and knows the dangers that humans see as well as those, they do not.

The word sharr includes both suffering itself, such as illness, poverty, sadness, loss, or injury, and the causes of suffering, such as disbelief, sin, envy, or wrongdoing, so the believer asks Allah SWT to protect him from every evil that has occurred and every evil that may yet occur.
Lesson: Every creation has the potential of Sharr.

translation.text: from the evil of night's darkness when it spreads around;

commentary.text: After seeking refuge from all evil in general, the believer is taught to seek protection from particular harms, beginning with the darkness of night. The word ghāsiq غَاسِقٍ means intense darkness, and waqab وَقَبَۙmeans when it settles, spreads, or enters, referring to the time when night fully covers everything. Night is mentioned because many evils occur in it: satan, Jinn, crimes, secret plots, attacks, and the movement of harmful creatures, and in the time of the Prophet (PBUH) people especially feared the dangers that came after dark. When we sleep no one can protect us.
The connection with Rabbil-falaq is subtle, since the One who brings the dawn out of darkness is the One whose protection is sought from the evils that spread in the darkness.

translation.text: from the evil of the women who blow on knots;

commentary.text: The word ʿuqad الۡعُقَدِۙmeans knots tied in a string or thread, and naffāthāt النَّفّٰثٰتِ  refers to those who blow upon them. This refers to magicians, because those who practice magic tie knots and blow on them while casting spells. Thus, the meaning is seeking refuge from the evil of those who perform sorcery, whether men or women. And from the evil of the blowers in knots when they perform their spells and blow into the knots.

Magic is condemned in the Quran and described as something connected with devils, and the Prophet (PBUH) counted it among the grave sins. Therefore, the believer is taught to seek refuge with Allah SWT from the evil of magicians who try to harm others through such practices.
Lesson: Magic is haram but it is a reality similarly alcohol is a reality but it is haram.

translation.text: and from the evil of the envier when he envies.”

commentary.text: Ask protection from the person who is envious or jealous. This means that a person feels unhappy at the favor, superiority, or good that Allah SWT has given to another and wishes that it be taken away from him, or that he be deprived of it. It does not mean wishing for a similar blessing for oneself but wishing the other to lose it.
Thus, refuge is sought from the evil of the envier when he envies, meaning when his jealousy.

When harm comes from an envier, refuge should be sought with Allah SWT. Protection from such evil is helped by trusting that none can harm except by Allah’s will, remaining patient over what the envier says or does, keeping dignity and piety, avoiding preoccupation with him, doing good even to him, and remaining firm upon tawḥīd, for the heart that holds to tawḥīd is not overcome by fear of anyone besides Allah SWT.
Lesson: Evil Eye and Plots of a Person who is envious.

When a person cannot protect himself from the harms of the world, the unseen, and the evil intentions of others, he turns to Allah SWT alone, because only the Creator has power over all creation and can truly protect.
Recite these Ayats after salah, AM and PM and before sleeping.
Surah al-Falaq teaches that every kind of harm — seen or unseen, natural or human, open or hidden — can only be escaped by seeking protection in Allah SWT, the Lord who controls all creation.

SURAH AL-FALAQ = SEEKING ALLAH’S PROTECTION FROM EVERY EXTERNAL EVIL.
(AND SURAH AN-NAS COMPLETES IT BY SEEKING PROTECTION FROM INTERNAL AND WHISPERING EVIL.)

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text:
The name of this Surah is from the first Ayat.

Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas are twin surahs of seeking refuge in Allah SWT, most likely first revealed in Makkah, then recited again later in Madinah in response to different forms of harm and opposition.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text:
Originally Makki surahs, then recited again later in Madinah.
A surah may be revealed earlier, then later brought back to the Prophet (PBUH)’s attention during a new event or when opposition was intense, and later during the incident of magic.

Theme

The theme of Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas (Al-Mu‘awwidhatayn) is seeking refuge in Allah SWT from every form of harm. These surahs were revealed at a time when the Prophet (PBUH) was surrounded by hostility, jealousy, secret plots, magic, and psychological pressure from the Quraysh and others who could not accept his message.

Allah SWT instructed him to rely not on worldly strength but on divine protection alone. Surah Al-Falaq teaches seeking refuge from external evils such as darkness, sorcery, and envy, while Surah An-Nas teaches seeking refuge from the hidden whisperings that enter the hearts of people, whether from jinn or human beings.

Together, they show that the one who remains steadfast on truth is protected only by turning to Allah SWT, whose power is above all forces of harm.

Is reciting Ayats for protection allowed in Islam, and do they actually work?

Authentic hadith show that the Prophet (PBUH) himself recited the Mu‘awwidhatayn, and sometimes Surah Al-Ikhlas with them, blew into his hands, and wiped his body for protection, especially during illness, and he allowed similar practices for others as long as they contained no shirk and relied on the words of Allah SWT or clear supplications.

The Prophet (PBUH) also permitted ruqyah (recitation for healing) for snakebite, illness, and the evil eye, while teaching that cure comes only by Allah SWT’s will and that one should not abandon medical treatment or place independent power in charms themselves.

Therefore, reciting Qur’anic Ayats or supplications for protection is allowed, but turning amulets, charms, or recitation into superstition, blind reliance, or a profession for earning money is against the spirit of Islam, which requires trust in Allah SWT together with lawful means of treatment.

translation.text: Say: “I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind;
