commentary.text: Reason: Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas were revealed when the Prophet (PBUH) was affected by a spell of magic cast by Labid ibn al-A‘ṣam, who used hair from the Prophet’s comb and placed it in a well. According to the reports, the Prophet (PBUH) experienced physical weakness and imagined certain personal actions without having done them, but no change occurred in his conveying of revelation.

Allah SWT informed him of the cause through a dream in which two angels explained where the spell had been hidden. The object was recovered, and when the Prophet (PBUH) recited the Mu‘awwidhatayn, the knots of the spell were undone one by one until he was cured. The narrations emphasize that the harm affected only his human condition, not his Prophethood, and that he did not seek revenge against the one responsible, showing his forbearance and trust in Allah SWT.
In Surah An-Nas, instead of simply saying A‘udhu billah (I seek refuge in Allah), the Quran teaches seeking refuge through three specific attributes of Allah SWT:
Rabb-in-naas (Lord and Sustainer/Nurturer of mankind.)
Malik-in-naas (King and Master/Authority of mankind), and
Ilah-in-naas (the true God of mankind. Our Creator).
These attributes show that Allah SWT alone has complete authority, control, and right to be worshipped, and therefore only He can give real protection from evil.

Because He is the Lord, King, and God of mankind, every human is under His control, and no one else can grant refuge from the evil of the whisperer who withdraws, meaning Shaytan, who is assigned to every person and constantly tries to mislead him by beautifying evil and casting doubts into the heart.

The Prophet (PBUH)said that every human has such a companion from satan, but Allah SWT protects whom He wills. Shaytan’s influence is hidden and enters the heart without being seen, the believer is taught to seek refuge with the One who has complete lordship, sovereignty, and divinity over mankind, for only Allah SWT can protect the heart from the whisperings of jinn and men that prevent a person from remaining on the straight path.
Lesson: Allah SWT controls, rules, and is worshipped — therefore He alone can protect the human heart.

translation.text: from the evil of the lurking whisperer—

commentary.text: The phrase “al-waswās al-khannās” الۡوَسۡوَاسِ   refers to the one who repeatedly whispers evil suggestions into the heart and then withdraws, only to return again when a person becomes heedless.
The word waswās indicates continual whispering, while khannās describes one who hides after appearing and comes back again and again.

This shows that evil usually begins with small, repeated thoughts rather than sudden actions. A suggestion enters the heart, then becomes a desire, then an intention, and finally an action if it is not stopped.

For this reason, seeking refuge in Allah SWT means asking Him to protect the heart at the earliest stage, before the whisper grows into sin. The whisperer may be from among the jinn, from human beings, or from a person’s own self, since the Qur’an states that Allah SWT knows the suggestions that arise within the soul.

Shayṭān misguides step by step, first trying to lead a person away from faith, then toward error, then toward sin, and if that fails, by stirring pride, anger, or distraction from what is right. Therefore, the surah teaches that the believer’s safety lies not in relying on himself, but in constantly seeking refuge in Allah SWT, because the struggle against these whispers continues throughout life and only Allah SWT can fully protect the heart.
"The devil who is squatting (perched) upon the heart of the Son of Adam. So when he becomes absentminded and heedless he whispers. Then, when he remembers Allah he withdraws."
"It has been mentioned to me that Shaytan is Al-Waswas. He blows into the heart of the Son of Adam when he is sad and when he is happy. But when he (man) remembers Allah, Shaytan withdraws."

And the word khannas means he retreats when Allah SWT is remembered and he returns when man become heedless. So the Surah teaches that the heart is a battlefield that keeps reopening. 24/7 active; Satan does not take a break.

So the whisperings of Satan do not penetrate into the heart (which is deeper in the chest) rather hover around it (in the chest/breast) suggesting a more superficial influence but still can be deeply impactful.

It’s a statement of surrender, not a direct expulsion.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah derived its name from the word in the second Ayat. This is not only a name but also a title of its subject matter, for implies the news of Resurrection and Hereafter and the whole Surah is devoted to the same theme.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: As we have explained in the introduction to Surah Al-Mursalat, the theme of all the Surahs, from Al- Qiyamah to An-Naziat, closely resembles one another's, and all these seem to have been revealed in the earliest period at Makkah.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text: Surah An-Naba affirms the certainty of the Resurrection and warns of its consequences, addressing the doubts the people of Makkah expressed about life after death. The Surah points to signs in creation—earth, mountains, night and day, human pairs, rain, and the ordered heavens—to show that the One who created all this can certainly resurrect mankind and hold them accountable. It describes the fate of those who deny the Hereafter—recorded deeds, inevitable punishment in Hell—and contrasts it with the reward of the righteous, who will receive abundant recompense and additional gifts. The Surah concludes by portraying the Divine Court where no one speaks without permission and where intercession is limited to those whom Allah SWT allows, ending with a warning that the Day of Judgment is near, and every person will face the outcome of their choices.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surahs name is from the first Ayat.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text:
Surah Abasa was revealed after an incident in which the Prophet (PBUH) was addressing several leading Quraysh chiefs, hoping they might incline toward Islam. During this, the blind Companion Ibn Umm Maktūm approached seeking guidance and explanation about the faith. The Prophet (PBUH) disliked the interruption and momentarily ignored him, whereupon Allah SWT revealed this Surah to correct the prioritization of sincere seekers over influential rejectors.

The historical details establish the Surah’s early Makkan origin:
• Ibn Umm Maktūm was among the earliest Muslims, already seeking knowledge with sincerity.
• The Quraysh figures present—‘Utbah, Shaybah, Abu Jahl, Umayyah bin Khalaf, Ubayy bin Khalaf—were still in occasional dialogue with the Prophet (PBUH), indicating a very early phase before hostilities hardened.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
This Surah tells us about the character of the bearer of the Quran. A person who has the Quran in their heart then despite how annoying a situation can be they must behave in a certain manner. Although the Surah opens with words that appear to reproach the Prophet (PBUH), the fuller context shows that Allah SWT’s real displeasure is directed at the arrogant Quraysh chiefs who rejected the truth with contempt.

The Prophet (PBUH) had focused on them only because he hoped that winning over influential leaders would help the spread of Islam—not out of disregard for the blind seeker, nor out of preference for the wealthy. Allah SWT corrected this approach: in the mission of da‘wah, the true priority is anyone sincerely seeking guidance, regardless of status, while those indifferent or arrogant are not to be given undue importance.

Ayats 1–16 address this principle of preaching. From Ayat 17 onward, the Surah turns to rebuking the disbelievers for their ingratitude toward their Creator and warns them of the severe consequences they will face on the Day of Resurrection.

This Ayat is a pair of Surah Naziat.

ALLAH SWT HAS OPENED BOTH WAYS MAKING EACH SMOOTH AND EASY SO THAT HE COULD FOLLOW ANY WAY THAT HE LIKED.

Man can do nothing more than to dig the soil, or plough it, and bury in it the seeds that God has already created. Beyond this everything is done by God.
Had God not created the seeds with these qualities and the upper layers of the earth with these capabilities; man could not by himself have arranged any kind of food on the earth.

15-29 AL-QURAN IS CONVEYED TO THE PROPHET THROUGH ANGEL GABRIEL AND THIS MESSAGE IS FOR ALL THE PEOPLE OF THE WORLD

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The name of this Surah is from Ayat one.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: The subject matter and the style clearly show that it is one of the earliest Surahs to be revealed at Makkah.

front_matter.label:
1. The Hereafter:
It describes the events of the DoJ—the sun darkening and folding up, stars scattering, mountains uprooted, seas boiling, souls returning to bodies, records opened, and every person seeing the results of their deeds.
front_matter.text:
2. The Quran is the Word of Allah SWT
It then confirms that Muhammad (PBUH) is truly Allah SWT’s Messenger, receiving the Quran from the trustworthy angel Gibriel. It is not madness or deception, so people should not turn away from this truth.

sections.title: 1-14 A SCENE FROM THE SCENES OF THE DoJ

translation.text: When the sun is wrapped up [in darkness]

commentary.text: “When the sun is wrapped up” means its light will be rolled back and extinguished on the Day of Resurrection.
The term takwīr— كُوِّرَتۡused for wrapping a turban—expresses the idea of the sun’s radiance being folded in until it disappears.
These events are mentioned as though they have already happened. It is the certainty of the future that is being described. That there is no doubt in this happening.
Lesson: The most catastrophic event on earth is the DoJ. So prepare for a future that is certain.

translation.text: and when the stars fall down,

commentary.text: “When the stars scatter away” means that the force holding the stars in their fixed positions will be released, causing them to fall, disperse, and lose their light. Inkidar انْكَدَرَتۡimplies both scattering and darkening.

translation.text: and when the mountains are blown away,

commentary.text: A day when the mountains will scatter like cotton wool and then become dust.

translation.text: and when pregnant camels are left untended,

commentary.text: This was by far the best way of giving an idea of the severities and horrors of Resurrection to the Arabs. Before the buses and trucks of the present day there was nothing more precious for the Arabs than the she-camel just about to give birth to her young. In this state she was carefully looked after and cared for, so that she is not lost, stolen, or harmed in any way. The people’s becoming heedless of such she-camels, in fact, meant that at that time they would be so stunned as to become unmindful of their most precious possessions.

translation.text: and when wild beasts are gathered together,

commentary.text: On that Day all kinds of beasts and animals gather in one place, then neither the snake bites, nor the tiger kills and devours.

translation.text: and when the seas are set on fire,

commentary.text: A day when the seas will be full of flaming fire.
The above Ayats vividly describe the DoJ. So take heed!

translation.text: and when the souls ˹and their bodies˺ are paired ˹once more˺,

commentary.text: From here begins mention of the second stage of Resurrection.

Men will be resurrected precisely in the state as they lived in the world before death with body and soul together. Every type (of soul) will be gathered with its peer (or mate). It will be said to the angels:" Every man will be with every group of people who performed the same deeds that he did.
Also see (37:22)
Assemble those who did wrong, together with their companions (from the devils).

translation.text: and when baby girls, buried alive, are asked

commentary.text: Questioning the Female Infant Who was buried Alive. Allah SWT will not even speak to the criminals rather will address the victims.

translation.text: for what crime they were put to death,

commentary.text: “For what crime…” exposes the horror of burying infant girls alive. Allah SWT questions the girl—not the parents—to show how innocent she was and how monstrous the act was. This Ayat proves two things: the moral corruption of pre-Islamic society and the necessity of a Judgment Day where all crimes will be accounted for. Islam abolished this practice and elevated the status of daughters.
Day of Justice.

translation.text: and when the records ˹of deeds˺ are laid open,

commentary.text: Every person will be given his paper in his right hand or in his left hand. All crimes will be exposed, and everyone’s truth will be apparent. Noone can hide their deeds.

translation.text: and when the sky is stripped away,

commentary.text: Everything which is hidden till now will become visible. At that time the Kingdom of God will appear in full view, without any veil in between.

translation.text: and when the Hellfire is fiercely flared up,
and when Paradise is brought near—

commentary.text: Unveiling the Heavens, both Hellfire, and Paradise Being Brought Near.

translation.text: ˹on that Day˺ each soul will know what ˹deeds˺ it has brought along.

commentary.text: This is the conclusive response of the previous statements, meaning at that time every soul will know what it has done, and that will be brought forth for.
Also see (3:30)
On the Day when every person will be confronted with all the good, he has done, and all the evil he has done, he will wish that there were a great distance between him and his evil.
Lesson: Soon we will be going on a journey so we should prepare.

sections.title: 15-29 AL-QURAN IS CONVEYED TO THE PROPHET THROUGH ANGEL GABRIEL AND THIS MESSAGE IS FOR ALL THE PEOPLE OF THE WORLD

translation.text: I do swear by the receding stars

commentary.text: Allah SWT takes an oath by the receding stars.

translation.text: which travel and hide,

commentary.text: The stars that proceed then disappear like comets and shooting stars.

translation.text: and the night as it falls

commentary.text: Allah SWT is swearing by the night and its darkness when it approaches.

translation.text: and the day as it breaks!

commentary.text: Allah SWT takes another oath by the morning light when it breathes life into the day. The day comes alive.

translation.text: Indeed, this ˹Quran˺ is the Word of ˹Allah delivered by Gabriel,˺ a noble messenger-angel,

commentary.text: The conclusion of the oaths is that the Quran is the Word of Allah SWT. What is being presented in the Quran is not the bragging of an insane person, or the evil suggestion of a devil.

It has been made clear that the Prophet (PBUH) is presenting the Quran in his capacity as the Messenger of God and not as Muhammad bin Abdullah (PBUH). It has been given to the Prophet (PBUH) by angel Gabriel.
For further explanation, see of Surah Al- Haaqqah Ayat 39 and 40.

translation.text: full of power, held in honour by the Lord of the Throne,

commentary.text: Angel Gabriel has a position of honor as he is near the Throne of his Lord.

translation.text: obeyed there ˹in heaven˺, and trustworthy.

commentary.text: That is, he is the chief of the angels, and all angels work under his command.
Lesson: Angel Gibriel has been entrusted with the Quran. He is near Allah SWT and the chief of all other angels. This is how high a status he has.

translation.text: (O people of Makkah), your companion is not mad;

commentary.text: Here, Allah SWT mentions that the Prophet (PBUH) was the companion of the people of Makkah. They are being reminded that the Prophet (PBUH) was no stranger for them. He was not an outsider but a man of their own clan and tribe; he had lived his whole life among them; even their children knew that he was a very wise man. They should not be so shameless as to call such a man a mad man.
For further explanation, see Surah An-Najm Ayat 1.

translation.text: And he has already seen Gabriel in the clear horizon.

commentary.text: This observation of the Prophet (PBUH) has been described in greater detail in Surah An-Najm Ayat 10.

translation.text: And Muhammad is not a withholder of [knowledge of] the unseen.

commentary.text: The Messenger (PBUH) does not conceal anything from you. Whatever of the unseen realities are made known to him by Allah SWT, whether they relate to the essence and attributes of Allah SWT, the angels, life-after death and Resurrection, or to the Hereafter, Heaven and Hell, he conveys everything to you without change.

translation.text: And this ˹Quran˺ is not the word of an outcast devil.

commentary.text: You are wrong in thinking that some Satan comes and whispers these words into the ear of Muhammad (PBUH).
It does not suit Satan that he should divert man from polytheism, idol worship, atheism and sin and then turn to God-worship and Tauhid.
For further explanation Surah Ash-Shuara, Ayats 210-212.

translation.text: So what ˹other˺ path would you take?

commentary.text: Where has your reason gone, in rejecting this Quran, while it is manifest, clear, and evident that it is the truth from Allah SWT.

translation.text: Surely this ˹Quran˺ is only a reminder to the whole world—

commentary.text: This Quran is a reminder for all of mankind. They are reminded by it and receive admonition from it. That is man in his fitra knows right from wrong and in his soul understands the truth however life has subdued or diminished his fitra.
The Quran is a reminder. Quran activates our dormant inner consciousness by reminding us of what we already know to be true. Quran is good for us!

translation.text: to whoever of you wills to take the Straight Way.

commentary.text: In other words, although this is an admonition for all mankind, only such a person can benefit by it, who is himself desirous of adopting piety and righteousness. Man’s being a seeker of truth and a lover of right is the foremost condition of his gaining any benefit from it. Meaning man must want/desire guidance to be guided.

translation.text: But you cannot will ˹to do so˺, except by the Will of Allah, the Lord of all worlds.

commentary.text: Humans are not independent beings; a person can only choose guidance or misguidance within the will and permission of Allah SWT. When the earlier Ayat said, “whoever wills to be upright,” Abu Jahl claimed this meant full human control. Allah SWT responded by revealing that no one can anything unless Allah SWT Himself wills it. This affirms divine sovereignty over all choices.
A MAN MUST WANT GUIDANCE AND THEN IF ALLAH SWT SO WILLS, HE WILL GET GUIDANCE. THERE IS NO COMPULSION IN RELIGION.
Lesson: Ask Allah SWT for guidance and then remain on guidance. ASK EVERY DAY!!

A vivid description of the Day of Judgement.  As well as what happens after we are resurrected from our graves.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surahs name is from the first Ayat.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: This Surah and the Surah At-Takwir closely resemble each other in their subject matter. This shows that both were sent down in about the same period.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
Its theme is the Hereafter.

The Holy Messenger (PBUH) said: "The one who wants that he should see the Resurrection Day as one would see it with one's eyes, should read Surah At-Takwir, Surah Al-Infitar and Surah Al-Inshiqaq".

In this Surah first the Resurrection Day has been described, and it is said that when it occurs, every person will see whatever he has done in the world.

In conclusion, it has been forcefully stated that the Day of Resurrection will surely take place when the righteous shall enjoy every kind of bliss in Paradise and the wicked shall be punished in Hell. On that day no one shall avail anyone anything. All powers of judgment shall be with Allah.

sections.title: 1-19 DESCRIPTION OF WHAT WILL HAPPEN ON THE DAY OF JUDGEMENT AND GUARDIAN ANGELS ARE RECORDING ALL ACTIONS AND ALLAH HIMSELF WILL BE THE JUDGE

translation.text: When the heaven is split asunder,

commentary.text: The beautiful blue sky overhead, which we take for granted in sunshine and storm, will be shattered to pieces before the New World is established. The partition which seems at present to divide things divine from the phenomenal world has to be shattered before each soul knows the reality about itself.
Lesson: We learn about this many times that the peaceful calm sky will split open. Total destruction. The veil will be lifted.

translation.text: And when the stars fall, scattering,
and when the seas burst forth,
and when the graves spill out,

commentary.text: In the first three Ayats, the first stage of the Resurrection has been mentioned, and, in this Ayat, the second stage is being described. Opening of the graves implies resurrection of the dead.

translation.text: ˹then˺ each soul will know what it has sent forth or left behind.

commentary.text: “What he sent forward and what he left behind” includes all three meanings:
Actions done and actions neglected—every deed of commission and omission.
Earlier and later deeds—a person’s entire life record, shown in full sequence.
Good or evil done directly and the lasting effects left behind—the influence of one’s actions on others after death. (legacy)

translation.text: O humanity! What has emboldened you against your Lord, the Most Generous,

commentary.text: This Ayat was revealed concerning Al-Aswad ibn Shariq, who allegedly struck the Prophet (PBUH). Despite this aggression, the Prophet (PBUH) did not retaliate, demonstrating his patience and forbearance. The Ayat was then revealed as a rebuke to the offender, asking: What deluded you into acting so arrogantly and sinfully against your Lord, Who is Most Generous?

Meaning in context: The question “What deceived you or emboldened you?” exposes the sinner’s misplaced confidence — behaving as if Allah SWT would not hold him accountable. The mention of “the Most Generous” intensifies the reproach: despite Allah SWT’s immense mercy and generosity, the person still dared to commit wrong.

Note: Classical commentators mention this story, but they also clarify that the Ayat carries a general meaning: it addresses every person who becomes heedless of accountability before Allah SWT, not only one individual.
Lesson: Surah Hadid and Lukman have the same theme. Satan emboldens man to commit sin thinking it is legit and saying that Allah SWT is most forgiving and Rehman.

translation.text: Who created you, fashioned you, and perfected your design,
moulding you in whatever form He willed?

commentary.text: Allah SWT made mankind perfectly balanced, upright and proportioned in stature. He fashioned you in the best of forms and shapes.

translation.text: But no! In fact, you deny the ˹final˺ Judgment,

commentary.text: The Ayats emphasize that there is no rational basis for a human being to be deceived about Allah SWT or to feel secure from accountability. A person’s very existence testifies that he was created deliberately by a Wise, Powerful, and Beneficent Lord—not by accident, nor by his parents, nor by blind natural forces.

Therefore, the real cause of a person’s delusion is not any justified reasoning but a false belief that there will be no resurrection, no reckoning, and no consequence for one’s actions. This baseless assumption breeds heedlessness, moral irresponsibility, and a deceptive sense of safety from Allah SWT’s justice.

translation.text: you do so the while there are watchers over you;
honourable angels, recording ˹everything˺.
They know whatever you do.

commentary.text: Denying the Hereafter does not change its reality. Allah SWT has appointed noble, righteous angels to record every action a person performs. They are completely honest, impartial, and uncorrupted:
A human being is never unobserved or alone. Every action and intention is faithfully documented for the final accountability before Allah SWT.

translation.text: Indeed, the righteous will be in pleasure,
and the wicked shall be in the Blazing Fire.
They shall enter it on the Day of Recompense
and they will have no escape from it.
What will make you realize what Judgment Day is?

commentary.text: Allah SWT is asking mankind that, ‘do you realize or understand what that Day is?? The significance of that Day?

translation.text: Again, what will make you realize what Judgment Day is?

commentary.text: Again, Allah SWT asks, what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is??

translation.text: ˹It is˺ the Day no soul will be of ˹any˺ benefit to another whatsoever, for all authority on that Day belongs to Allah ˹entirely˺.

commentary.text: On that Day, every human being stands alone. No person—no matter how close, noble, or righteous—will have any power to benefit or protect another. Parents, children, relatives, leaders, and even Prophets cannot save their own people except those whom Allah SWT permits.
This is reinforced by the Prophet (PBUH)’s warning to his own clan: “O children of Hāshim! Save yourselves from the Fire, for I possess no power to help you against Allah.”
IT IS A REMINDER THAT LINEAGE, FAMILY TIES, STATUS, AND WORLDLY RELATIONSHIPS WILL BE OF NO VALUE WITHOUT PERSONAL RIGHTEOUSNESS.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The name of this Surah is from Ayat 1.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: A Makki Surah in content and style.

front_matter.label: Theme and subject matter
front_matter.text:
Surah al-Muṭaffifīn teaches that cheating, injustice, and moral corruption arise when people stop believing that they will one day face Allah SWT and be held accountable for every deed.

The Surah begins by condemning those who demand full rights for themselves but give less to others, using this one example to show how denial of the Hereafter destroys honesty.

It then explains that the deeds of the wicked are already being recorded in Sijjīn, a low register that leads to humiliation and punishment, while the deeds of the righteous are written in ‘Illiyyīn, a lofty record guarded by noble angels and leading to joy and honor.

In the end, the Surah comforts the believers who were mocked in Makkah, warning that the very people who ridicule them now will face disgrace on the Day of Resurrection, and the believers will be the ones rewarded and vindicated.

sections.title: 1-28 DEFRAUDERS WILL BE CALLED TO ACCOUNT AND PUNISHED WHILE THE RIGHTEOUS WILL BE REWARDED WITH SOFT COUCHES, CHOICEST WINE AND SPECIAL SPRING WATER

translation.text: Woe to the defrauders!

commentary.text: The word mutaffifīn لِّلْمُطَفِّفِينَ comes from tatfīf, which in Arabic refers to a small, sneaky form of cheating—specifically giving short weight or short measure. It means the person does not steal a large or obvious amount but deducts tiny quantities from every customer in a way that the buyer cannot detect.
This makes tatfīf one of the lowest, most disgraceful forms of fraud, because the cheater pretends to act normally while subtly depriving others of their rightful due.
Lesson: This is a powerful beginning!

translation.text: Those who take full measure ˹when they buy˺ from people,

commentary.text: These people take their right by demanding full measure and extra as well.
Also see, Surah Al-Anaam Ayat 152, Surah Bani Israil Ayat 35 and Surah Ar-Rehman Ayat 8 and 9.

translation.text: but give less when they measure or weigh for buyers.

commentary.text: When it is time for them to give to others, they cause loss to the other by very little. The cheat! This attitude is not just in business but extends to all aspects of life. The rights and responsibilities placed on a person. Even our relationship with Allah SWT.
Lesson: At several places in the Quran, giving of little measure and weight has been condemned and measuring fully and weighing rightly has been stressed.

translation.text: Do such people do not think that they will be resurrected

commentary.text: Lesson: Why do people do this small but nasty deed? Bec they do not truly believe in the DoJ.

translation.text: for a tremendous Day—

commentary.text: On the Day that is very tough and difficult. The Day that begins with a tremendous quake.

translation.text: the Day ˹all˺ people will stand before the Lord of all worlds?

commentary.text: A Day when all humanity will be standing waiting for their judgment before Allah SWT.
Lesson: Look at the connection between the Ayats. Minor crimes but big punishment because the problem or issue is deeper. We have different standard for ourselves and for others.

arabic_lines: كَلَّاۤ اِنَّ كِتٰبَ الۡفُجَّارِ لَفِىۡ سِجِّيۡ

translation.text: But no! The wicked are certainly bound for Sijjîn ˹in the depths of Hell˺—

commentary.text: This is not Ok! These people are wrong in thinking that they will be let off without being called to account when they have committed such crimes in the world. Their crimes are being recorded in the Book of Deeds.

The word SIJJIN in the original is derived from sijn (a prison) and the explanation of it that follows shows that it implies the general register in which the actions and deeds of the people worthy of punishment are being recorded.

translation.text: and what will make you realize what Sijjîn is?—

commentary.text: Sijjīn is the lowest realm where the records of the wicked are kept — a tight, dark, miserable prison beneath the seventh earth, symbolizing the humiliation and torment awaiting those who lived in arrogance and disbelief.

translation.text: It is a Book inscribed.

commentary.text: Sijjin.is a destination where deeds are recorded, inscribed, and written. No one can add nor remove anything from it.
Sijjīn and ‘Illiyyīn are two opposing registers of deeds or actions.
Sijjīn = the lowest record of the wicked.
‘Illiyyīn = the highest record of the righteous.

They illustrate how deeds are preserved in a way that reflects their moral worth and the final status of the person before Allah SWT. The Quran and Sunnah teach us that every deed—good or evil—directly affects the soul, shaping its purity, clarity, and ultimate destiny. These effects are real, cumulative, and determine whether a person becomes spiritually illuminated and at the higher plain or darkened and in the depths of Sijjin. Thus, both souls will have a huge distance between them.
So register to deeds may be our souls that the angels are taking to their final destination.

translation.text: Woe on that Day to the deniers—
those who deny Judgment Day!

commentary.text: Those who deny the Day of Judgment deny that their actions or deeds have any consequences.

translation.text: None would deny it except every evildoing transgressor.

commentary.text: The denial of the DoJ is the same as the proverb, which suggests that a pigeon closes its eyes when a cat approaches, foolishly believing that if it cannot see the cat, the cat does not exist.
This is the willful blindness or foolish self-deception of disbelievers.

translation.text: Whenever Our revelations are recited to them, they say, “Ancient fables!”

commentary.text: The disbelievers say that the Quran is nothing but stories of the past. They reject the Quran. People do that because they want to follow their own desires.

translation.text: But no! In fact, their hearts have been stained by all ˹the evil˺ they used to commit!

commentary.text: The explanation of this rust or staining of the heart as given by the Prophet (PBUH) is: When a servant commits a sin, it marks a black stain on his heart. If he offers repentance, the stain is washed off, but if he persists in wrongdoing, it spreads over the entire heart.

translation.text: Undoubtedly, they will be sealed off from their Lord on that Day.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah is named Al-Inshiqāq from the verb inshaqqat, meaning “to split open/ split asunder.” This refers to the opening scene of the Surah, where the sky is described as splitting apart on the Day of Resurrection.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: Surah Al-Inshiqāq belongs to the early Makkan period.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
Its theme is the Resurrection and Hereafter. The central objection from the Quraysh was the denial of Resurrection, accountability, and the afterlife.

The opening Ayats (1–5) vividly describe the events of Resurrection: the sky will split apart, the earth will be flattened and emptied, releasing all buried bodies and the hidden evidence of human deeds. This scene serves as a proof of the Hereafter: when Allah SWT commands, the heavens and earth — His creation — cannot disobey. Their submission itself testifies to the certainty of Resurrection.

Ayats 6–19 explain that every human being, knowingly or unknowingly, is moving toward the inevitable moment when they will stand before Allah SWT.

front_matter.label: Humanity will then divide into two groups:
front_matter.text:
Our heading toward judgment Day is portrayed as certain and natural, just like the transition from day to twilight, nightfall, creatures returning to their shelters, and the waxing of the crescent into a full moon.

The Surah concludes by a warning for those who reject the Quran and refuse to prostrate when they hear it, and by giving glad tidings of boundless reward to the believers who obey and do righteous deeds.

SAJDAH TILAWAT is performed on Ayat 21.

translation.text: So, I do swear by the twilight!

commentary.text: Also see Surah 69 Ayat 37

Allah SWT takes an oath by the twilight. Ash-Shafaq refers to the red glow that remains in the sky after sunset, lasting until the onset of complete darkness and marking the end of Maghrib time -- post-sunset redness. Thus, Allah SWT’s oath “فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالشَّفَقِ” highlights this natural transition in the sky as a sign, pointing to the certainty of human transitions and the inevitability of returning to Allah SWT.

Nothing in worldly life is fixed or lasting; everything moves through phases that pass swiftly. Three enduring phenomena are cited—signs known to humanity across all ages—yet each is only fleeting when observed closely. The first is the sun, which appears immense and permanent, even becoming an object of worship for some, yet the glow it leaves at sunset (ash-shafaq) is brief, ever-changing, and disappears with twilight. This highlights the transient nature of worldly existence and reminds the human being that true completion and permanence lie only in the Hereafter.

translation.text: And by the night and whatever it envelops!

commentary.text: Allah SWT takes an oath by the night. Night is another sign of life’s transience. Night shows how all things return home. Just as animals and people come back to rest when darkness falls, our souls too will return to their final place when this life ends.

translation.text: and by the moon, when it reaches its fullness:

commentary.text: Allah SWT takes an oath by the moon. The full moon appears complete only for a moment before it begins to wane, and when it disappears, it immediately starts a new cycle as the growing new moon. In the same way, human life is never fixed or permanent—our physical, intellectual, emotional, and spiritual states are always changing.

translation.text: You will certainly pass from one state to another.

commentary.text:
An oath has been sworn (above) by three things: 

(1) By the twilight. 

(2) By the darkness of night and the gathering together in it of all those human beings and animals who remain scattered in the daytime. 

(3) By the moon’s passing through different phases to become full. These are some of those things which testify that rest and stillness is unknown in the universe in which man lives.
There is a continuous and gradual change taking place everywhere.
Here is the response to the oath.
Human life is only a temporary stage, and because his destiny is high, man should naturally welcome Allah SWT’s guidance.

Allah SWT created human beings for a noble purpose: to know Him, worship Him, live with moral responsibility. Humans are not meant for a low or meaningless existence; their true goal is spiritual elevation and closeness to Allah SWT, which is far greater than anything in worldly life.

Allah SWT states that man will not remain in one and the same state, but will have to pass through countless stages gradually, from youth to old age, from old age to death, from death to barzakh (the intermediary state between death and Resurrection), from barzakh to Resurrection, from Resurrection to the Plain of Assembly, then to the Reckoning, and then to the meting out of rewards and punishments.
Therefore, the disbelievers are wrong in thinking that life comes to an end after man has breathed his last.
Lesson: We should not make life with its phases the purpose of our existence rather we should prepare for the Hereafter.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah takes its name from Ayat 1.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: The subject matter itself indicates that this Surah was sent down at Makkah in the period when persecution of the Muslims was at its climax and the disbelievers of Makkah were trying their utmost by tyranny and coercion to turn away the new converts from Islam.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
The Surah warns the disbelievers of Makkah about the severe consequences of persecuting the early Muslims, and it comforts the believers by assuring them that if they stay firm, Allah SWT will reward them and punish their oppressors.

It recalls the story of the People of the Ditch, who burned believers for their faith, showing that tyrants always face Allah SWT’s punishment and the steadfast always receive Paradise.

The Surah teaches that Allah SWT is in full control, sees all deeds, and will avenge the wronged. It warns the Quraysh that even powerful nations like Pharaoh and Thamud were destroyed, and that they too cannot escape Allah SWT’s power. The Quran they deny is protected and unchangeable, written in the Preserved Tablet.

commentary.text: This Ayat refers to the people who burned believers in large fire-filled ditches and watched their suffering. These people were persecuted only because they believed in Allah SWT.
So, Allah SWT swears by the sky with its constellations, by the Day of Judgment, and by all who will witness its events, to show that He will surely punish such tyrants.

History contains many examples of this crime, including famous events like the boy and the king, the Persian king who forced people into sin, and the people of Najran who were burned for refusing to give up their faith. The king, fearing the spread of true belief, tortured the monk, the courtier, and finally the boy. The boy told the king he could only be killed if the king shot an arrow saying, “In the Name of Allah, the Lord of the boy.” When the king did this, the boy died and the whole nation believed.

In anger, the king dug huge ditches of fire and burned the believers who refused to abandon their faith. This is the story behind the Ayat about the “People of the Ditch” (Ashab al-Ukhdud). History records similar events, especially in Najran, where Dhu Nuwas killed thousands of believers for refusing to give up their faith.
Allah SWT revealed these Ayats to show that the believers’ patience is honored and that the tyrants who burn the faithful will face His severe punishment.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah taken its name from the word in its first Ayat.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: The style of its subject matter resembles that of the earliest Surahs revealed at Makkah, but this surah was sent down at a stage when the disbelievers of Makkah were employing all sorts of devices and plans to defeat and frustrate the message of the Quran and Muhammad (PBUH).

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
Surah At-Tāriq affirms two central truths: (i) every human will be resurrected and held accountable before Allah SWT, and (ii) the Quran is an authoritative, undefeatable revelation.

The surah begins by invoking the night-star to show that nothing in creation exists without the watchful oversight of its Lord. It then directs man to reflect on his origin—a single drop of fluid—highlighting that the Creator who fashioned him effortlessly the first time can resurrect him again.

That resurrection will unveil all hidden intentions, and no one will possess any power to protect or rescue himself.

The surah concludes by stressing that the Quran is not a trivial message but a decisive word, and while the disbelievers devise plans to resist it, Allah SWT is preparing a superior plan that will nullify theirs. The Prophet (PBUH) is reassured to remain patient, for soon the truth will prevail and the deniers will see the outcome of their own schemes.

sections.title: 1-17 OVER EACH SOUL THERE IS AND APPOINTED GUARDIAN ANGEL AND AL-QURAN IS A DECISIVE WORD OF ALLAH SWT

translation.text: By the heaven, and the night-visitor,

commentary.text: Allah SWT swears or takes an oath by the heaven and what He has placed in it of radiant stars.

translation.text: what do you know what the night-visitor is?
˹It is˺ the star of piercing brightness.

commentary.text: The star has been named Tariq because it is only seen at night and it is hidden during the day.

arabic_lines: اِنۡ كُلُّ نَفۡسٍ لَّمَّا عَلَيۡهَا حَافِظ

translation.text: There is no living being but there is a protector over it

commentary.text: Why is this oath being taken? To say that every soul has a Guardian. Every soul has a protecting guardian angel who records every deed and watches over us.

The surah swears an oath by the sky and by every piercing star—not to highlight a single star but the entire order of the night sky. Each star, with its fixed course, light, and stability, testifies that a supreme Being created it, placed it in space, sustains its motion, and guards it from falling, drifting, or colliding despite the vast multitude of celestial bodies.
Hafiz حَافِظ the one who memorizes the Quran so protects/gurads/preserves the Quran.

translation.text: So let man consider of what he was created.

commentary.text: After calling man to reflect on the heavens, the surah directs him to examine his own creation. What a humble beginning. So why is then man so arrogant. Pride and ego are often at the root cause of man’s downfall.

These realities reveal the frailty of human origin and point clearly to a single, purposeful Creator. The message is to awaken man to the truth of resurrection: the One who begins creation with such mastery is fully able to repeat it.

translation.text: He was created of a gushing fluid,
stemming from between the backbone and the ribcage.

commentary.text: The origin of man is from the spine and ribcage.
Lesson: So, look at your origin and you are walking so proudly.

translation.text: Surely He is fully capable of bringing them back ˹to life˺

commentary.text: Allah SWT’s creating and sustaining man from conception to death proves He can create him again after death. The One who originated life can easily repeat it. Human creation is far more complex than anything people make; if someone insists it happened by chance, then they could call anything accidental.

translation.text: on the Day all secrets will be disclosed.

commentary.text: The “hidden secrets” are all deeds whose inner motives were concealed in worldly life. On the Day of Resurrection, every action will be exposed along with the intentions behind it. It will become clear: the true purpose of each act and the full chain of its effects in the world, how far those effects spread, and how long they continued to influence others for good or for harm.

translation.text: Then one will have neither power nor ˹any˺ helper.

commentary.text: On the Day of Judgement man will have no power or helper means that he will not be able to save himself from the torment of Allah SWT, and nor will anyone else be able to save him.

translation.text: By the sky with its recurring cycles,

commentary.text: Here another oath is being taken by the sky (having rain clouds) which gives rain, again and again.

The words dhat ar-raje have been used for the sky. Literally raje means to return, but metaphorically this word is used for rain in Arabic, for rain does not fall just once, but returns over and over again in the season and sometimes out of season as well. Another reason for calling the rain raje is that water rises as vapor from the oceans of the earth and then falls back as rain on the same earth.

translation.text: and the earth with its sprouting plants!

commentary.text: And then the earth splits open to bring forth plant growths. Rain brings out vegetation from the earth.

translation.text: Surely this ˹Quran˺ is a decisive word,

commentary.text: This is the Word that separates فَصۡلٌۙ (falsehood from truth or Haq). Quran makes a person humble/productive like rain helps bring out vegetation from the ground but first the ground must be soft and clear/cleans out the soil. Similarly, hearts become soft with the Quran and then make us useful.

translation.text: and is not to be taken lightly.

commentary.text: The Quran is not a thing for amusement or fun rather it is serious and true!

translation.text: They are certainly devising ˹evil˺ plans,

commentary.text: Then Allah SWT informs us about the disbelievers saying that they reject Him and hinder others from His path. Allah SWT says they are but plotting a plot meaning they plot to oppose the Quran.

translation.text: but I too am planning.

commentary.text: Allah SWT says, “but I too am planning.” That is, these disbelievers are devising every kind of plan to defeat the invitation of the Quran; they are creating all sorts of doubts in the people’s minds; they are inventing false accusations against the Prophet (PBUH).

translation.text: So bear with the disbelievers ˹O Prophet˺. Let them be for ˹just˺ a little while.

commentary.text: So be patient with them for a short time and do not rush. Soon they will see the punishment and destruction that awaits them. Maybe they will repent and turn back to Allah SWT.
As Allah SWT says elsewhere: “We let them enjoy for a little while, then We drive them into a severe torment.” (31:24)

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The surah is named Al-A‘lā after the word in its opening Ayat.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text:
The content and tone show that this surah belongs to the very early Makkan revelations.

Ayat 6 — ‘We will have you recite ˹the Quran, O Prophet,˺ so you will not forget ˹any of it˺ — indicates a phase when the Prophet (PBUH) was still becoming accustomed to receiving revelation and feared forgetting its wording. When this Ayat is considered alongside Surah Al-Qiyāmah (75:16–19) and Surah Ṭā Hā (20:114), a clear sequence emerges:

After these occasions, the Prophet (PBUH) never felt this concern again, and the Quran contains no further reference to such fear.

items.text: In Surah Al-A‘lā: Allah SWT reassures the Prophet (PBUH) that He will firmly preserve the revelation in his memory, and he will not forget it.

Later, during the revelation of Surah Al-Qiyāmah: When the Prophet (PBUH) began moving his tongue quickly to retain the Ayats, Allah SWT instructed him not to hasten, for preserving and explaining the Quran is Allah’s responsibility.

Finally, during the revelation of Surah Ṭā Hā: The Prophet (PBUH) again feared missing part of the long, continuous revelation, so he began memorizing as it came down. Allah SWT instructed him not to rush before the revelation was completed.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
The surah presents three themes: Tawḥīd, Guidance to the Prophet (PBUH), and the Hereafter.

It’s a pair with the next Surah. Was recited by the Prophet (PBUH) on Friday and Eid prayers as a khutba.

items.text: Tawḥīd: Allah SWT’s name must be exalted and described only with attributes befitting His perfection. He alone created, proportioned, decreed, and guided every created thing, and He alone brings forth vegetation and reduces it to decay—signs of His exclusive power.

Guidance to the Prophet (PBUH): The Prophet (PBUH) is assured that Allah SWT will preserve the Quran in his memory, and he need not fear forgetting it. His task is to convey the message, not to compel acceptance. Those who fear Allah SWT will respond; those who turn away will face the consequences.

The Hereafter: Success belongs to those who purify themselves, remember their Lord, and pray. Most people prefer the fleeting world, though the Hereafter is everlasting and far superior—a truth affirmed in the scriptures of Ibrahim and Musa.

sections.title: 1-19 GLORIFY ALLAH, AL-QURAN WILL REMAIN AS IS, THOSE WHO HEED ITS REMINDERS WILL BE SUCCESSFUL IN THE HEREAFTER

translation.text: Glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most High,

commentary.text: “Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High” carries multiple included meanings:

Use only names befitting Allah SWT:
He must be remembered with names that reflect His perfection and majesty, free from any deficiency, error, or resemblance to creation. The safest approach is to use the names He Himself revealed.

Mention Allah SWT with full respect:
His name should not be spoken in contexts that involve mockery, sin, disrespect, or annoyance.
Also see: Surah Hashr Ayat 24
هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْخَـٰلِقُ ٱلْبَارِئُ ٱلْمُصَوِّرُ ۖ لَهُ ٱلْأَسْمَآءُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ ۚ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۖ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
He is Allah: the Creator, the Inventor, the Shaper. He ˹alone˺ has the Most Beautiful Names. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth ˹constantly˺ glorifies Him. And He is the Almighty, All-Wise.
Lesson: We cannot imagine our Raab except by His names. This Ayat provides us the foundation or structure.
Subhaan Allahah hi wa bi hamdi – Do this tasbeeh often.

translation.text: Who created and ˹perfectly˺ fashioned ˹all˺,

commentary.text: He created everything, from the earth to the heavens, and gave whatever he created the right proportion and balance and limitations. And each person is given a unique Shakilah -- as discussed earlier – which will determine their test parameters. Therefore, Allah SWT does not test anyone beyond their capacity or limitations, for example a mentally handicapped person’s test will be different from a person with a high IQ.
Also see Surah Bakarah Ayat 286
Allah does not require of any soul more than what it can afford…
Surah As-Sajdah Ayat 7.

translation.text: And who destined and [then] guided

commentary.text: Allah SWT first determined every created thing destiny (taqdīr): its form, lifespan, and role. Nothing in creation is random; everything operates according to a deliberate, pre-ordained plan.
He then guided every created being according to its function. This guidance manifests in multiple layers:
Cosmic guidance: the sun, moon, earth, and celestial bodies follow precise laws.
Elemental guidance: water, air, and minerals perform their appointed roles.
Biological guidance: plants grow, feed, blossom, and bear fruit exactly as designed.
Animal guidance: each species acts with innate instincts that enable survival and reproduction.
Human guidance: Unconscious/instinctive guidance: bodily systems (breathing, digestion, senses, growth) operate without choice.
Conscious/moral guidance: humans are given reason, will, and revelation to choose right from wrong; guidance is therefore provided in a form suitable to this freedom.
The Ayat thus emphasizes that Allah SWT is not only the Creator but also the Guide, providing every creation with the precise direction it requires to fulfill its purpose.

translation.text: and Who brings forth ˹green˺ pasture,

commentary.text: Allah SWT brings out from the ground all types of green fresh vegetation and crops.

translation.text: and then made it into a blackish straw.

commentary.text: Not only does Allah SWT bring about spring but autumn as well.

On the one hand, He causes lush green vegetation to grow, the freshness of which pleases the hearts and, on the other, He renders the same vegetation pale, dry and black rubbish, which is blown about by winds and swept away by floods.
Also see Surah Younus, Ayat 24, Surah Al-Kahf, Ayat 45, Surah Al-Hadid, Ayat 20.
Lesson: There is a beginning, a middle and an end.

translation.text: We will have you recite ˹the Quran, O Prophet,˺ so you will not forget ˹any of it˺,

commentary.text: This is Allah SWT informing and promising him (the Prophet) that He will teach him a recitation that he will not forget.

Background: The Prophet (PBUH) repeated the words of the Quran for fear that he should forget them. Even before Gabriel finished recitation of the revelation the Prophet (PBUH) would start repeating the initial Ayats lest he should forget them.
On this very basis Allah SWT assured him that he should listen quietly when the revelation was coming down.
This is the third occasion where the Prophet (PBUH) has been taught the method of receiving the revelation.
The first two occasions have been referred to in Surah TaHa, Ayat 114 and Surah Al-Qiyamah, Ayats 16-19.

This Ayat proves that just as the Quran was sent down to the Prophet (PBUH) as a miracle, so also its each word was preserved in his memory as a miracle and no possibility was allowed to remain that he should forget anything of it, or that he should utter another synonymous word for any word of it.
Lesson: Allah SWT reminds us of our weakness and then we are told to rely on Alah SWT only. Review the Quran often to retain it.

translation.text: unless Allah wills otherwise. He surely knows what is open and what is hidden.

commentary.text: Everything happens by the will of Allah SWT. If Allah SWT wills He can make the Prophet (PBUH) forget the abrogated Ayats.

translation.text: We will facilitate for you the Way of Ease

commentary.text: There are many interpretations of this Ayat. Meaning, `We will make good deeds and statements easy for you, and We will legislate such Law for you that is easy, tolerant, straight and just, with no crookedness, difficulty or hardship in it.
This topic will open up again later on.
Lesson: Make dua and Allah SWT will make ease, in sha Allah.

translation.text: So ˹always˺ remind ˹with the Quran˺—˹even˺ if the reminder is beneficial ˹only to some˺.

commentary.text: Allah SWT instructs the Prophet (PBUH) that his mission is meant to be easy, not burdensome. Allah SWT does not require him to force guidance upon those who are spiritually deaf or unwilling. Instead, he should give general admonition to all and then focus his serious effort on those who show openness and readiness to benefit.

translation.text: Those in awe ˹of Allah˺ will be mindful ˹of it˺.

commentary.text: Those who benefit from the Quran are the ones whose heart fears and loves Allah SWT and who knows that they are going to meet Allah SWT.

translation.text: But it will be shunned by the most wretched,

commentary.text: Those who avoid or keep away from the Quran are the unlucky or wretched ones.

translation.text: who will burn in the greatest Fire,
where they will not ˹be able to˺ live or die.

commentary.text: That is, he will neither die to escape the punishment nor live as one truly lives to enjoy the pleasures of life. This punishment is for those who persist in disbelief, polytheism and atheism till death. There will be no relief in Hell.

As for those who believe in their hearts but are cast into Hell because of their evil deeds, it has been said in the Hadith that when they will have undergone their punishment, Allah SWT will give them death; then intercession on their behalf will be accepted, and their scorched bodies will be brought to the canals of Paradise, and the dwellers of Paradise will be asked to sprinkle water on them; then by that water they will come to life even as vegetation grows up when water is sprinkled on the earth. (Dr Israr).

translation.text: Successful indeed are those who purify themselves,

commentary.text: The Ayat describes true success, which is not measured by worldly gain but by inner purification and obedience. Even if worldly prosperity accompanies it—or does not—real success lies in the moral and spiritual cleansing that leads a person toward Allah SWT.
Like rain purifies and enriches the earth.  Makes a person soft hearted and productive. تَزَكّٰ is from zakat that purifies ones wealth.

translation.text: remember the Name of their Lord, and pray.

commentary.text: A believer who goes beyond inner purification and expresses his faith through active actions of obedience. Thus, remembrance of Allah SWT includes both inward remembrance (awareness of Allah SWT in the heart) and outward remembrance (mentioning His Name by the tongue).

Establishing Prayer
The person proves the sincerity of his remembrance by performing Ṣalāh consistently at its proper times, seeking Allah SWT’s pleasure and submitting to His command.
Establishing Zikr of Allah SWT
TRUE SUCCESS = PURIFICTION + ZIKR + SALAH

FYI - Giving Charity
Early scholars (such as ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and Qatādah) linked this Ayat with both inner purification and purifying one’s wealth—such as by giving Zakāh or Sadaqat al-Fiṭr—before standing in prayer.
Purification of the soul and purification of wealth together prepare the heart for sincere worship. Control your fitra.

translation.text: But you ˹deniers only˺ prefer the life of this world

commentary.text: The main reason for deniers to deny or reject is because they give precedence to this world over the matter of the Hereafter. Their preference is their lowly, immediate desires, livelihood, fun, families etc.

translation.text: even though the Hereafter is far better and more lasting.

commentary.text:
This worldly life is lowly and temporal, whereas the Hereafter is superior, noble and eternal. Thus, how can an intelligent person prefer that which is short-lived over that which is eternal. 

HADITH: WHOEVER LOVES HIS WORLDLY LIFE, WILL SUFFER IN HIS HEREAFTER, AND WHOEVER LOVES HIS HEREAFTER, WILL SUFFER IN HIS WORLDLY LIFE. THEREFORE, CHOSE THAT WHICH IS EVERLASTING OVER THAT WHICH IS TEMPORAL.

translation.text: This is certainly ˹mentioned˺ in the earlier Scriptures—

commentary.text: The Scriptures of Ibrāhīm and Mūsā” affirms that the core teachings just mentioned in this surah—(i) purification of the soul, (ii) remembrance of Allah SWT, (iii) establishing prayer, (iv) avoiding attachment to the worldly life, and (v) recognizing the greater permanence of the Hereafter—are not new.
They were already revealed in the ancient scriptures given to Prophet Ibrāhīm and Prophet Mūsā (PBU them).

Ibn Kathīr links this to the similar passage in Sūrat an-Najm (53:36–42), which outlines the same principles: no soul bears the burden of another, each person receives only what he strives for, deeds will be shown and recompensed fully, and all return is to Allah SWT.
Thus, the sūrah concludes by emphasizing the continuity of divine guidance across all prophetic scriptures.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: Sūrat al-Ghāshiyah is named after the word “al-ghāshiyah” in its opening Ayat.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: Its subject matter clearly indicates an early Makkan revelation, during the stage when the Prophet (PBUH) had begun public preaching, and the Quraysh were hearing the message but responding with indifference.

front_matter.label: Theme and subject matter
front_matter.text:
The Surah focuses on the two truths the Prophet (PBUH)’s emphasized most in the early Makkan period: (i) Tawḥīd (the Oneness of Allah SWT) and (ii) the Hereafter, both of which the people of Makkah were denying.

Description of the Day of Overwhelming Calamity
The Surah vividly describes how humanity will be divided into two groups:

One group punished in Hell, enduring humiliation and torment.

The other group honored in an elevated Paradise with abundant blessings.

Rational Appeal to Tawḥīd
The Surah then shifts to a reflective, rational argument. The people are asked to ponder the signs they witness daily:

The camel, perfectly created for desert life.

The sky raised above.

The mountains, firmly set.

The earth, spread out for habitation.
These are reminders that creation is purposeful, guided by the wisdom and power of the One Creator. If they accept this Creator, why reject His sole Lordship, or deny His ability to resurrect and judge?

Instruction to the Prophet (PBUH)
Finally, the address turns to the Prophet (PBUH): his duty is to preach and remind, not to force belief. Their return is to Allah SWT, Who will judge them fully and punish those who persist in disbelief.

This summarizes the Surah’s message: awakening the heedless, affirming Tawḥīd, proving the Resurrection through reason, and clarifying the Prophet’s role as a warner—not a controller—over people.

sections.title: 1-16 WHAT WILL BE THE CONDITION OF THE DISBELIEVERS AND THE BELIEVERS ON THE DAY OF JUDGEMENT

translation.text: Has the news of the Overwhelming Event reached you ˹O Prophet˺?

commentary.text: Al-Ghashiyah is one of the names of the Day of Judgement. Al-Ghashiyah (the overwhelming), It has been called this because it will overwhelm the people and overcome them. Ghashiyah means covering that takes over an object. The DoJ will take over and envelop everything that day.

translation.text: Some faces that Day shall be downcast with fear,

commentary.text: The face is the most conspicuous part of the human body that reflects a person’s state of mind whether good or bad. Some faces will be humiliated and overcome with fear.

translation.text: ˹totally˺ overburdened, exhausted,

commentary.text: They will be cast into a blazing Fire on the Day of Judgement despite their toil and exhaustive work in life.

translation.text: burning in a scorching Fire,

commentary.text: These faces will burn in the scorching fire.

translation.text: left to drink from a scalding spring.

commentary.text: Only boiling water to drink.

translation.text: They will have no food except a foul, thorny shrub,

commentary.text: The only food available will be thorns that are bitter, smelly and state. No longer fresh. Some say it is dead seaweed that smells horrible.

translation.text: neither nourishing nor satisfying hunger.

commentary.text: The people of Hell will always be hungry and thirsty so due to the extreme hunger and thirst they will eat and drink anything. Yet nothing gives them relief or satisfaction.
Lesson: Those who do not fill their bellies in this world will have amazing food in Heaven. But those who indulge in this world will suffer hunger in the Next.

translation.text: On that Day ˹other˺ faces will be glowing with bliss,
fully˺ pleased with their striving,

commentary.text: They will be overjoyed to see their striving, saee and hard work in the world has paid off. They adopted a life of faith, virtue and piety, by sacrificing the desires of the flesh, incurred losses and suffered deprivation at times while trying to avoid sins and acts of disobedience.
But Allah SWT is very appreciative. Heaven is the repayment in full.

translation.text: in an elevated Garden,

commentary.text: Heaven is high. Elevated.

translation.text: where no idle talk will be heard.

commentary.text: This has been mentioned several places in the Quran as a major blessing of Paradise. (See Below) لَاغِيَةً or idle /useless talk. No extra or loud noises will be heard in Heaven a complete opposite of Hell.
FYI – People of Heaven in this world too avoid and do not like useless/idle talk. No arguments, no chaos, no fasad. Only tasbeeh.
They shall not hear therein any Laghw, لَاغِيَةً but only Salam. (19:62)
Free from any Laghw, and free from sin. (52:23)
No Laghw will they hear therein, nor any sinful speech. But only the saying of:"Salam! Salam!" (56:25-26)
Also see Surah Maryam Ayat 38, Surah At-Toor Ayat 18, Surah Al-Waqiah Ayat 13 and Surah An Naba Ayat 21.

translation.text: In it will be a running spring,
and couches raised high,
and goblets laid out,
and ˹fine˺ cushions lined up,
and ˹splendid˺ carpets spread out.

commentary.text: FYI – Keep in mind that the names of things are the same here on earth that are mentioned in Heaven but in Heaven we cannot even imagine what is awaiting us in sha Allah.

translation.text: Do they not ever reflect on camels—how they were ˹masterfully˺ created;

commentary.text:
After mentioning Heaven, we are directed to Look and Reflect at the Creation of the Camel, the Heaven, the Mountains and the Earth. If all this is possible on earth then the DoJ and Heaven is very possible as well. 

The camel is an amazing creation, and the way it has been fashioned is strange. For it is extremely powerful and strong, yet gentle, carrying heavy loads. It allows itself to be guided by a weak rider. It is eaten, and its milk is drunk. They are reminded of this because the most common domestic animal of the Arabs was the camel.
Believer is like a submissive camel that is goes where it is lead.

translation.text: and the sky—how it was raised ˹high˺;

commentary.text: How has Allah SWT raised it in such magnificence above the ground.

translation.text: and the mountains—how they were firmly set up;

commentary.text: Reflect on how the mountains have been firmly affixed so that the earth does not sway with its dwellers. And He made them with the benefits and minerals.

translation.text: and the earth—how it was levelled out?

commentary.text: When Allah SWT says, “And the earth—how it was levelled out?” He calls people to reflect thoughtfully on the world beneath their feet: how the earth has been extended, leveled, and made suitable for life, travel, agriculture, and habitation. Together with the camel perfectly adapted for desert life, the sky raised above with its atmosphere, sun, moon, and clouds, and the mountains set firm with diverse structures and minerals, these signs prove the presence of an All-Powerful, All-Wise Designer.
Only a stubborn mind denies that the One who created the first creation can recreate it again and bring about the Resurrection.
Thus, the Ayat teaches that observing creation leads to recognizing the Creator, affirming the Prophet’s message, and committing to the essential acts of faith that secure salvation.

Lesson: Look around more than just mere animals rather reflect and think about creation and the signs of Allah SWT to gain closeness to our Raab in sha Allah. GAIN MASTERY OVER THE THINGS THAT ALLAH SWT HAS MADE SUBSERVIENT TO HIS GREATEST CREATION.

translation.text: So, ˹continue to˺ remind ˹all, O Prophet˺, for your duty is only to remind.
You are not ˹there˺ to compel them ˹to believe˺.

commentary.text: These Ayats mean that the Prophet (PBUH)’s duty is only to remind people of the truth Allah SWT sent him. His role is to convey the message clearly, while guidance and judgment belong only to Allah SWT. There is no compulsion in religion.
Prophet’s mission is to deliver the message, not to force belief.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah is name is from Ayat 1.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: Its contents show that it was revealed at the stage when persecution of the new converts to Islam had begun in Makkah. On that very basis the people of Makkah have been warned of the evil end of the tribes of Ad and Thamud and of Pharaoh.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
The Surah focuses on proving the reality of the Hereafter, which the Quraysh denied. It begins by swearing oaths by the dawn, the ten nights, the even and the odd, and the departing night—signs of the perfect order Allah SWT placed in creation.

This regular system shows that the One who controls night and day has full power to bring about the Resurrection and to hold people accountable. The Surah then reminds the listeners of past nations—ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Pharaoh—whose arrogance and corruption led to their destruction.

This proves that the world is governed by a Wise and Just Lord, not blind forces, and that moral accountability is part of His system. The Surah next critiques the moral decay of society: people judged honor and disgrace only by wealth, forgetting that both wealth and poverty are tests from Allah SWT; they neglected orphans, oppressed the weak, and hoarded wealth without limit. This exposes why such societies must be held accountable.

The Surah ends by affirming that the Day of Judgment will certainly come: the disbeliever will regret failing to prepare, but regret will be useless then. Meanwhile, the believers who accepted the truth with a content heart will be welcomed with Allah’s pleasure and admitted among the righteous into Paradise.

sections.title: 1-14 ADMONITION FOR SOCIAL WELFARE THROUGH THE EXAMPLES OF PRIOR NATIONS

translation.text: By the dawn,

commentary.text: Allah SWT Swears by the dawn or early morning. Al-Fajr refers to the day of Sacrifice (An-Nahr) in particular.
It is darkest before dawn.
Fajr is a time of worship esp. the recitation of the Quran. New beginning of a new day. What we do at Fajr affects our whole day.

translation.text: and the ten nights,

commentary.text: Allah SWT Swears by the ten nights refers to the (first) ten days of Dhul-Hijjah or last ten nights of ramadan. The Prophet (PBUH) said, there are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to Allah SWT than these days meaning the ten days of Dhul-Hijjah. Or it can mean the last ten nights including Layla tu Qadr night of ramdan.

translation.text: and the even and the odd,

commentary.text: Allah SWT Swears by the even and the odd. Complimentary and opposites. Months are at times even and odd i.e., 29 or 30 days.

translation.text: and the night when it passes!

commentary.text: Allah SWT Swears by the departing night.
For all these oath times are being mentioned. Time is slipping away. Similarly, our time in this world is also slipping away. Soon it will be time to depart.
Lesson: What r you doing with these times? FYI - Fajr and Isha is also a time of worship.

translation.text: Is all this ˹not˺ a sufficient oath for those who have sense?

commentary.text: Allah SWT asks whether these oaths —(i) by the dawn, (ii) the ten nights, (iii) the even and the odd, and (iv) the departing night—are not powerful enough evidence for a thinking mind.

These signs show a perfectly regulated system: light emerging from darkness, the moon waxing and waning through the ten nights, days progressing in even and odd numbers, and night steadily giving way to morning.

All of this reflects the power, precision, and wisdom of a deliberate Creator. In the context of the Surah, these oaths support the Prophet (PBUH)’s message about the Hereafter, which the disbelievers were rejecting. Anyone with true understanding can see that the One who governs the universe with such flawless order is fully capable of resurrecting mankind and judging them.

translation.text: Did you not see how your Lord dealt with ’Ȃd—

commentary.text: The people of Ad did not make good use of their time. They wasted their time being rebellious, disobedient, arrogant, deniers of Allah SWT, His Messengers and rejectors of His Scriptures. Thus, Allah SWT mentions how He destroyed them, annihilated them and made them legends to be spoken of and an exemplary lesson of warning.

translation.text: ˹the people˺ of Iram—with ˹their˺ great stature,

commentary.text: Allah SWT destroyed the powerful Aad people descendants of Aad son of Iram—who rejected Prophet Hūd (PBUH). Allah SWT blessed them with great physical strength and power.  But instead of obedience and gratitude they became arrogant, boasting that none was stronger than them.
Allah SWT sent their way a fierce wind that raged for seven nights and eight days, leaving their bodies like hollow date-palm trunks, with no trace of them remaining.
Their destruction stands as a clear lesson and warning.

translation.text: the like of whom no nation was ever created in the lands of the world?

commentary.text: That is, they were a matchless people of their time; no other nation in the world compares with them in strength, glory and grandeur.

translation.text: and Thamûd who carved ˹their homes into˺ the rocks in the ˹Stone˺ Valley;

commentary.text: And Thamud, who they cut the rocks in the valley to make homes. Wadi ul Qura south of Madian.
FYI:  On the Tabuk expedition, the Prophet (PBUH) passed the ruins of the punished people of Thamud in Wadi ul Qura south of Madian he instructed the army:
do not enter except weeping
do not drink from their wells (except one permitted well)
move on quickly

translation.text: and the Pharaoh of mighty structures?

commentary.text: Pharon’s great military power and the vast number of his armies, whose tent-pegs filled every place they camped; or the stakes used to torture people; or even the pyramids, towering monuments that stand fixed in the earth like enormous stakes. All meanings highlight Pharaoh’s strength and dominance—and how none of it saved him from Allah SWT’s punishment.

translation.text: They all transgressed throughout the land,

commentary.text: Allah SWT tells us about three mighty nations that transgressed. They misused their power and authority given to them by Allah SWT.

translation.text: spreading much corruption there.

commentary.text: THIS IS THE MAIN ISSUE.
They all rebelled, were arrogant, and went about making corruption in the land, and harming the people.

translation.text: So your Lord unleashed on them a scourge of punishment.
Truly your Lord is ever watchful.

commentary.text: He watches over His creation in that which they do, and He will reward them in this life and in the Hereafter based upon what each of them strove for. He will bring all of the creation before Him and He will judge them with justice. He will requite each with that which he deserves, for He is far removed from injustice and tyranny.
Lesson: We have limited time! As established in the first few Ayats.

sections.title: 15-20 WHAT SHOULD BE AVOIDED TO DO REAL SOCIAL WELFARE

translation.text: Now, whenever a human being is tested by their Lord through ˹His˺ generosity and blessings, they boast, My Lord has ˹deservedly˺ honoured me!

commentary.text: One kind of test. Nature of man is that when Allah SWT tests him with abundance, health, status etc., man’s response is that Allah SWT has honored me. But remember that these blessings are a test. If people remain steadfast and grateful Alla SWT pours more blessings.
Allah SWT tests man with good and evil – end of Surah Jinn.

translation.text: But when He tests them by limiting their provision, they protest, “My Lord has ˹undeservedly˺ humiliated me!”

commentary.text: Another kind of test is when Allah SWT constricts provision and then some men say Allah SWT has humiliated me. Allah SWT gives wealth to those whom He loves as well as those whom He does not love. Likewise, He withholds/constricts sustenance from those whom He loves and those whom He does not love.
THE POINT IS THAT ALLAH SWT SHOULD BE OBEYED IN EITHER CIRCUMSTANCE. If one is wealthy, he should thank Allah SWT for that, and if he is poor, he should exercise patience.
WEALTH AND POVERTY ARE BOTH TEST. Neither is a criterion for honor or disgrace by Allah SWT.
Our response is being witnessed.
LESSON: WEALTH AND CHILDREN MIGHT BE THE BIGGER BURDEN OR TEST BECAUSE WE TEND TO FORGET ALLAH SWT IN EASE.

translation.text: But no; you do not treat the orphan honourably,

commentary.text: This is a negation of people’s misconception that honor is with things rather it is with taqwa and how you treat the orphans, needy and those without support.

As long as his father is alive, your treatment of him is attentive and when his father dies, even the paternal and maternal uncles and the elder brothers, to say nothing of the neighbors and distant relatives, neglect him.

translation.text: and do not urge one another to feed the poor,

commentary.text: Neither a man himself feels inclined to feed a hungry person, nor is there among the people any urge to do something to satisfy the hunger of the hungry, nor do they exhort one another to do so.

translation.text: And you devour ˹others’˺ inheritance greedily,

commentary.text: And you devour the inheritance with greed, however they can get it, whether lawful or forbidden.
Lesson: Advocacy and caring for the needy and vulnerable.

translation.text: and love wealth fervently.

commentary.text:
And you love wealth with love Jamma meaning, in abundance.
This increases some of them in their wickedness. That is, you have no regard for the permissible or the forbidden, the lawful or the unlawful. You feel no qualms about acquiring wealth in any way or by any means, fair or foul, and your greed is never satisfied however much you may have acquired and amassed.
All the above are extreme selfishness.
Lesson: Reflect on what your idea of honor is compared to what Allah SWT says.

commentary.text: When the earth is flattened, Dakkan Dakka meaning, the earth and the mountains will be flattened, leveled and made even, and the creatures will rise from their graves for their Lord.

That is, you are wrong in thinking that you may do whatever you like in your life of the world, but you will never be called to account for it. The meting out of rewards and punishment will certainly come to pass at the time being mentioned below.

translation.text: and Hell is brought forth on that Day—this is when every ˹disbelieving˺ person will remember ˹their own sins˺. But what is the use of remembering then?

Hell will be brought on near that Day and it will have seventy thousand leashes, and each leash will have seventy thousand angels pulling it.
On that Day man will remember whatever he had done in the world and will regret, but what will remembrance and regretting avail him then.

translation.text: They will cry, “I wish I had sent forth ˹something good˺ for my ˹true˺ life.”

commentary.text: And if he was a disobedient person, he will be sorry for the acts of disobedience he committed. If he was an obedient person, he will wish that he performed more acts of obedience.

Remember life is a test. Time on earth is finite. 

This is similar to what Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal recorded from Muhammad bin Abi `Amirah, who was one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, He said,
"If a servant fell down on his face (in prostration) from the day that he was born until the day he died as an old man, in obedience to Allah, he would scorn this act on the Day of Judgement. He would wish to be returned to this life so that he could earn more reward and compensation."
