commentary.text: For some there will be a beautiful message on the DoJ. Peaceful and fully satisfied soul: The man who believed in Allah SWT, and adopted the way of life brought by the Prophets, who withheld himself from whatever he was forbidden by Allah SWT’s religion, not unwillingly but with perfect conviction, who endured with full peace of mind whatever difficulties, troubles and hardships he met on this way and remained fully satisfied with Allah SWT’s decree.

The righteous enter into their inheritance and receive their welcome with a title that suggests freedom from all pain, sorrow, doubt, struggle, disappointment, passion, and even further desire: at rest, in peace; in a state of complete satisfaction. In Muslim theology, this stage of the soul is the final stage of bliss.

Reactions to things we don’t like is calm and peaceful.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah has been so named after the word in the first Ayat.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: Its subject matter and style resemble those of the earliest Surahs revealed at Makkah.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
This Surah presents a complete moral worldview in remarkably concise form, AFFIRMING THAT HUMAN LIFE IN THIS WORLD IS DEFINED BY STRUGGLE AND PURPOSEFUL EFFORT, NOT EASE, AND THAT MAN’S ULTIMATE OUTCOME DEPENDS SOLELY ON WHAT HE STRIVES FOR.

Allah SWT reminds man that he has been endowed with intellect and shown both the paths of virtue and vice: one downward and easy, driven by desire, the other upward and steep, requiring discipline. The steep path consists of sincere charity, aiding the vulnerable, faith in Allah SWT, moral perseverance, and compassion—actions that lead to His mercy. Those who reject this path and choose moral decline are warned of an inescapable punishment in Hell.

sections.title: 1-20 ADMONITION TO THE DISBELIEVERS OF MAKKAH AND ALLAH HAS GIVEN YOU ONE TONGUE AND TWO LIPS TO HOLD IT AND QUALITIES OF RIGHTEOUS PERSON

translation.text: I do swear by this city ˹of Mecca˺

commentary.text: Here Allah SWT swears by sanctity Makkah, the Mother of the Towns. It is the most blessed of all lands.

translation.text: even though you ˹O Prophet˺ are subject to abuse in this city

commentary.text: Although Makkah has been sacred and inviolable since the creation of the heavens and the earth, Allah SWT granted the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) a unique, temporary permission to fight within it during the Conquest of Makkah.

translation.text: and I swear by the parent and his offspring

commentary.text: Father could only imply Adam (PBUH) and children the human beings who existed in the world, exist today and will exist in the future.
Or by every father who raises his children.

translation.text: Indeed, We have created humankind in ˹constant˺ struggle.

commentary.text: This is the conclusion of the oaths. Very profound! This teaches us that human life is inherently built on struggle and pure hardship. No one lives free of effort, danger, or trial. Whether wealthy or powerful, every person faces constant challenges, proving that Allah SWT created man to strive/struggle rather than live in ease. Noone is free to challenges or struggles.
Lesson:  At every stage of life there is struggle/toil. Life is not fun. Even in obedience there is hardship.

translation.text: Do they think that no one has power over them,

commentary.text: This Ayat challenges man’s false sense of autonomy. Despite living in constant vulnerability, he imagines he is free to act without accountability. Yet even in this world he repeatedly witnesses how powerless he is before Allah SWT’s decrees: natural disasters, accidents, sudden loss of strength, and the downfall of powerful rulers and nations all show that human control is fragile.
Lesson: These slogans and thinking of my body, my freedom etc. are not good.

translation.text: boasting, “I have wasted enormous wealth!”?

commentary.text: The Ayat exposes a boastful person who wastes vast wealth purely for show and pride. His extravagance—lavish feasts, public displays, and wasteful spending to impress others.

translation.text: Do they think that no one sees them?

commentary.text: Allah SWT knows how man obtains wealth, and why he spends it, that is, with what intention, motive, and purpose he does all this?

translation.text: Have We not given them two eyes,

commentary.text: Meaning, for him to see with them.

translation.text: a tongue, and two lips;
and shown them the two ways ˹of right and wrong˺?

commentary.text: After giving man intellect and the ability to reason, Allah SWT did not leave him unguided; Allah SWT clearly showed man the two paths—the way of good and the way of evil. Man is fully capable of recognizing both, and he is responsible for choosing his direction.

translation.text: If only they had attempted the challenging path ˹of goodness instead˺!

commentary.text: Man avoided the steep, uphill path of moral effort and boldly embarks on the way of ease. Allah SWT showed him two ways: one difficult but leading to spiritual height, requiring discipline and resistance to desire; the other easy and downhill, requiring no effort and leading to moral ruin.
Instead of choosing the demanding path of goodness and salvation, man chose the effortless descent.

translation.text: And what will make you realize what ˹attempting˺ the challenging path is?

commentary.text: The difficult path of virtue is defined as the path of charity or unselfish love, and three specific instances are given below for our understanding.
THE “STEEP PATH” IS EXPLAINED AS CONCRETE ACTS OF COMPASSION AND SACRIFICE.

translation.text: It is to free a slave;

commentary.text: Freeing a slave meaning all kinds of slavery that now exists in modern society. There is the slavery of conventions, of ignorance, and of superstition. There is slavery to wealth or passions or power. The good man tries to liberate men and women from all kinds of slavery, often at great danger to himself. But he begins by first liberating himself.

translation.text: or to give food in times of famine

commentary.text: Feeding others in times of hunger is also highlighted as a core expression of this difficult but noble path.

translation.text: to an orphan near of kin;

commentary.text: All orphans should be fed and helped. But orphans related to us have a special claim on us. They should be near and dear to us, and if charity begins at home, they have the first claim on us.
Hadith: Charity given to the poor person is counted as one charity, while if it is given to a relative it is counted as two because it is charity couple with connecting the ties (of kinship).

translation.text: or to a poor person in distress;

commentary.text: Feeding a needy/deprived person, meaning someone in extreme poverty with no support. This contrasts with wasteful, reputation-seeking spending: true moral elevation comes from helping the most vulnerable—freeing slaves, relieving debtors, feeding orphan relatives, and supporting the utterly helpless.

These acts require sacrifice, not showmanship, and therefore form the steep, uphill path of spiritual growth. The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) strongly praised these deeds: freeing a slave brings protection from Hell; supporting widows and the needy equals the reward of jihad, constant prayer, and continuous fasting; and caring for orphans earns closeness to him in Paradise.

commentary.text: (i) The Ayat teaches that righteous deeds must be joined with faith/Iman, because no act has value before Allah SWT without belief.

It also stresses that a believer should not remain isolated but must join the community of believers to help build a moral, compassionate society. Such a society has two key qualities:(ii) its members encourage one another to steadfastness, since the path of faith requires constant patience in worship, obedience, resisting desires, and facing social pressure; and (iii) they encourage one another to mercy, showing kindness to all and mutual support among themselves.
Lesson: Also discussed in Surah Hadid. Once you remove the love of wealth from your heart then things will flow.

extras.text: 1-10 SUCCESS DEPENDS ON KEEPING THE SOUL PURE AND FAILURE DEPENDS ON CORRUPTING IT
11-15 PEOPLE OF THAMUD WHO CORRUPTED, WERE LEVELLED TO THE GROUND

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah title comes from Ayat 1.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: The subject matter and the style show that this Surah too was revealed in the earliest period at Makkah at a stage when opposition to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) had grown very strong and intense.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
Its theme is to distinguish the good from the evil and to warn the people, who were refusing to understand this distinction and insisting on following the evil way, of the evil end.

The first part (1–10) uses contrasting cosmic elements—sun and moon, day and night, sky and earth—to illustrate that moral opposites, taqwā and fujūr, likewise differ completely in nature and outcome. Allah SWT has endowed the human being with bodily and mental faculties and has placed within the soul an innate moral intuition that recognizes right and wrong. A person’s destiny depends on whether he nurtures the soul’s inclination toward good or suppresses it beneath evil; purification leads to success, while corruption leads to failure.

The second part (11–15) presents the example of Thamud to show why Prophets are necessary: natural intuition alone is insufficient, and without revelation people invent false standards of good and evil. Prophet Ṣāliḥ (PBUH) brought clear guidance, yet Thamud—overcome by their own corruption—rejected him and defied the divine sign of the she-camel, leading to their destruction.

Although the Surah does not directly warn Quraysh, the parallel between their situation and that of Thamud serves as an implicit caution that rejecting the Prophet carries the same consequences.

sections.title: 1-10 SUCCESS DEPENDS ON KEEPING THE SOUL PURE AND FAILURE DEPENDS ON CORRUPTING IT

translation.text: By the sun and its brightness,

commentary.text: Allah SWT swears by the sun and its daytime. The word duha as used in the original applies both to the light of the sun and to its heat.

translation.text: and the moon as it follows it,

commentary.text: Allah SWT swears by the moon that follows the sun. Talaha (follows it) is referring to the night of the Hilal (the new crescent moon). When the sun goes down, the Hilal is visible. Talaha is derived from tiawat or recitation to follow.

translation.text: and by the day as it displays the sun's glory,

commentary.text: Allah SWT swears by the day that reveals all the sun’s glory.

translation.text: and the night as it conceals it!

commentary.text: Allah SWT swears by the night that covers the day.
Pairs are coming i.e Sun and Moon. Day and Night

translation.text: And by heaven and ˹the One˺ Who built it,

commentary.text: Allah SWT swears by the sky and the One who created it.

translation.text: and the earth and ˹the One˺ Who spread it!

commentary.text: Allah SWT swears by the earth and the One who spread it out.

translation.text: and by the soul and by Him Who perfectly proportioned it,

commentary.text: Allah SWT swears by the human soul that is created in a pure, moderate and balanced manner as compared to the animalistic nature of animals. The human soul has a fitrah — the natural instinct to recognize truth and worship Allah SWT.
The Quran confirms this in 30:30, saying that Allah SWT created all people upon this upright nature.
The Prophet (PBUH) explained that every child is born on this pure fitrah, but parents and society later shape the child into other beliefs.

“Proportioned it” means Allah SWT created the human being in the best physical, mental, and moral form. He gave us an upright body, strong senses, and powerful thinking abilities so we can learn and make responsible choices. It also means every person is born on a pure, natural disposition (fitrah)—not sinful or crooked—fully capable of recognizing and following the right path. Later influences, not birth, lead people astray.

translation.text: then with ˹the knowledge of˺ right and wrong inspired it!

commentary.text: Allah SWT placed inside every human being a natural awareness of right and wrong, and the inner pull toward both evil desires (fujūr) فُجُوۡرَهَا and moral restraint (taqwā) وَتَقۡوٰٮهَا. This inspiration includes two things:
Humans have innate tendencies toward good and evil. A natural moral sense that recognizes good actions as good and bad actions as bad.

This inner moral compass is universal; all human societies reward good and punish evil, showing that Allah SWT created humans with this awareness. JUST AS ANIMALS ARE GUIDED INSTINCTIVELY TO THEIR SURVIVAL SKILLS, HUMANS ARE GUIDED INSTINCTIVELY IN THEIR MORAL NATURE.

translation.text: He who purifies it will prosper,

commentary.text: This is the conclusion to the oaths. There is a battle of struggle inside man between good and evil. What we feed the soul is what overpowers it. This is a lifelong process.
The Surah previously mentioned the sun and moon, day and night, sky and earth—all opposites—to show that good and evil are also complete opposites and cannot produce the same results.

THIS IS THE TURE DEFINITION OF SUCCESS!! He who builds his character and purifies it. Elevates his self his ego his soul. SO ALLAH SWT HAS PLANTED THE SEEDS BUT WE HAVE TO ELEVATE OUR POTENTIAL VIA GOOD DEEDS AND IMAN.

Lesson: One person’s Ruh e Rabbani has been elevated the other is a person who is following his worldly desires forgetting his elevated soul. THERE IS A UNIVERSAL MORAL SENSE THAT IS EMBEDDED IN EVERYONE’S NAFS OR SOUL BUT THE RUH IS HIGHER AND HIDDEN WHICH HAS THE LOVE OF ALLAH SWT AND AN ELEVATED LEVEL OF FITRA.

translation.text: and he who suppresses it will be ruined.

commentary.text: THIS IS THE TURE DEFINITION OF FAILURE!! A person destroys himself when he suppresses the good inside his soul and allows evil desires to take over. The nafs of humans is different from animals because it contains the universal moral compass. Via wahi. Maroof and Munkar is because we know the difference. But is a person suppresses the internal voice and buries the noise then he is ruined.

Allah SWT created the human soul with the ability to recognize both fujūr (wrongdoing) and taqwā (self-restraint), and He gave each person the freedom to choose. If someone purifies the soul—strengthening good tendencies and resisting evil—he succeeds. But if someone buries the soul under wrongdoing, letting fujūr dominate until taqwā is covered like a body buried in dirt, he ends in loss.

translation.text: Thamûd rejected ˹the truth˺ out of arrogance,

commentary.text: These Ayats now introduce the historical example of Thamud to explain the principles mentioned above: (i) that Allah SWT created the human soul with an inner sense of good and evil, but this natural awareness is not enough unless a person also accepts the clear guidance brought by the Prophets.

Prophet Ṣāliḥ (PBUH) was sent to Thamud to explain what true righteousness (taqwā) is and what sinful corruption (fujūr) looks like in practice. But the people of Thamud were steeped in wrongdoing and did not want to give it up, so they rejected Ṣāliḥ’s message, just as they rejected the moral responsibility placed within their own souls.

The Quran then shows the second principle: (ii) the results of one’s moral choices. Purifying the soul leads to success; corrupting it leads to destruction. Thamud becomes the clearest proof of this law. Their ruins were well-known to the Arabs of Makkah, who passed by their territory on trade journeys, and their destruction was famous in Arab poetry. By denying Prophet Ṣāliḥ, refusing taqwā, and persisting in fujūr, they sealed their own fate. Their arrogance blinded them to truth, and their downfall became a living example of what happens when a people reject both inner guidance and Prophetic revelation.

translation.text: when the most wicked of them was roused ˹to kill the she-camel˺.

commentary.text:
The most wicked person of the tribe, and he was Qudar bin Salif, the one who killed the she-camel. He was leader of the tribe of Thamud, and he is the one whom Allah refers to in His saying, “But they called their comrade and he took (a sword) and killed (her).” (54:29)
This man was mighty and respected among his people. He was of noble lineage and a leader who was obeyed.

translation.text: But the messenger of Allah warned them, “˹Do not disturb˺ Allah’s camel and her ˹turn to˺ drink!”

commentary.text:
The Story of Salih's She-Camel
At other places in the Quran the following details, are given: The people of Thamud challenged the Prophet Salih (PBUH) to present a sign (a miracle) if he was truthful. Thereupon the Prophet (PBUH) presented a she-camel miraculously before them and warned them to the effect: This is Allah’s she-camel. She will graze at will in the land.

One day will be for her to drink and one day for you and your cattle. If you molest her, you will be punished with a scourge. This proved to be a deterrent for some time. Then they appealed to their most wicked and rebellious chief to put an end to the she-camel, and he took up the responsibility and hamstrung her.
Also see Surah Al-Aaraf, Ayat 73, Surah Ash-Shuara, Ayats 134, Surah Al-Qamar, Ayat 29.

translation.text: Still they defied him and slaughtered her. So their Lord crushed them for their crime, levelling all to the ground.

commentary.text: According to Surah Al-Aaraf, Ayat 77, after they had killed the she-camel, the people of Thamud said to the Prophet Salih (PBUH): Bring the scourge with which you threatened us. And according to Surah Houd, Ayat 65, the Prophet Salih (PBUH) said to them: Well, you have only three more days to enjoy yourselves in your houses. This is a limit that will not prove false.

Allah SWT made the punishment descend upon them all equally.
Qatadah said, "It has reached us that the leader of tribe of Thamud did not kill the she-camel until their youth, their elderly, their males and their females all pledged allegiance to him. So when the people cooperated in killing her, Allah destroyed them all with the same punishment due to their sin."
Lesson: The whole nation failed to listen to their inner voice and were corrupted.

translation.text: He has no fear of consequences.

commentary.text: Allah SWT is not like the kings of the world and the rulers of governments, who, when they want to take some action against a people, are compelled to consider what will be the consequences of their action. Allah SWT’s power is supreme. He had no apprehension that some supporting power of the Thamud would come out to avenge itself on Him.

items.text: TWO PRINCIPALS ARE MENTIONED
Humans have innate tendencies toward good and evil. A natural moral sense that recognizes good actions as good and bad actions as bad.
The results of one’s moral choices. Purifying the soul leads to success; corrupting it leads to destruction.
قَدۡ اَفۡلَحَ مَنۡ زَكّٰٮهَا
(90:9) He who purifies it will prosper,
وَقَدۡ خَابَ مَنۡ دَسّٰٮهَا ؕ
(90:10) and he who suppresses it will be ruined.
EXAMPLE OF NATION OF THAMUD AND THEIR ULTIMATE DESTUCITION
(90:11) Thamûd rejected ˹the truth˺ out of arrogance,
(90:12) when the most wicked of them was roused ˹to kill the she-camel˺.
(90:14) Still they defied him and slaughtered her. So their Lord crushed them for their crime, levelling all to the ground.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah takes its name from the word with which it opens.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: Its subject matter so closely resembles that of Surah Ash-Shams that each Surah seems to be an explanation of the other. It is one and the same thing which has been explained in Surah Ash-Shams in one way and in this Surah in another. This indicates that both these Surahs were sent down in about the same period.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
Its theme is to distinguish between the two different ways of life and to explain the contrast between their ultimate ends and results. In view of the subject matter this Surah consists of two parts, the first part consisting of Ayat 1-11 and the second of Ayat. 12-21.

Surah Al-Lail distinguishes between two opposing moral paths and clarifies the radically different outcomes that follow from them. The Surah opens with oaths by the night, the day, and the creation of male and female, establishing contrast as the frame of the message.

1. The Two Ways of Life (1–11)

front_matter.label: Human beings differ in their efforts:
front_matter.text:
One path involves generosity, God-consciousness, and affirming what is true. Such a person will find ease opened for them, and their goodness will become self-reinforcing.

The other path involves miserliness, self-sufficiency, and denial of ultimate truth. For this person, the path of hardship is made increasingly difficult, and their refusal of guidance leads toward ruin.

2. Guidance, Accountability, and the Final Reward (12–21)

Allah SWT provides guidance, yet individuals choose their course. The Surah warns of a blazing Fire prepared for those who reject the truth and highlights the example of the righteous who purify themselves through sincere giving, seeking nothing but the pleasure of Allah SWT. Their ultimate reward is profound satisfaction and contentment in the Hereafter.

sections.title: 1-21 FOR GOOD PEOPLE ALLAH WILL FACILITATE THE EASY WAY AND FOR THE WICKED THE HARD WAY, AND WHAT BENEFIT WILL HE GET FROM WEALTH, IF HE HIMSELF IS DOOMED

translation.text: By the night when it covers,

commentary.text: Allah SWT takes an oath or swears by the night as it envelops meaning, when it covers the creation with its darkness.

translation.text: and the day when it shines!

commentary.text: Allah SWT takes an oath or swears by the day as it appears meaning, with its light and its radiance.

translation.text: And by ˹the One˺ Who created male and female!

commentary.text: Allah SWT takes an oath or swears by the One who created males and females.
Thus far Allah SWT is swearing by opposing things.
Also see:

And We have created you in pairs. (78:8)
And of everything We have created pairs. (51:49)

translation.text: Surely the ends you strive for are diverse.

commentary.text: Conclusion of the oath. Just as the night and the day, and the male and the female are different from each other, so are the aims and objects for which men are endeavoring and struggling, for example, there are those who do good and there are those who do evil. Two very different paths that are contradictory with regard to their results. Some people are actively making an effort for Heaven while others are striving for Hell. Their lifestyles, striving and choices are completely different.
In the following Ayats, these different strivings or endeavors are categorized into two main kinds i.e. good and evil.

translation.text: As for him who gave out his wealth (for Allah's sake) and abstained (from disobeying Him),

commentary.text: As for him who gives and has Taqwa meaning, he gives what he has been commanded to give and he fears Allah SWT in his affairs, then Allah SWT eases his path toward goodness.

The Prophet (PBUH) explained through an authentic narration in Bukhārī that although each person’s ultimate abode is known to Allah SWT, people must still act, because Allah facilitates each person toward the path they choose.

Righteous give only to purify himself, seeking nothing but the pleasure of Allah SWT, and that such a person will ultimately be content. The story of Bilāl (RA) reinforces this: after being tortured for rejecting idols, he was ransomed by Abu Bakr (RA), prompting the Quraysh to suggest he did so out of obligation. Allah SWT revealed that Abu Bakr’s actions were purely for His sake, not to repay any favor.
These narrations illustrate the Surah’s central theme: the contrast between selfless devotion that earns divine ease, and arrogance that leads to hardship.
Lesson: Give as much as you can for Allah SWT’s sake and have taqwa that keeps us on the right path.

translation.text: and ˹firmly˺ believes in the finest reward,

commentary.text: This describes a person who embraces the entire framework of righteousness. This includes spending wealth generously rather than worshipping it, observing taqwā by avoiding what displeases Allah SWT in every aspect of conduct, and sincerely believing in al-husnā, the highest good.

Early commentators such as Qatādah explained al-husnā as believing in the promised recompense, while Khusayf interpreted it as affirming the reward that Allah SWT has prepared for those who follow this path.

translation.text: We will facilitate for them the Way of Ease.

commentary.text: When a person embraces these three qualities (i) generosity, (ii) taqwā, and (iii) the truthfulness in all goodness, Allah SWT makes the righteous path naturally easy for him (towards Heaven).

This “easy way” aligns with human nature and with the Creator’s design, freeing a person from the inner conflict, agitation, and moral resistance that accompany sin. Instead, he experiences harmony with his conscience, dignity among people, and a life marked by peace and stability, as reflected in other Ayats promising a “pure life” for believers (16:97) and divine love placed in their hearts (19:96).

Although the moral path first appears steep—like the “uphill road” of Surah Al-Balad—once a person commits to goodness, Allah SWT eases the ascent and makes slipping back into corruption increasingly difficult. But hard work and striving is required then Allah SWT helps facilitate matters in sha Allah. This is Allah’s promise.
Lesson: Absolutely beautiful and inspiring Ayat!

translation.text: As for him who was a miser and behaved with aversion (to Allah),

commentary.text: This is the second kind of human endeavoring, which in every part is different from the corresponding part of the first kind.
He is stingy with his wealth (with what Allah SWT gave him) and considers himself to be in no need of his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.
Niggardliness (bukhl) is not just one who hoards money: neither spends it on himself nor on his children, but bukhl here implies to refrain from spending in the cause of Allah SWT and public welfare.
Independence of God implies that one makes worldly, material benefits the only object of all his endeavoring and strivings and does not care about what pleases Allah SWT and what displeases Him.

translation.text: and ˹staunchly˺ denies the finest reward,

commentary.text: When good is presented to him he refuses to accept despite knowing in his heart that this is in fact that truth. Arrogance/pride/love for this world all stop him from believing.

translation.text: We will facilitate for them the path of hardship.

commentary.text: Allah SWT declares that the one who is miserly, self-satisfied, and denies the truth will have the path of hardship or path to evil made easy for him.

Although such a person seeks worldly gain, he lives in constant conflict with his conscience and with the moral order of Allah SWT, damaging himself and society until corruption and disgrace surround him. Allah SWT withdraws the grace that inclines the heart toward good, so sinful actions become easy while obedience becomes heavy.

Hadith teach us that every person is facilitated toward what they choose: those who intend goodness are guided toward it, and those who choose denial and wrongdoing find the path of misguidance opened before them.

translation.text: And their wealth will be of no benefit to them when they tumble ˹into Hell˺.

commentary.text: He must die one day and leave behind in the world whatever he had amassed for his ease and enjoyment. If he did not earn and send forward something for the Hereafter, what would this wealth avail him? He will not take his palatial residence, his majestic conveyance, his property and wealth into the grave.
Lesson: So here are three things to do for Heaven and then in contrast the things to do to earn Allah SWT’s wrath.

translation.text: It is certainly upon Us ˹alone˺ to show ˹the way to˺ guidance.

commentary.text: Allah SWT as the Creator of man has on the basis of His wisdom, His justice and His mercy, taken on Himself the responsibility not to leave him uninformed in the world, but to tell him what is the right way and what are the wrong ways, what is good and what is evil, what is lawful and what is unlawful, what attitude and conduct will make him an obedient servant and what attitude and conduct will make him a disobedient servant.
Also see: Surah An-Nahl Ayat 9
Allah has taken upon Himself to show the right way, when there are also crooked ways.

Lesson: We have a nafs that innately helps us distinguish good from bad, Allah SWT’s has blown into us meaning our souls have an even greater yearning and leaning for the love of Allah SWT. And then Allah SWT send Prophets and Scriptures to guide us.

translation.text: And surely to Us ˹alone˺ belong this life and the next.

commentary.text: Both this world and the Hereafter belong entirely to Allah SWT.

translation.text: I have now warned you of a Blazing Fire,

commentary.text: Hadith: Verily, the lightest punishment received by the people of the Hellfire will be a man who will have two sandals whose straps will be made of fire that will cause his brain to boil just as a cauldron boils. Yet he will not think that anyone is receiving a torment more severe than him, even though he will be receiving the lightest punishment of them.
Lesson: We have been warned over and over again.

translation.text: where none shall burn except the most wicked,

commentary.text: Meaning, none will enter surrounded by it on all sides except the most wretched. Then Allah SWT explains who this (the most wretched) below.

translation.text: who rejected the Truth, calling it falsehood and turned his back on it.

commentary.text:
Hadith: The Prophet (PBUH) stated that, All of my followers will enter Paradise on the Day of Judgement except for whoever refuses. They (the Companions) said, "Who would refuse, O Messenger of Allah"
He replied, whoever obeys me, he will enter Paradise, and whoever disobeys me, then he has refused.
Lesson: The literal meaning of Kufur or Disbelief is concealment or hiding the truth.

translation.text: But the God-fearing shall be kept away from it,

commentary.text: And those with Taqwa will be far removed from it meaning, the righteous, pure, most pious person will be saved from the Fire.
Consensus is that this Ayat particularly refers to Abu Bakr (RTA).

translation.text: who donate ˹some of˺ their wealth only to purify themselves,

commentary.text: He who gives of his wealth for self-purification meaning, he spends his wealth in obedience of his Lord in order to purify himself, his wealth and whatever Allah SWT has bestowed upon him of religion and worldly things.
Lesson: Charity averts disasters and troubles. Should give sadqa every day in some form.

translation.text: not as payment for any favours that he received,

commentary.text: Giving his wealth is not done so that he may gain some favor from someone or hoping he gets something in return. Rather Sadqa should be given to seek the pleasure of Allah SWT only.

translation.text: but only to seek the good pleasure of his Lord Most High.

commentary.text: Rather he spends only hoping to attain the blessing of seeing Allah SWT in the final abode in the Gardens of Paradise. This is further explanation of the sincerity of the pious man. he is helping and spending only in order to seek the goodwill of his Lord, the Supreme.

Its best illustration is the act of Abu Bakr Siddiq, he would purchase and set free the poor slaves and slaves-girls who accepted Islam in Makkah and were cruelly treated by their masters on that account. When Abu Bakr’s father saw him spending money to purchase the freedom of the poor slaves and slave-girls, he said to him: Son, I see that you are getting the weak people free; had you spent this money on the freedom of strong, young men, they would have become your helpers and supporters. Abu Bakr replied: Dear father, I only seek the reward that is with Allah.

translation.text: They will certainly be pleased.

commentary.text:
Indeed, those people with these characteristics will be pleased.

The Reason for this Revelation and the Virtue of Abu Bakr
Many of the scholars of Tafsir have mentioned that these Ayat were revealed about Abu Bakr As-Siddiq. Some of them even mentioned that there is a consensus among the Quranic commentators concerning this. (Abu Bakr) was the first and foremost of this Ummah to have all of these characteristics and other praiseworthy characteristics as well. He was truthful, pious, generous, charitable, and he always spent his wealth in obedience of His Master (Allah) and in aiding the Messenger of Allah. 

Lesson: People are never easy to please, but we can please Allah SWT. IA.

items.text: WHAT ARE YOU STRIVING FOR?
(92:4) Surely the ends you strive for are diverse.
THREE THINGS THAT ONE MUST STRIVE FOR TO ATTAIN HEAVEN
(i)GENEROSITY, (II) TAQWĀ, AND (III) THE TRUTHFULNESS IN ALL GOODNESS, ALLAH SWT MAKES THE RIGHTEOUS PATH NATURALLY EASY FOR HIM (TOWARDS HEAVEN).

وَصَدَّقَ بِالۡحُسۡنٰ
(92:6) and ˹firmly˺ believes in the finest reward,
فَسَنُيَسِّرُهٗ لِلۡيُسۡرٰىؕ

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah takes its name from the very first word.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text:
Its subject matter clearly indicates that it belongs to the earliest period at Makkah. Traditions also show that the revelations were suspended for a time, which caused the Holy Prophet (PBUH) to be deeply distressed and grieved.

On this account he felt very anxious that perhaps he had committed some error because of which his Lord had become angry with him and had forsaken him.

Thereupon he was given the consolation that revelation had not been stopped because of some displeasure but this was necessitated by the same expediency as underlies the peace and stillness of the night after the bright day, as if to say: "If you had continuously been exposed to the intensely bright light of Revelation () your nerves could not have endured it.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
Its theme is to console the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and its object to remove his anxiety and distress, which he had been caused by the suspension of Revelation. First of all, swearing an oath by the bright morning and the stillness of night, he has been reassured, so as to say: "Your Lord has not at all forsaken you, nor is he displeased with you."

Then, he has been given the good news that the hardships that he was experiencing in the initial stage of his mission, would not last long, for every later period of life for him would be better than the former period, and before long Allah SWT would bless him so abundantly that he would be well pleased. This is one of the express prophecies of the Quran, which proved literally true, afterwards, whereas when this prophecy was made there seemed not to be the remotest chance that the helpless and powerless man who had come out to wage a war against the ignorance and paganism of the entire nation, would ever achieve such wonderful success.

Then, addressing His Holy Prophet (PBUH) Allah says: "O My dear Prophet, what has caused you the anxiety and distress that your Lord has forsaken you, and that We are displeased with you? Whereas the fact is that We have been good to you with kindness after kindness ever since the day of your birth. You were born an orphan, We made the best arrangement for your upbringing and care: you were unaware of the Way, We showed you the Way; you were indigent, We made you rich. All this shows that you have been favored by Us from the very beginning and Our grace and bounty has been constantly focused on you.

sections.title: 1-11 GOOD NEWS TO MUHAMMAD (PBUH) THAT LATER PERIOD WILL BE BETTER FOR HIM THAN THE EARLIER

translation.text: By the morning brightness

commentary.text: Allah SWT takes an oath by the morning light and brightness. Here, the word duha has been used in contrast to the night; therefore, it implies the bright hours of the day.

A woman from the Quraysh said to the Prophet (PBUH): ‘I think your demon has forsaken you’, and so it was revealed (By the morning hours, and by the night when it is stillest, thy Lord hath not forsaken thee nor doth He hate thee)”. This was narrated by Bukhari

translation.text: and by the night when it covers the world with peace:

commentary.text: Allah SWT takes an oath by the night that covers with peace and tranquility. The word saja in the original does not only signify the spreading of darkness but it also contains the meaning of stillness and peace that prevails at night. This quality of night deeply relates to the theme that follows.
Night and day are completely different and contrasting. Nothing in life is permanent.
Lesson: We need both day and night for the world and humans to survive and thrive similarly revelation needs a pause at times for the best absorption.

translation.text: (O Prophet), your Lord has neither forsaken you, nor is He displeased.

commentary.text: Conclusion of the oath:

It was in this state that Surah Ad-Duḥā was revealed, swearing by the morning light and the stillness of night to assure him that the pause was not a sign of divine displeasure. Just as day and night alternate by Allah SWT’s wisdom—not because one indicates His approval and the other His anger—the sending and withholding of revelation also follow divine wisdom.

Constant revelation would have overwhelmed the Prophet (PBUH), so the pauses (fatrah) were necessary for rest and renewal, like night after day. Thus, Allah SWT declares with certainty that He had never abandoned him at all.

The revelation had paused for a period long enough to distress the Prophet (PBUH) and embolden his opponents. Reports differ on the duration—some say 12, 15, 25, or even 40 days—but the gap allowed the pagans to mock him, claiming his “Lord” or “satan” had abandoned him, while the Prophet (PBUH) himself felt deep anguish, fearing he had erred and lost Allah SWT’s favour.

translation.text: And the next life is certainly far better for you than this one.

commentary.text: What awaits the Prophet (PBUH) with Allah SWT is far superior to anything in this worldly life, which is why he lived with profound detachment from worldly comforts and a constant orientation toward the next life.

Ibn Kathīr cites the narration in which Ibn Masʿūd found the Prophet (PBUH) lying on a straw mat that left marks on his side, and when offered a softer bedding, the Prophet (PBUH) replied that his relationship with this world was like a traveler who rests briefly under the shade of a tree and then moves on, capturing perfectly the meaning of the Ayat and his lived expression of its truth.
Lesson: World should not be our goal. Striving in this world will ensure paradise. Relief comes after difficulty.

translation.text: And ˹surely˺ your Lord will give so much to you that you will be pleased.

commentary.text: A promise of Allah SWT to His Messenger (PBUH). Allah SWT will grant the Prophet (PBUH) blessings so immense that he will be completely satisfied, especially in the Hereafter, where he will rejoice in both his own honor and the salvation of his followers. These gifts include Al-Kawthar in Paradise, with its banks of pearl-like domes and musk-scented soil, and far greater generosity beyond human comprehension.
But in this world as well there will be victory after victory. Happiness and joy in this world too for all the striving and patience.

translation.text: Did He not find you an orphan and then gave you shelter?

commentary.text: The Prophet’s (PBUH) father passed away three months before his birth; thus, he was an orphan at birth. But Allah SWT did not leave him without support even for a day. Up to six years of age his mother nourished and looked after him. After her death, his grandfather took him and brought him up with great love. He would proudly tell the people: ‘This son has a great future’. When he died, his uncle, Abu Talib, became his guardian and treated him with such rare love that no father could treat his son better. So much so that when after his proclamation to be a Prophet the entire nation turned hostile, Abu Talib alone stood firm as his chief supporter for as long as ten years.

When he was forty years of age and Allah SWT commissioned him with the Prophethood. Abu Talib died a short time before the Hijrah. After this (Abu Talib's death) the foolish and ignorant people of the Quraysh began to attack him, so Allah SWT chose for him to migrate away from them to the city of Al-Aws and Al-Khazraj among those who helped him (in Al-Madinah).

Allah SWT caused his Sunnah to be spread in the most perfect and complete manner. Then, when he arrived at their city, they gave him shelter, supported him, defended him and fought before him (against the enemies of Islam) -- may Allah be pleased with all of them.
ALL OF THIS WAS FROM ALLAH'S PROTECTION FOR HIM, GUARDING OVER HIM AND CARING FOR HIM.
Lesson: When one is feeling a bit heavy or anxious or depressed understand what Allah SWT has given us. Hardships can either make you bitter and hard or soften you.

translation.text: Did He not find you unaware of the Right Way, and then directed you to it?

commentary.text: This does not mean that the Prophet (PBUH) was ever misguided in belief or involved in shirk. The Quran itself states that before revelation he did not know the Book or the formal structure of faith (42:52), though he already believed in Allah’s Oneness and lived with exemplary character.

Thus, the Ayat means that Allah SWT found him without access to revealed guidance and then directed him, unveiling the truth to him, awakening his mission, and placing him as a guiding light in a world engulfed in jahiliyyah.
Lesson: Reflect on your own life. Hardships are always followed by ease. Always be hopeful that Allah SWT will take care of me.
Hardships are here to soften our hearts.

translation.text: And did He not find you in want, and then enriched you?

commentary.text: The Prophet’s (PBUH) father had left only a she-camel and a slave-girl in heritage for him; so he started his life in a state of poverty. Then a time came when the wealthiest lady among the Quraish, Khadijah, first made him her partner in trade, then married him, and he took charge of all her trade and business.
Thus, he not only became wealthy but his riches in no way were dependent on the resources of his wife; his own hard work and ability had gone a long way towards promoting her trade and commerce.

translation.text: Therefore, be not harsh with the orphan;

commentary.text: That is just as you (O Prophet) were an orphan and Allah SWT sheltered and graced you, then do not oppress the orphan. Do not humiliate him, scorn him or despise him. Rather, you should be kind and gentle to him.
Lesson: When one has experienced difficulty then by empathetic of others and don’t afflict difficulty on others.

translation.text: nor repulse the beggar.

commentary.text: The command instructs the Prophet (PBUH) to show no harshness toward anyone who turns to him, whether the person is seeking guidance or seeking material help. Just as Allah SWT guided him when he did not yet know the revealed path, he must not scorn those asking to be guided; and just as Allah SWT relieved his need, he must treat the poor with gentleness and mercy.
Ibn Isḥāq explained that this Ayat forbids arrogance or roughness toward the weak, while Qatādah emphasized meeting the needy with compassion.
Lesson: This was when the Prophet (PBUH) was sad. So remedy to saddens is to be kind to others. Helpers High. Show compassion and mercy to others to get it from Allah SWT.

translation.text: And proclaim the blessings of your Lord.

commentary.text: This Surah is a remedy for sadness. (i) Hope (that this too shall pass) (ii) kindness (iii) gratitude (iv) blessing of the Quran.
The Prophet (PBUH) should convey the blessing of revelation.
Generally, we should talk about our blessings and not our problems.
Lesson: So in essence spread the wealth and wealth of knowledge. Don’t hoard it.

In short, this is a very comprehensive instruction which Allah SWT gave to His Messenger (PBUH) telling him how to treat the creatures of God and how to give thanks after having described the bounties and blessings Allah SWT has bestowed upon him.

items.text:
THE SURAH BEGINS WITH A PROMISE EMBEDDED IN NATURE:
NIGHT ALWAYS GIVES WAY TO MORNING.
SADNESS SAYS:
I’M ABANDONED → FUTURE IS DARK → NOTHING CHANGES → I’M ALONE

THE SURAH REPLIES:

IT REPLACES DESPAIR NARRATIVE WITH DIVINE NARRATIVE.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah name is from Ayat 1.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: Its subject matter so closely resembles that of Surah Ad-Duha that both these Surah seem to have been revealed in about the same period under similar conditions. According to Hadrat Abdullah bin Abbas, it was sent down in Makkah just after Surah Ad-Duha.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
Surah Alam-Nashrah, revealed in Makkah shortly after Ad-Duḥā, shares the same purpose of consoling and strengthening the Prophet (PBUH) during the difficult early phase of his mission.

After a lifetime of honor and esteem, he suddenly faced hostility, ridicule, and rejection from the very people who once respected him, and the drastic change in his circumstances weighed heavily on him.

Allah SWT then reassures him that the hardship he faces is temporary and will soon be followed by ease, echoing the promise in Ad-Duḥā that every later stage of his life will surpass the previous.

An interesting aspect of this Surah as discussed by Dr Israr is that after Prophethood the Prophet (PBUH) would much rather be in worship all the time having a direct link with Allah SWT rather than go and convey to people who may or may not accept. So here that is the hardship being mentioned that get up and go and convey.

Similarly, we should worship at night for a much deeper and closer connection with our Raab and then in the AM continue with worldly chores as well as worship but then once again to regain the more profound and intense connection we should worship at night.

Once one gains the pleasure/delight of assentation/closeness with Allah SWT then the descent into humankind even if is to convey is tough for mankind so just imagine what it would be for a Prophet of Allah SWT. That is the hardship being mentioned.

sections.title: 1-8 ALLAH EXPANDED THE CHEST OF PROPHET, LIGHTEN HIS BURDEN AND EXALTED HIS FAME

translation.text: Did We not expand for you, [O Muhammad], your breast?

commentary.text: This is a reminder meant to console the Prophet (PBUH) during the difficult early years of his mission. The phrase sharḥ-ṣadr here carries two complementary meanings found throughout the Quran: (i) first, Allah SWT freed his heart from confusion, doubt, and the search for truth by revealing the clear path of Islam to him, giving him complete inner conviction and peace; (ii) second, Allah SWT strengthened him with courage, resilience, and spiritual breadth so he could shoulder the immense responsibilities of prophethood, confront a hostile society, endure hardship, and stand-alone against powerful forces without hesitation.

Before revelation, he rejected the false religions around him but did not yet know the detailed right way; with prophethood, Allah SWT opened his heart to guidance and endowed him with extraordinary firmness, wisdom, and capacity and gave him this great gift of inner clarity and strength.

translation.text: and relieve you of the burden

commentary.text: This is specific to the Prophet (PBUH).
That Allah may forgive you your sins of the past and the future. (48:2)

translation.text: which weighed so heavily on your back,

commentary.text: The heavy distress the Prophet (PBUH) carried as he watched his society buried in idolatry, injustice, immorality, and oppression with no solution in sight.  This moral anguish pressed on him like a crushing weight.

When Allah SWT guided him and then granted him prophethood, He removed that burden by revealing the path of Tawḥīd, the Hereafter, and divine guidance, showing the Prophet (PBUH) that he now possessed the message capable of curing the very corruption that had grieved him.

translation.text: and elevated your renown for you?

commentary.text: Allah SWT declares that He has raised the Prophet’s (PBUH) fame, a promise made when he had only a few followers and no one could imagine the honor that awaited him. The very attempts of his enemies to discredit him in Makkah spread his name across Arabia, leading people to inquire about his character and message.

After the Hijrah, the just and moral society formed under his leadership, and the victories of the believers, further elevated his standing until all of Arabia openly proclaimed his apostleship. From that point onward, his name has been joined with Allah SWT’s in every call to prayer and in the worship of Muslims across the world.

translation.text: So, surely with hardship comes ease.
Surely with ˹that˺ hardship comes ˹more˺ ease.

commentary.text: Whatever troubles are encountered by the creation, Allah SWT always provides a relief with it. The relief does not merely come after the difficulty: it is provided with it.

This has been repeated twice to reassure the Prophet (PBUH) that the bad times he was passing through at that time would not last forever but were going to be replaced by good times in the near future.

On the surface this appears to be a contradiction that hardship should be accompanied by ease, for these two things do not co-exist. But the words hardship with ease instead of ease after hardship have been used in the sense that the period of ease is so close to it as if it were a concomitant of it.

translation.text: So once you have fulfilled ˹your duty˺, strive ˹in devotion˺,

commentary.text: So, when you have finished your work and are free then stand up and worship Allah SWT. Spend your free time in worship and don’t waste any time.

When there is rest from the task of instructing the world, the contact with the spiritual kingdom continues, and indeed it becomes more intimate and concentrated especially during qiyam ul lail or night prayers.
Lesson: Once my tafseer curation is done I will begin tajweed course in sha Allah.

translation.text: turning to your Lord ˹alone˺ with hope.

commentary.text: Turn towards your Lord for His worship and turn to Him for all hopes.
Worldly greatness or success may be a means to an end, but it may also be a hindrance to true spiritual greatness. Allah SWT is the goal of the righteous man's whole attention and desire.

items.text: SURAH ASH-SHARḤ TEACHES THAT US THAT ALLAH SWT EXPANDS THE BELIEVER’S INNER CAPACITY, LIFTS BURDENS, AND RAISES HONOR THROUGH THE VERY PROCESS OF HARDSHIP, AND THAT RELIEF ACCOMPANIES DIFFICULTY WHILE EFFORT AND DEVOTION MUST CONTINUE.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah has been so named after the very first word.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: The majority of scholars regard it as a Makki revelation, a manifest symbol of which is the use of the words (this city of peace) for Makkah.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
The Surah affirms accountability in the Hereafter by declaring, through oaths taken by lands associated with great Prophets, that Allah SWT created human beings in the finest and most balanced form, endowed with a nature capable of the highest moral and spiritual achievement.

Yet people clearly divide into two types: (i) those who corrupt this noble nature through disbelief and moral decline, sinking to the lowest level, and (ii) those who preserve it through faith and righteous conduct, remaining true to their created dignity. This undeniable contrast in human character itself proves the necessity of judgment and recompense, for if the corrupt and the righteous were to share the same end, it would negate justice altogether—something impossible for Allah SWT, the most just of all judges.

sections.title: 1-8 MAN IS MADE THE BEST CREATURES OF ALL EXCEPT THE DISBELIEVERS

translation.text: By the fig and the olive;

commentary.text: Allah SWT takes an oath by the fig and the olive. Commentators differed over whether the fig and the olive refer to the fruits themselves or to specific lands.

Because Quranic oaths consistently relate to the theme that follows, many scholars held that fig and olive symbolize the lands where they are abundantly grown, namely Syria and Palestine, regions associated with a long chain of Prophets and divine guidance.
This interpretation preserves thematic coherence: Allah SWT swears by places connected to major revelations to affirm humanity’s noble creation and ultimate accountability.

Lesson: The topic continues from previous Ayats regarding man’s character which can be base, lying, cheating, etc. and some reach the conclusion that man is a lowly creature who just wants to eat, sleep, poop rinse and repeat.  animalistic instincts only. But Allah SWT revealed this Surah to announce that infact man is a very high natured creature. Prophets are the best example of this.
The soul of man is very elevated. But when it turns into an animal is it is the most base.

translation.text: and by the Mount Sinai,

commentary.text: Allah SWT takes an oath by the Mount Sinai. It is the mountain upon which Allah SWT spoke to Musa.

translation.text: and by this city (of Makkah), a haven of peace:

commentary.text: Allah SWT takes an oath by the city of Makkah. This refers unanimously to Makkah.

Many commentators explain that the oaths in this Surah refer to three sacred locations, each associated with a great Messenger and a divine law: (i) the land of the fig and the olive, identified as Jerusalem where ʿĪsā ibn Maryam was sent; (ii) Mount Sinai, where Allah SWT spoke to Mūsā ibn ʿImrān; and (iii) Makkah, the city of peace and security, where Muhammad (PBUH) was sent.

These places are mentioned in chronological order of prophethood and revelation, progressing from noble to nobler, culminating in Makkah as the most honored of all. Through these oaths, Allah SWT highlights the continuity of divine guidance and the supreme dignity of the final Messenger and the sanctuary from which his message emerged.

translation.text: Indeed, We created humans in the best form.

commentary.text: Conclusion of the oath: Allah SWT swears by the lands of the fig and the olive (Syria and Palestine), Mount Sinai, and Makkah to affirm that HUMAN BEINGS WERE CREATED IN THE FINEST MOLD, endowed with the most refined physical form and the highest intellectual and moral capacities. The clearest proof of this noble design is prophethood itself, the highest rank attainable by any creature.

These oaths are taken by places uniquely associated with the Prophets—Syria and Palestine with many Prophet’s including Ibrahim and ʿIsa, Sinai with Musa, and Makkah, founded by Ibrahim and Ismail as a sanctuary of peace—testifying that humanity was created with the potential to reach the supreme station of prophethood.

translation.text: But We will reduce them to the lowest of the low ˹in Hell˺,

commentary.text: Human beings—despite being created in the finest mold—misuse their intellectual, moral, and physical capacities for evil, Allah SWT allows them to descend into the lowest level of moral degradation. Whether throw drug use, immoral acts, acts of violence etc.

This is a reality observable in human societies, where greed, cruelty, lust, arrogance, and injustice can reduce people to a state far worse than animals. Unlike beasts, humans employ their superior intellect to commit extreme brutality, corruption, and moral perversion, even distorting religion itself.

Thus, the Ayat highlights how humanity, by abandoning faith and righteousness, can fall from the highest dignity to the lowest degradation, preparing the ground for the argument of just recompense in the Hereafter.

commentary.text: When it is a common observation in human society that a section of mankind which has been created in the best of molds and nature, is rendered lowest of the low because of moral degradation, and the other section remains secure by adopting the path of constant faith and righteousness in view of its being created in the best of molds and nature how can judgment be denied after this?

Does common sense require that the end of both these men be the same? Does justice demand that neither those who are reduced to the lowest of the low be punished nor those who strive to adopt a righteous life be rewarded?
The same theme has been expressed at other places in the Quran thus:
Surah 68 Ayat 35

Do those who have committed evil think that We shall hold them and those who have believed and done righteous deeds as equal so that their life and their death should be alike?

Does Allah SWT judgment then not necessitate a final judgment.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah is so entitled after the word in the second Ayat.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: This is a Makki Surah.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
Surah Al-ʿAlaq takes its name from the word ʿalaq in its second Ayat and consists of two distinct sections revealed at different moments.

Ayats 1–5 constitute the very first revelation sent to the Prophet (PBUH) in the Cave of Ḥirāʾ, as established by rigorously authentic reports from ʿĀʾishah (RA) and corroborated by Ibn ʿAbbās and other Companions. The revelation came unexpectedly through Jibrīl, commanding the Prophet (PBUH) to read in the name of Allah SWT, marking the beginning of prophethood without prior anticipation or preparation. The Prophet (PBUH) returned deeply shaken, and Khadījah (RA) reassured him by affirming his lifelong moral integrity.

Ayats 6–19 were revealed later in Makkah when the Prophet (PBUH) began performing ṣalāh at the Kaʿbah and Abu Jahl arrogantly attempted to stop him, threatening violence. These Ayats expose human transgression born of self-sufficiency, condemn opposition to worship, and affirm divine protection of the Prophet (PBUH), as illustrated by authentic reports describing Abu Jahl’s retreat in terror when confronted by unseen divine forces.

Together, the Surah establishes the foundations of revelation, knowledge, worship, moral restraint, and the inevitable defeat of arrogance before Allah SWT.

sections.title: 1-19 READ IN THE NAME OF ALLAH, WHO CREATED MAN AND TAUGHT HIM BY THE PEN AND THOSE WHO FORBID FROM THE WORSHIP OF ALLAH WILL BE DRAGGED TO HELL BY THEIR FORELOCK

translation.text: Recite in the name of your Lord Who created,

commentary.text: The command “Recite in the name of your Lord who created” marks the beginning of revelation and carries profound meaning. This first revelation-the divine commission to preach and proclaim Allah's Message came to the Prophet, in the cave of Hira when Jibrīl commanded the Prophet (PBUH) to “recite” or read from memory.

The verb khalaqa (created) is used without an object, signifying Allah SWT as the absolute Creator of all existence—everything in the universe without exception. Thus, the verse establishes from the very first moment that knowledge, revelation, and human purpose begin with Allah SWT, the sole Creator and Sustainer.
Iqra’ may mean “read”, or “recite or rehearse”, or “proclaim aloud”, the object understood being Allah SWT’s Message.
Lesson: It is said the revelation came on a Monday an odd night of the last ten days of Ramadan.

translation.text: created man from a clot of congealed blood.

commentary.text: After mentioning the creation of the universe, mention has been made of how Allah SWT created man from a clot of congealed blood thus from an insignificant and humble state. Alaq is plural of alaqah, which means congealed blood. This is the primary state of the embryo which appears a few days after conception. Then it assumes the form of a lump of flesh, then afterwards it gradually takes human shape. (For details, see Surah Al-Hajj, Ayat 5.

translation.text: Recite: and your Lord is Most Generous,

commentary.text: Allah SWT created man from a most insignificant state, then made man a possessor of knowledge/guidance which is the noblest attribute of creation.

translation.text: Who taught by the pen—

commentary.text: The pen is a tool for learning knowledge. Allah SWT taught man the art of writing by the use of pen, which became the means of propagation and preservation of knowledge on a large scale. And a means of transmission of knowledge from one generation to the next.

translation.text: taught man what he did not know.

commentary.text: Man, originally was illiterate. Whatever of knowledge he obtained, he obtained it as a gift from Allah SWT.

These five Ayats were the very first to be revealed to the Prophet (PBUH). This first experience was so intense and tremendous that the Prophet (PBUH) could not bear it anymore. Then after an intermission the opening Ayats of Surah al-Muddaththir were revealed in which he was told what mission he had to perform after his appointment to Prophethood.

translation.text: Nay, surely man transgresses;

commentary.text: All our knowledge and capacities come as gifts from Allah SWT. But man, in his inordinate vanity and insolence, mistakes Allah SWT's gifts for his own achievements. The gifts may be strength or beauty, wealth, position, or power, or the more subtle gifts of knowledge or talents in individuals.

translation.text: for he believes himself to be self-sufficient.

commentary.text: When the man has attained wealth, honor and rank and whatever else he desired to attain in the world, he becomes rebellious instead of being grateful and transgresses the boundaries of servitude to Allah SWT.
Lesson: This world is based on physical laws (operative) and not moral laws meaning if you eat poison, you will die but if you lie or steal you will not die. Thus, this emboldens man.

translation.text: Surely to your Lord is your return.

commentary.text: There is a law of good and bad when you return to your Raab. He is the greatest of all judges; do you think that He will not do any justice? Do you expect that He will treat the good and the evil alike?

translation.text: Did you see him who forbids

commentary.text: This may be applied generally regarding those who seek not only to rebel against Allah SWT’s Law, but also to prevent others from following it.

Specifically, Abu Jahl, a confirmed and hardened enemy of Islam, who used, to insult and persecute the Prophet (PBUH) and those who followed his teaching. He used to use shameful methods to prevent the Prophet (PBUH) from going to the Ka'bah for devotions, and forbid any who came under his influence, from offering prayers or performing devotions. He was arrogant and met his end in the battle of Badr.

translation.text: a servant (of Allah) when he prays?

commentary.text: The Prophet (PBUH) has been mentioned by this epithet, ‘a servant’ at several places in the Quran. This shows that it is a special style of love by which Allah SWT makes mention of His Messenger Muhammad (PBUH) in His Book.

translation.text: Did you consider: what if he is on the Right Way,

commentary.text: Do you think this man whom you are preventing is upon the straight path in his action.

translation.text: or encourages righteousness?

commentary.text: Or enjoins Taqwa. in his statements.

translation.text: What if that ˹man˺ persists in denial and turns away?

commentary.text: Yet, you rebuke him and threaten him due to his prayer.

translation.text: Does he not know that Allah sees everything?

commentary.text: Meaning, doesn't this person who is preventing this man who is following correct guidance know that Allah SWT sees him and hears his words, and He will compensate him in full for what he has done
Allah SWT’s watching the oppressor and his wrongdoing here implies that He will punish the oppressor and redress the grievances of the wronged and downtrodden person.

translation.text: No indeed; if he does not desist, We shall drag him by the forelock;

commentary.text: That is, the person (Abu Jahl) who threatens that he would trample the neck of Muhammad (PBUH) down when he performed the Prayer, would never be able to do so.
We will make it extremely black for him on the Day of Judgement.

translation.text: by the lying forelock steeped in sin.

commentary.text: The forehead of Abu Jahl.

translation.text: So let him call his associates.

commentary.text: The Prophet (PBUH) was praying when Abu Jahl came to him and said: ‘Did we not warn you against this?’ The Prophet (PBUH) went to him and spoke to him harshly. Abu Jahl retaliated by saying: ‘Indeed, you know very well that there is no one in Mecca who has more guards than me’, and as a response Allah SWT revealed this Ayat.

translation.text: We too shall summon the guards of Hell.

commentary.text: Here the arrogance of Abu Jahl, who threatened to assault the Prophet (PBUH) for praying at the Ka‘bah and boasted of his tribal power and supporters.

Allah SWT responds by exposing the emptiness of such worldly strength, declaring that while Abu Jahl may call his nādi (council), Allah SWT will call the Zabāniyah, the angels appointed for punishment. The accompanying hadiths confirm this divine warning: when Abu Jahl attempted to approach the Prophet (PBUH) he recoiled in terror, perceiving a barrier of fire and angels, and the Prophet (PBUH) stated that had he come closer, the angels would have seized him.

The passage illustrates that human tyranny and arrogance collapse before divine authority, and that Allah SWT protects His Messenger (PBUH) through unseen but decisive means, making clear that true power lies not in numbers or lineage, but in submission to Allah SWT.
Hadith confirms
Abu Jahl threatens to stomp on the Prophet (PBUH) during prayer.
The Prophet (PBUH) states plainly: angels would seize him if he tried.
When Abu Jahl approaches, he panics, retreats, and claims he sees fire, terrifying beings, and wings.
The Prophet (PBUH) explains: had Abu Jahl come closer, the angels would have torn him apart limb by limb.

commentary.text:
Meaning, `O Muhammad! Do not obey him from steadfastness in worship and performing worship in abundance. Pray wherever you wish and do not worry about him. For indeed Allah SWT will protect you and help you, and He will defend you against the people.'

"The closest that a servant can be to his Lord is when he is in prostration. Therefore, make abundant supplications (i.e., while prostrating)."
