front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah name is from Ayat 1.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: The majority agree this is a Makki Surah.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
The central theme of Surah Al-Qadr is to impress upon humanity the immense value, dignity, and historical significance of the Quran. Its placement immediately after Surah Al-‘Alaq is deliberate, for revelation began with the command “Read”, and this Surah explains the extraordinary nature of the moment in which that revelation commenced. Allah SWT declares, “Indeed, We sent it down,” making it explicit that the Quran is a direct act of divine revelation, not the product of the Prophet Muhammad’s (PBUH) own composition or reflection.

The phrase Laylat al-Qadr carries two closely related meanings, both intended in the Surah. First, it refers to the Night of Decree, during which divine destinies are determined. The revelation of the Quran on this night was therefore not an ordinary event, but one that reshaped the destiny of humanity as a whole. Second, it denotes a night of supreme honor, dignity, and worth, described as better than a thousand months. This serves as an implicit response to the disbelievers of Makkah, who regarded the Quran as a misfortune, whereas in reality its revelation was an unparalleled blessing for mankind.

The Surah concludes by stating that the angels and Jibrīl (عليه السلام) descend during this night with every wise decree by the permission of Allah SWT. The night is described as entirely peace until dawn, meaning it is free from evil interference and filled with divine order and mercy. Even decrees that involve hardship or punishment are grounded in wisdom and ultimately serve a greater good. In this way, Surah Al-Qadr presents the revelation of the Quran as a moment of unmatched blessing, mercy, and transformative power for human history.

Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), when divine mercy, guidance, and destiny descend upon the world.

front_matter.label: The Surah does three things in a tight arc:
front_matter.text:
Establishes the event: “We sent it down in Laylat al-Qadr”

Establishes the value: “better than a thousand months”

Establishes the atmosphere: angels and the Spirit descend, peace until dawn, cosmos aligned with mercy and decree

Surah Al-Qadr declares that the night the Quran descended is the most spiritually powerful moment in human history, when divine guidance and destiny flood creation with peace.

Link to Al-ʿAlaq (important)

front_matter.label: Scholars read them together:
front_matter.text:
Al-ʿAlaq: first Ayats revealed (beginning of revelation)

Al-Qadr: night of that revelation’s descent (cosmic significance)

So, one shows what came down (knowledge), the other shows when and how great its descent was.

sections.title: 1-5 THE NIGHT OF QADR IS BETTER THAN ONE THOUSAND MONTHS

translation.text: Behold, We revealed this (Quran) on the Night of Power.

commentary.text: The Virtues of the Night of Al-Qadr (the Decree)

The Quran was sent down on the Night of Power, clearly referring to the beginning of divine revelation even though the Quran is not named explicitly. This night occurred in Ramadan and is identified with the first revelation to the Prophet (PBUH) in the Cave of Ḥirā’.
Scholars explain this “sending down” either as the entrusting of the entire Quran to the angels, to be revealed gradually over twenty-three years, or as the start of revelation itself.

The term qadr signifies both divine decree and supreme honor, making the night one of destiny and unmatched dignity. While its exact date is not fixed, it lies among the odd nights of the last ten days of Ramadan, with many scholars favoring the 27th night, a deliberate uncertainty meant to encourage increased worship.

Ibn Abbas and others have said, "Allah SWT sent the Quran down all at one time from the Preserved Tablet (Al-Lawh Al-Mahfuz) to the House of Might (Baytul-`Izzah), which is in the heaven of this world. Then it came down in parts to the Messenger of Allah based upon the incidents that occurred over a period of twenty-three years."
Lesson: Dr Israr is of the personal opinion that 27 night is the 27 nights in Makka. Thus, not locally but rather follow Makka.

translation.text: And what will make you realize what the Night of Glory is?

commentary.text: The Prophet (PBUH) explained that Laylat al-Qadr occurs in Ramadan, a blessed month in which the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of Hell are closed, and the devils are restrained, and that whoever is deprived of the good of this night is truly deprived.

translation.text: The Night of Power is better than a thousand months.

commentary.text: Worship performed on this night is superior in value to worship carried out over a very long span of time, and whoever stands in prayer during it with faith and sincere hope for reward is granted forgiveness of past sins.
The night itself is better than a thousand months.

translation.text: The angels along with the Spirit descend in it by the permission of their Lord with all kinds of decrees.

commentary.text: The Spirit: Gabriel, who has been mentioned separately from the angels in view of his unique eminence, honor and merit. That is, they do not descend of their own accord but by leave of their Lord, and every decree implies “amr hakim” (a wise decree) as described in Surah Ad-Dukhan, Ayat 5.

The angels descend in abundance during the Night of Al-Qadr due to its abundant blessings. The angels descend with the descending of blessings and mercy, just as they descend when the Quran is recited, they surround the circles of Dhikr (remembrance of Allah) and they lower their wings with true respect for the student of knowledge.
Lesson: This is the night of the annual budget session when orders are given, and angels then implement the orders throughout the year.

translation.text: It is all peace until the break of dawn.

commentary.text: This signifies that Laylat al-Qadr is entirely a night of goodness, mercy, and safety, free from evil until daybreak. The angels, along with Jibrīl (عليه السلام), descend throughout the night, spreading peace and conveying divine decrees, and some early scholars explained this as the angels greeting the believers engaged in worship. Authentic hadiths establish that Laylat al-Qadr occurs every Ramadan within the last ten nights, particularly the odd nights, and that standing in prayer during it with faith and sincere hope for reward results in forgiveness of sins.

While various reports mention signs such as a calm, moderate night and a sun rising without harsh rays the following morning, the Quran and Sunnah intentionally leave it’s exact timing uncertain to encourage sustained devotion.
The Prophet (PBUH) therefore emphasized increased worship and taught a concise supplication for this night:

قُولِي اللْهُمَّ إِنَّكَ عَفُوٌّ تُحِبُّ الْعَفْوَ فَاعْفُ عَنِّي
"O Allah!  You are the Most Pardoning, You love to pardon, so pardon me."

items.text: THE NIGHT OF POWER
اِنَّاۤ اَنۡزَلۡنٰهُ فِىۡ لَيۡلَةِ الۡقَدۡرِ
(97:1) Behold, We revealed this (Quran) on the Night of Power.
(97:3) The Night of Power is better than a thousand months.
DUA

قُولِي اللْهُمَّ إِنَّكَ عَفُوٌّ تُحِبُّ الْعَفْوَ فَاعْفُ عَنِّي
"O Allah!  You are the Most Pardoning, You love to pardon, so pardon me."

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah is named after the word occurring at the end of the first Ayat.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: It is a Makki revelation according to most scholars.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
Being placed after Surahs Al-Alaq and Al-Qadr in the arrangement of the Quran is very meaningful. Surah Al-Alaq contains the very first revelation, while Surah Al-Qadr states when the Quran was revealed, and in this Surah it has been explained why it was necessary to send a Messenger along with this Holy Book.

Firstly, need of sending a Messenger has been explained, saying: The people of the world, be they from among the followers of the earlier scriptures or from among the idolaters, could not possibly be freed from their state of unbelief, until a Messenger was sent who presents the Book of God before the people in its original, pristine form, which should be free from every mixture of falsehood corrupting the earlier Divine Books; and which should comprise sound teachings.

Then, about the errors of the followers of the earlier Books it has been said that the cause of their straying into different creeds was not that Allah SWT had not provided any guidance to them, but they strayed only after a clear statement of the Right Creed had come to them. From this it automatically follows that they themselves were responsible for their error and deviation. Now, if even after the coming of the clear statement through this Messenger, they continued to stray, their responsibility would further increase.

In conclusion, it has been pointed out clearly that the followers of the earlier Books and the idolaters who would refuse to acknowledge this Messenger are the worst of creatures: their punishment is an everlasting Hell; and the people who would believe and act righteously, and would spend life in the world in awe of God, are the best of creatures: their reward is eternal Paradise wherein they will live forever. Allah SWT became well pleased with them and they became well pleased with Allah SWT.

sections.title: 1-8 PEOPLE OF THE BOOK DID NOT GET DIVIDED INTO SETS UNTIL AFTER RECEIVING THE GUIDANCE AND PEOPLE OF THE BOOK WERE ALSO COMMANDED TO ESTABLISH SALAH AND PAY ZAKAH

arabic_lines: لَمۡ يَكُنِ الَّذِيۡنَ كَفَرُوۡا مِنۡ اَهۡلِ الۡكِتٰبِ وَالۡمُشۡرِكِيۡنَ مُنۡفَكِّيۡنَ حَتّٰى تَاۡتِيَهُمُ الۡبَيِّنَةُ ۙ

translation.text: Those who disbelieved – be they from the People of the Book or from those who associated others with Allah in His Divinity – will not desist from unbelief until the Clear Proof should come to them;

commentary.text: The opening Ayat of Surah Al-Bayyinah describes the condition of the disbelievers among both the People of the Scripture and the idolators, stating that they were not going to abandon their unbelief until the Bayyinah came to them. Here, unbelief (kufr) is used in its broad sense, encompassing denial of Allah SWT, associating partners with Him, rejecting Prophets, or selectively accepting revelation.
These groups were stuck in disbelief, and they were going to stay that way until Allah SWT sent the final, undeniable guidance.
Lesson: People weren’t going to change their beliefs just on their own. It took Allah SWT sending the final Messenger (PBUH) with clear revelation. And even then, some still refused.

translation.text: A Messenger from Allah, reciting purified scriptures

commentary.text: Muhammad (PBUH) and the Magnificent Quran he recites, which is written down among the highest gathering in purified pages is the clear proof. This is the clear guidance now there is no room for disbelief.

The Clear Proof came as a Messenger from Allah SWT, namely the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), whose life, character, message, and unwavering consistency all testified to the truth of his prophethood. Though unlettered, he recited divine revelation and brought about a profound moral and spiritual transformation, making him himself living evidence. The purified scrolls refer to the Quran, a revealed scripture entirely free from falsehood, error, and moral corruption, distinguished by its clarity, truth, and ethical purity.

The People of the Scripture refer specifically to Jews and Christians, who possessed earlier divine books but deviated from their guidance, while the idolators are those who upheld shirk as their religion, whether among Arabs or non-Arabs. (Here the crime/sin is being mentioned).

translation.text: containing upright commandments.

commentary.text: The Quran is just, moderate and straight containing no mistakes in it because it is from Allah SWT, the Mighty and Majestic.

The Bayyinah, identified as the Quran and the Messager as decisive proof that exposed falsehood and established guidance, leaving no excuse for continued rejection once divine clarification had been fully delivered.

translation.text: It was not until this clear proof came to the People of the Book that they became divided ˹about his prophethood˺—

commentary.text: The People of the Book did not fall into division until after the Clear Proof had come to them, meaning that their differences and sectarianism were not due to lack of guidance, but arose after divine evidence had already been established.
They denied the Prophet (PBUH) despite recognizing him, due to arrogance, pride, want of power and jealousy.

Allah SWT had fulfilled His obligation by sending clear revelation, so responsibility for deviation rested with them alone. This pattern is repeated throughout Quranic history: once guidance becomes clear, then differences اختلاف stems from human choice, not divine neglect.

By sending the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) with the Quran a purified and final revelation Allah SWT once again completed the proof, leaving no excuse for continued division. True religion, as the Quran repeatedly emphasizes, is not sectarianism but sincere devotion to Allah SWT alone, avoiding shirk and adhering to the path of pure monotheism (ḥanīfiyyah) followed by the Prophet (PBUH) and his Companions.

translation.text: even though they were only commanded to worship Allah ˹alone˺ with sincere devotion to Him in all uprightness, establish prayer, and pay alms-tax. That is the upright Way.

commentary.text: Message is Tauhid, Salah and Zakat. The command is nothing new or complex, but only to (i) worship Allah SWT with complete sincerity, devoting religion exclusively to Him, avoiding all forms of shirk, and (ii) to establish prayer and (iii) give zakah.
This was the same message conveyed by all earlier Prophets and scriptures, and it represents the constant core of true religion throughout history.
The false beliefs and sectarian divisions that later emerged were human inventions, not part of divine guidance.

This simple yet comprehensive devotion to Allah SWT alone, expressed through sincere worship and righteous practice, is described as the Right Faith (dīn al-qayyimah), the straight and upright religion.

translation.text: Indeed, those who disbelieve from the People of the Book and the polytheists will be in the Fire of Hell, to stay there forever. They are the worst of ˹all˺ beings.

commentary.text: Mentioning the Worse and Best of Creation and Their Recompense

Those who disbelieved by refusing to acknowledge the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) after clear proof had come to them whether from the People of the Book or the idolators will abide eternally in the Fire. Their disbelief is especially grave because it occurred despite the presence of reason, authority, and unmistakable guidance through revelation and prophethood.

For this reason, they are described as the worst of creatures, even worse than animals, since animals lack moral responsibility, whereas these people knowingly rejected the truth. The Ayat thus underscores that final accountability is tied not merely to disbelief, but to conscious rejection of manifest guidance after Allah SWT had fully established His proof.

translation.text: Indeed, those who believe and do good—they are the best of ˹all˺ beings.

commentary.text: IMAN + GOOD DEEDS = SUCCESS
May Allah SWT make us of these people. Ameen.

arabic_lines: جَزَآؤُهُمۡ عِنۡدَ رَبِّهِمۡ جَنّٰتُ عَدۡنٍ تَجۡرِىۡ مِنۡ تَحۡتِهَا الۡاَنۡهٰرُ خٰلِدِيۡنَ فِيۡهَاۤ اَبَدًا ؕ رَضِىَ اللّٰهُ عَنۡهُمۡ وَرَضُوۡا عَنۡهُ ؕ ذٰلِكَ لِمَنۡ خَشِىَ رَبَّهٗ

translation.text: Their reward with their Lord will be Gardens of Eternity, under which rivers flow, to stay there for ever and ever. Allah SWT is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him. This is ˹only˺ for those in awe of their Lord.

commentary.text: The reward of the believers with their Lord on the Day of Judgement is eternal: Gardens of lasting residence beneath which rivers flow, where they will dwell forever without end. Beyond all physical delights, the greatest honor is that Allah SWT is pleased with them, and they are fully pleased with Him, in content with His favor and decree.

This supreme reward is promised to those who truly fear and love their Lord, worshipping Him with awareness and reverence, knowing that even if they do not see Him, He sees them. The Prophet (PBUH) described such people as the best of creation, whether striving in the way of Allah SWT or living quietly while establishing prayer and giving zakah, for true excellence lies in sincere faith, obedience, and God-consciousness.
May Allah SWT make us of these people. Ameen.

This was the same message conveyed by all earlier Prophets and scriptures, and it represents the constant core of true religion throughout history.
(98:5) even though they were only commanded to worship Allah ˹alone˺ with sincere devotion to Him in all uprightness, establish prayer, and pay alms-tax. That is the upright Way.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah takes its name from the word zilzāl (earthquake) zalzala (urdu) occurring in the first Ayat.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: The Surah’s brief, powerful style and focus on core beliefs strongly indicate that it belongs to the early Makki period, when foundational doctrines of faith were being emphasized with clarity and force.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
Surah Al-Zalzalah centers on resurrection and accountability in the Hereafter, portraying how the second life will commence in a sudden, overwhelming manner. It declares that the earth itself, by command of Allah SWT, will testify to every deed performed upon it, specifying actions by time and place. Humanity will then rise from their graves in distinct groups to be shown the complete record of their deeds, with such perfect justice that not even an atom’s weight of good or evil will remain hidden.

The Surah affirms resurrection, accountability, and absolute justice in the Hereafter.

sections.title: 1-8 EARTH WILL REPORT WHATEVER HAPPENED ON HER AND MEN SHALL BE SHOWN THEIR BOOKS OF DEEDS

translation.text: When the earth will be shaken with a mighty shaking,

commentary.text: The word zalzalah denotes repeated, violent convulsions, indicating that the entire earth will be shaken with extreme intensity, not merely a part of it. The phrase zilzālahā further emphasizes that the shaking will occur to the fullest degree befitting a massive sphere like the earth. Zal means to slip and zal zala means to slip, slip.

While some commentators interpret this as the first quake marking the end of worldly life, the stronger view is that it refers to the second stage of Resurrection, when humanity will be brought back to life, as the subsequent Ayats clearly focus on accountability and the presentation of deeds. The earth’s movement from beneath thus signals the beginning of the final reckoning by command of Allah SWT.

translation.text: and when the earth throws out ˹all˺ its contents,

commentary.text: The earth will expel everything concealed within it by command of Allah SWT. This includes, first, the bodies of the dead, wherever and in whatever state they lie, which will be brought forth for resurrection; second, the full record of human deeds, traces, and events that occurred upon it, enabling the earth to testify to them.
Thus, nothing buried, whether bodies, actions, or possessions, will remain hidden when the Hour arrives.

translation.text: and humanity cries, “What is wrong with it?”—

commentary.text: This cry of mankind expresses utter shock and bewilderment at the drastic transformation of the earth, once stable and familiar, now violently altered by Allah SWT’s command.
Believers, however, will not be confused, as these events are in accordance with their conviction.

translation.text: on that Day the earth will recount everything,

commentary.text: The earth, by command of Allah SWT, will testify in precise detail to every action performed upon it, specifying what each person did, when, and where.

Alongside the records of the angels and the testimony of one’s own limbs, this earthly testimony fulfills the demands of perfect divine justice, leaving no deed, intention, or motive concealed and no room for denial or excuse on the Day of Judgment.

The purpose of this emergence is that each person be shown his or her deeds in full clarity, through the handing over of personal records and the testimony of creation itself. This unveiling will present not only individual actions but also the broader struggle between truth and falsehood across history, leaving every person fully aware of their role and responsibility before divine judgment.
Lesson: In Surah Ha Mim it tells us how our own limbs will testify against or for us.

translation.text: for your Lord will have commanded her (to do so).

commentary.text: It is apparent that the implied meaning here is that Allah SWT will permit it (the earth).

translation.text: On that Day people will proceed in separate groups to be shown ˹the consequences of˺ their deeds.

commentary.text:
Mankind will return from the station of the Judgement in separate groups – believers and non-believers. 
They will be divided into types and categories: between those who are miserable and those who are happy, and those who are commanded to go to Paradise and those who are commanded to go to the Hellfire.
Lesson: Choose your company wisely on earth as that will be your company in the Hereafter.

translation.text: So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it.

commentary.text: Reason: These Ayats establish the principle of absolute and precise accountability before Allah SWT, where no deed, however small, is disregarded.

This is concerning two individuals: (i) one who dismissed small acts of charity as worthless, believing reward lay only in major sacrifices, and (ii) another who trivialized minor sins such as small lies, backbiting, and unlawful glances, assuming punishment applied only to grave offenses.

Through these Ayats Allah SWT corrected both misconceptions, affirming that even the smallest acts of goodness accumulate in reward, and even minor sins accumulate in consequence. The passage thus instills moral vigilance, teaching that nothing is insignificant in the divine scale of justice.

The person who did not live in the world fearlessly and independent of God, but feared Him at every step lest he should do something which might entail His wrath and punishment, will have this reward reserved for him with Allah SWT.

translation.text: And whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it.

commentary.text: No deed, however small, escapes divine record or consideration, yet it does not mean that every minor sin will necessarily be punished in the Hereafter in isolation. Rather, it establishes perfect awareness and justice: every action will be brought to light and weighed within Allah SWT’s comprehensive system of reckoning.

The Quran and Sunnah clarify that believers who avoid major sins may have minor faults forgiven, that good deeds are rewarded many times over by Allah SWT’s grace, and that disbelievers receive recompense for their good deeds in this world, not the next.

The Ayat therefore serves as a profound moral warning and encouragement: no act of goodness should be dismissed as insignificant, and no sin should be treated as trivial, because small deeds accumulate and carry real weight in the final balance before Allah SWT.

items.text: DESCRITPTION OF DOJ
اِذَا زُلۡزِلَتِ الۡاَرۡضُ زِلۡزَالَهَا
(99:1) When the earth will be shaken with a mighty shaking,
NOTHING IS INSIGNIFICANT IN THE DIVINE SCALE OF JUSTICE
ABSOLUTE AND PRECISE ACCOUNTABILITY ON THE DOJ
(99:7) So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it
(99:8) And whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah has been so designated after the word occurring at the end of the last Ayat, al-ma`un

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: This Surah is Makki.

front_matter.label: Theme and Subject Matter
front_matter.text:
These were the prevalent characteristics of the Arabs society before the Prophet (PBUH). Its theme is to point out what kind of morals a man develops when he refuses to believe in the Hereafter, its judgment, and the meting out of rewards and punishments.

The central message of Surah Al-Maʿūn is that true faith must manifest in compassion and sincere worship; otherwise, religion becomes hypocrisy. The surah condemns those who outwardly appear religious yet neglect the vulnerable and perform acts of worship without sincerity.

The opening Ayat links denial of the Day of Judgment with social cruelty: such a person repels the orphan and does not encourage feeding the poor.

The surah then turns to religious hypocrisy, warning those who pray but are heedless of the meaning of their prayer and perform it merely to be seen by others. Their worship lacks sincerity and humility.

Finally, the surah criticizes those who withhold even small acts of assistance (al-Maʿūn), such as simple help or everyday kindness. This demonstrates that their religiosity is empty, because genuine faith naturally produces generosity and care for others.

SURAH AL-MAʿŪN TEACHES THAT BELIEF IN ACCOUNTABILITY BEFORE ALLAH SWT MUST TRANSFORM BOTH WORSHIP AND SOCIAL CONDUCT; OTHERWISE, RELIGION BECOMES HOLLOW RITUAL AND MORAL HYPOCRISY.

sections.title: 1-7 DISBELIEVE IN THE HEREAFTER IS THE MAIN CAUSE OF MORAL DECAY AND LACK OF CARING ABOUT OTHERS

translation.text: Have you seen the one who denies the ˹final˺ Judgment?

commentary.text: "O Muhammad! Have you seen the one who denies the Din"
Here the word Din means the Hereafter, the Recompense and the Final Reward.

The words “have you seen”, apparently, are directed to the Prophet (peace be upon him), but the Quranic style is that on such occasions it generally addresses every intelligent and thinking person. And seeing means seeing with the eyes, for what has been described in the succeeding Ayats can be seen by every seer with his eyes, as well as knowing, understanding and considering something deeply.

If the word araaita is taken in the second meaning, the Ayat would mean: Do you know the kind of man who belies the rewards and punishments. Or: Have you considered the state of the person who belies the Judgment?

The style shows that the object of asking this question at the outset is not to ask whether he has seen the person or not, but to invite the listener to consider as to what kind of character is produced in man when he denies the judgment of the Hereafter

translation.text: That is the one who repulses the orphan,

commentary.text: He is the one who oppresses the orphan and does not give him his just due. He does not feed him, nor is he kind to him. What is the benefit is there is no reward in the Hereafter?

translation.text: and does not encourage the feeding of the poor.

commentary.text:
The person neither persuades his own self, nor tells the people of his household, to provide the poor man with his food, nor does he urge others to recognize the rights of the poor and needy people of society who are starving and do something to satisfy their hunger. Again, what is the benefit is there is no reward in the Hereafter?

Here, by giving only two conspicuous examples, Allah SWT has pointed out what kind of evils are produced in the people who deny the Hereafter. The real object is not to point out only these two evils rather present them as an example of the endless evils that occur as a result of the denial of the Hereafter.

The characteristics of the believers in the Hereafter which have been described in Surah Al-Asr and Surah Al-Balad are that they exhort one another to mercy, and they exhort one another to the truth and to render the rights of others.

translation.text: So woe to those ˹hypocrites˺ who pray

commentary.text: The open deniers of the Hereafter and the hypocrites who despite being Muslims regard the Hereafter as a falsehood; and although they pray they pray in a very deformed manner, i.e., clapping in prayer or doing tawaf of the Kaaba naked etc.

translation.text: yet are unmindful of their prayers;

commentary.text: What this heedlessness/mindlessness of prayer look like these days:
They delay prayers beyond their proper time.
They perform them reluctantly or carelessly.
Their prayer becomes a mechanical routine, not sincere remembrance of Allah SWT.
They only pray when necessary or when others are watching.
The adhān is heard but ignored.
The Prophet (PBUH) described this attitude when speaking about hypocrites: they wait until the sun is about to set for ʿAṣr, then quickly perform the prayer with little remembrance of Allah SWT.
Key distinction
Unintentional distraction – thoughts briefly enter the mind, but the believer pulls their attention back to Allah SWT. This is normal human weakness.
Neglectful prayer – the heart never turns toward Allah SWT at all; the person simply goes through the motions. This is what the Ayat condemns.

The Ayat exposes a deeper spiritual problem: a heart that does not truly value standing before Allah SWT. Prayer may still exist outwardly, but its purpose, remembrance, and seriousness have disappeared.

translation.text: those who ˹only˺ show off,

commentary.text: This can be an independent sentence as well as one relating to the preceding sentence. In the first case, it would mean that they do not perform any act of goodness with a pure intention for the sake of God, but whatever they do, they do to be seen of others so that they are praised, are considered righteous, their good act is publicized and its advantage and benefit accrues to them here in the world.

In the second case, the meaning would be that they pray to be seen. The commentators generally have preferred the second meaning, for at first sight it appears that it relates to the preceding sentence. Ibn Abbas says: It implies the hypocrites who prayed to be seen. They performed the Prayer if there was somebody to see them but did not perform it if there was nobody to see them.
In another tradition his words are to the effect: If they were alone they did not pray; but if there were others, they prayed.

translation.text: and deny people the articles of common necessity.

commentary.text: This means that they do not worship their Lord well, nor do they treat His creation well. They do not even lend that which others may benefit from and be helped by, even though the object will remain intact and be returned to them. These people are even stingier when it comes to giving Zakah and different types of charity that bring one closer to Allah SWT.

And withhold Al-Ma`un.
Ibn Mas`ud about Al-Ma`un and he said, "It is eery day items that people give to each other, like an axe, a pot, a bucket and similar items."

Many scholars concluded that maʿūn includes both meanings:
the greater form is zakat,
the lesser form is everyday kindness and lending small necessities such as salt or a pen etc.

The Ayat exposes a deep spiritual stinginess. A person who denies accountability before Allah SWT becomes so narrow-hearted that he will not even help others with minor things that cost him almost nothing.
Someone may pray outwardly yet still fail the test of faith because their heart refuses even the smallest acts of generosity toward people.
In other words, the Quran is quietly dismantling religious hypocrisy: prayer without compassion is just choreography. Allah SWT expects both.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The name of the Surah is in Ayat 1.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: According to Hadrat Abdullah bin Abbas, this Surah was sent down after Surah An-Naba. Its subject matter also testifies that it belongs to the earliest period at Makkah.

front_matter.label: Theme and subject matter
front_matter.text:
Surah An-Nazi‘at affirms the certainty of Resurrection and warns of the consequences of rejecting Allah SWT’s Messenger. It begins with oaths by the angels who seize souls, carry out Allah SWT’s commands, and manage the universe—showing that the same forces controlling life and death today can easily bring about the Resurrection tomorrow.

The Surah reminds the Quraysh of Pharaoh’s ruin for rejecting Musa, warning that similar arrogance leads to the same fate.

It then argues that resurrecting humans is far easier than creating the vast universe in the first place, and that a world so precisely designed for human life cannot end without accountability.

This is the fourth Surah of its kind beginning with Surah Saffat.

sections.title: 1-14 DUTIES OF ANGELS AND THE DAY OF RESURRECTION

translation.text: By those ˹angels˺ stripping out ˹evil souls˺ harshly,

commentary.text: An oath is being taken of the angels who swim into the body of humans and then pull or remove the soul with great harshness, as if the person is being drowned during its removal. Those angels who plunge deep inside and extract the soul with great violence.
Naza means pulling (the soul out of the body).

translation.text: and those pulling out ˹good souls˺ gently,

commentary.text: There are those people whose souls the angels remove with ease and gently, as if they were unraveling him (i.e., his soul from him) due to their briskness. Like a water drop from a washed cup.
FYI _ Where these souls are being taken will be discussed in Surah Muttaffifin 83.
Lesson: From the moment of our death we know where we are heading. How the angels take our souls out we know our ultimate destination and outcome.

translation.text: and those gliding ˹through heavens˺ swiftly,

commentary.text: Angels are prompt to execute the order of Allah SWT. Angels are with us all the time and change guard at the timeof fajr and Asr.

translation.text: and those taking the lead vigorously,
and those conducting affairs ˹obediently˺!

commentary.text: The oaths in Ayat 1-5 are about angels who:

• Extract souls at the time of death—sometimes forcefully for the wicked and gently for the righteous.
• Move swiftly through the cosmos to fulfil Allah SWT’s commands.
• Race to obey the slightest indication of divine will.
• Manage the affairs of the universe strictly according to Allah SWT’s order.
The oath by these angels serves to assert the certainty of Resurrection, even though both angels and the
Resurrection are unseen realities.

The reasoning is grounded in the beliefs of the Makkan Arabs: they already accepted the existence of angels, believed angels seize the soul, move with extraordinary speed, and execute Allah SWT’s commands without fail.

Thus, if angels can take the soul, they can also restore it by Allah SWT’s command; if they manage the current universe, they can also disrupt it and bring about a new order when the Resurrection occurs. Their obedience illustrates that when Allah SWT commands the cosmos to transform on the Day of Resurrection, it will happen without delay or resistance.
The answer to the oath is in Surah Zariyat and Surah Mursital it is open or obvious here it is hidden.

translation.text: ˹Consider˺ the Day ˹when˺ the quaking Blast will come to pass,
followed by a second Blast.

commentary.text: Two great cosmic blasts associated with the Trumpet (Ṣūr) on the Day of Resurrection. The first signifies the mighty blast that destroys the present order of the universe: the earth, the heavens, and all living beings collapse except those whom Allah SWT wills to spare.
The second is the subsequent blast that revives all the dead, causing humanity to rise from their graves, alert and looking on.
Also see Surah Az-Zumar Ayat 68.

translation.text: ˹The deniers’˺ hearts on that Day will be trembling ˹in horror˺,

commentary.text: Hearts shall tremble because, according to the Quran, only the disbelievers, the wicked people and the hypocrites will be terror-stricken on the Resurrection Day, the righteous believers will remain secure from this terror.
Surah Al-Anbiya Ayat 103 says, that the time of great fright will not trouble them at all; the angels will rush forth to receive them, saying: This is the very day which you were promised.

translation.text: with their eyes downcast.
˹But now˺ they ask ˹mockingly˺, “Will we really be restored to our former state,

commentary.text: Right now, the same people described above ask mockingly about the DoJ. They feel that after the disintegration of their bones and their decaying they could never be resurrected.

translation.text: Even after we have been reduced to decayed bones?”
Adding, “Then such a return would be a ˹total˺ loss ˹for us˺!”

commentary.text: If Allah SWT brings us back to life after we die, then surely, we will be losers the deniers say jokingly or mockingly. They are making fun but in reality it will indeed be a great loss.

translation.text: But indeed, it will take only one ˹mighty˺ Blast,
and at once they will be above ground.

commentary.text: Just one loud mighty blast will be enough to bring the dead out of their graves.

sections.title: 15-26 STORY OF MUSA WHEN HE CALLED FIR'ON TO HIS RABB, HE DENIED AND WAS SEIZED FOR PUNISHMENT

translation.text: Has the story of Moses reached you ˹O Prophet˺?

commentary.text: The story of Mūsā (PBUH) and Pharaoh is introduced to show that denying the Messenger and opposing Allah SWT leads to destruction. Their outcome serves as a warning to the Quraysh’s who were also rejecting the Prophet (PBUH) and Allah SWT’s message.
The Prophet (PBUH) is being comforted that the denial of reality does not change the reality.

translation.text: When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa,
and directed him: “Go to Pharaoh, he has rebelled,

commentary.text: Allah SWT addresses Musa (PBUH) and directed him to go to Pharaon who has become haughty, rebellious and arrogant.

translation.text: and say to him: ''Are you willing to be purified”,

commentary.text: This means, `will you submit (accept Islam) and be obedient.

translation.text: that I may direct you to your Lord and then you hold Him in awe?

commentary.text: Mūsā (PBUH) is commanded to address Pharaoh with a gentle invitation: to adopt purity so he may be guided to the knowledge of his true Lord and develop fear of Him. The result of guidance is fear. This is the litmus test. Fear is based on our knowledge/awareness that is, when we realize who Allah SWT really is. His Might. Mercy and Power. Fear is the fruit of knowledge or guidance. Like fasting = Taqwa.
The Quran here presents a brief version of the larger dialogue found in other surahs. Pharaoh’s rebellion involved defying Allah SWT and oppressing people by dividing society and enslaving the weak.

Mūsā’s mission was not only to free the Israelites but first to call Pharaoh and his people to the truth. “Purity” (tazakkā) means purity of belief, character, and action—accepting Islam. Recognizing one’s Lord naturally produces fear of Allah SWT, which is the foundation of right conduct.

translation.text: Then Moses (went to Pharaoh and) showed him the Great Sign;

commentary.text: The great sign: The turning of the staff into a serpent, as has been mentioned at several places in the Quran. Obviously there could be no greater sign than that a lifeless staff should turn into a living serpent right in front of the eyes of the people, that it should devour the artificial serpents produced by the magicians out of their staffs and cords, and when the Prophet Musa (PBUH) should pick it up, it should become a walking stick again.
This was proof that it was Allah SWT sent Musa (PBUH) as a Prophet.

translation.text: But Pharaoh denied and disobeyed.
then turned his back, striving ˹against the truth˺.
Then he summoned ˹his people˺ and called out,

commentary.text: According to the details given at other places in the Quran, he (Pharon) summoned skillful magicians from all over Egypt hoping they would reproduce the same miracle as Musa (PBUH). But the defeated magicians themselves admitted that what Musa (PBUH) had displayed was no magic but a miracle.

translation.text: saying, “I am your lord, the most high!”

commentary.text: When Pharaoh gathered his people and made his proclamation, his claim of being their “supreme lord” this did not mean he denied Allah SWT as Creator or saw himself as a literal god in a religious sense—he himself worshipped other deities. His claim was political: he asserted absolute sovereignty, denying that anyone— including Allah SWT—had authority over him in his kingdom.
His threats to Musa (PBUH) and statements like “I know no god for you but myself” were meant to reinforce this total earthly control, not to claim divine creatorship. (Dr Israr commentary)

translation.text: So Allah overtook him, making him an example in this life and the next.

commentary.text: Allah SWT avenged Himself against him with a severe vengeance, and He made an example and admonition of him for those rebellious people in the world who are like him.

arabic_lines: اِنَّ فِىۡ ذٰلِكَ لَعِبۡرَةً لِّمَنۡ يَّخۡشٰىؕ

translation.text: Surely there is a great lesson in it for whoever would fear (Allah).

commentary.text: Ibrat from the word Oboor (meaning going from one place to the other so you conquer that thing or place).
So ibrat means looking at something and understanding its meaning related to other things. Taking lessons.
Lesson: When reading the Quran, one should take lessons or Ibrat from so many things. Don’t fear people rather fear only Allah SWT.

sections.title: 27-33 CREATION OF MAN IS NOT HARDER THAN THE CREATION OF HEAVENS, EARTH AND ITS CONTENTS

translation.text: Are you a more difficult creation or is the heaven? Allah constructed it.

commentary.text: The Qurān argues that Resurrection is fully possible and rational: if Allah SWT created the vast heavens—filled with stars, planets, and galaxies—then re-creating human beings is far easier.

The Makkan disbelievers found it hard to believe their scattered remains could be restored, yet the One who created them the first time and fashioned the entire cosmos cannot be incapable of raising them again.

translation.text: raising it high and forming it flawlessly.

commentary.text: He raised its height and has perfected it. He made it a lofty structure, vast in its space.

translation.text: He dimmed its night, and brought forth its daylight.

commentary.text: He made its night dark and extremely black, and its day bright, luminous, shining and clear.

translation.text: As for the earth, He spread it out as well,

commentary.text: “He spread it out as well” does not indicate a sequence of creation. The Quran sometimes mentions the earth before the heavens and sometimes the heavens before the earth, depending on the emphasis required.

translation.text: bringing forth its water and pastures
and setting the mountains firmly ˹upon it˺—
all as ˹a means of˺ sustenance for you and your animals.

commentary.text: Allah SWT prepared the earth with deliberate wisdom: spreading it out, stabilizing it with mountains, causing rivers and springs to flow, bringing forth vegetation, trees, and fruits, and unlocking its hidden resources. This finely balanced system—day and night, water, land, climate—shows that the universe is purposeful, not accidental.

These arrangements provide humans and animals with everything they need: food, drink, shelter, and means of livelihood and transport. Such purposeful design proves that the Creator who perfected this world can easily bring about Resurrection, and that human life cannot be left without accountability.

sections.title: 34-46 PUNISHMENT AND REWARD ON THE DAY OF JUDGEMENT

translation.text: But when the great calamity will come about

commentary.text: Resurrection for which the words at- Taammat alkubra have been used. Taammah by itself is a grievous calamity which afflicts everybody. Then it has been further qualified by the word kubra (great), which shows that the mere word taammah is not enough to describe fully its intensity and severity.
Lesson: In life when a huge calamity befalls us its tough/difficult but remember that there is nothing bigger in disaster than the DoJ.

translation.text: the Day every person will remember all ˹their˺ striving,

commentary.text: When man will see that the same Day of accountability of which he was being foretold in the world, has come, he will start remembering each one of his misdeeds done in the world even before his records are handed over to him. Some people experience this even in the world. If at some time they come across a dangerous situation suddenly when death seems to be staring them in the face, their whole life-film flashes across their mind’s eye all at once.
Lesson: What are you striving for in this world or what is your saee  سَعٰى. Do you rush towards prayer or rush through prayer.

translation.text: and the Hellfire will be displayed for all to see—
then as for those who transgressed

commentary.text: Then for him who transgressed, meaning, who rebels and behaves arrogantly.
طَغ or Taghut is an Islamic term for anything or anyone that is worshipped or obeyed instead of Allah SWT. So a person who is following his ego, desires or others as their god.

translation.text: and preferred the ˹fleeting˺ life of this world,

commentary.text: Meaning, he gives this world precedence over the matters of his religion and his Hereafter.

translation.text: the Hellfire will certainly be ˹their˺ home.

commentary.text: For such people Hell is their eternal home.

arabic_lines: وَاَمَّا مَنۡ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهٖ وَ نَهَى النَّفۡسَ عَنِ الۡهَوٰىۙ

translation.text: And as for those who were in awe of standing before their Lord and restrained themselves from ˹evil˺ desires,

commentary.text: But as for him who fears standing before his Lord and forbade himself from desire means, he fears Allah's judgement of him which prevents his soul from following its desires, and he compels it to obey its Master.
He restrained or kept in check his Hawa or desires. Nafs الۡهَوٰىۙ
This is a person who knows his position in relation to Allah SWT.

translation.text: Paradise will certainly be ˹their˺ home.

commentary.text: May Allah SWT make us of these people. Always say this dua after reading something like this.
Here, in a few words, we have been told briefly what the criterion of the final judgment in the Hereafter shall be.

One kind of the conduct of life in the world is that transgressing all bounds; man who rebels against Allah SWT and seeks only the benefits and pleasures of this world in whatever way they could be sought and achieved. (Final abode Hell).

The other kind of conduct is that man constantly keeps in mind the truth that ultimately one day he has to stand before his Lord, and therefore should refrain from fulfilling evil desires/pleasure, because what answer will he give to his Lord. (Final abode Heaven).
THE ABOVE ARE VERY IMP AYATS THAT WE ALL SHOULD KEEP INGRAINED IN OUR MINDS.

translation.text: They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ regarding the Hour, “When will it be?”

commentary.text: The disbelievers of Makkah asked this question of the Prophet (PBUH) over and over again. By this they did not mean to know the time and date of the coming of Resurrection but to mock it. Also see Surah Al-Mulk Ayat 25.

translation.text: But it is not for you to tell its time.
That knowledge rests with your Lord ˹alone˺.
Your duty is only to warn whoever is in awe of it.

commentary.text: The Prophet (PBUH) is only a warner for those who fear.

translation.text: On the Day they see it, it will be as if they had stayed ˹in the world˺ no more than one evening or its morning.

commentary.text:
When we stand up from our graves to go to the place of Gathering, we will feel that the period of the worldly life was short, it will seem to them that it was only the afternoon of one day.
This refers to the time period of the worldly life in the eyes of the people when they see the Hereafter.
Lesson: Life is temporary and the Hereafter is eternal. So strive in this world and say no to desires. Obey and submit.
